Account Basics

Change color themes

Personalize the look and feel of your Todoist by choosing the color theme that best suits you. Pick one of the several Free and Pro options:

Free themes

Todoist, Dark, Moonstone, and Tangerine.

Pro themes

Kale, Blueberry, Lavender, and Raspberry.

How to select your theme:

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Select Theme.
  • Select the theme you’d like to use.
  • Optional: Toggle the Sync Theme option OFF to use different themes across your devices or ON to use the selected theme on all your devices.
  • Optional: You can set Todoist to automatically switch to Dark theme whenever your device uses Dark theme. Simply turn on the Auto dark theme toggle.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Select Theme.
  • Select the theme you’d like to use.
  • Optional: Toggle the Sync Theme option OFF to use different themes across your devices or ON to use the selected theme on all your devices.
  • Optional: You can set Todoist to automatically switch to Dark theme whenever your device uses Dark theme. Simply turn on the Auto dark theme toggle. This is available on Android 10 or above.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Select the theme you’d like to use.
  • Optional: Toggle the Sync Theme option OFF to use different themes across your devices or ON to use the selected theme on all your devices.
  • Optional: You can set Todoist to automatically switch to Dark theme whenever your iOS device uses Dark Mode. Simply turn on the Auto Dark Mode toggle. Quick tip

Once you reach Karma Enlightenment, a new mystery theme will be unlocked on your account.

FAQ

No. Even though a true black theme would save some battery over our current dark theme, we don’t regard the difference in power consumption significant enough (0.3% mW). Additionally, without an entire redesign, supporting a true black theme would make it harder to distinguish visual hierarchies and depth.

Change languages in Todoist

When you set up an account, Todoist will automatically detect your system’s default language. However, Todoist is available in a wide variety of languages (and we are always adding more), so should you wish to use it in a different language, here is how!

Warning

The Smart Date recognition language is automatically based on the selected language in Todoist, and only one language is detected at a time. If the selected language isn’t available yet, Smart Date recognition will default to English.

This means a date typed in a different language than your app’s language won’t be recognized. For example, if Todoist is set to Japanese, typing “today” in English won’t be detected. To use a different language for dates, change your language in Todoist using the steps below, or click the calendar icon below the task name and type the date manually in English.

Todoist is available in these languages

English

Chinese (Simplified)

Chinese (Traditional)

Czech

Danish

Dutch

Finnish

French

German

Italian

Japanese

Korean

Norwegian

Polish

Portuguese (Brazil)

Russian

Spanish

Swedish

Turkish

It’s possible to have the app set to different languages across the platforms. For example, the Todoist web app is in English, and the mobile app is in Spanish.

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Open the General tab.
  • Use the dropdown menu under Language to select your preferred language.
  • Once you’ve selected a language, click Update. Todoist for iOS will use the first language that it supports from the Language & Region settings of the Apple device.

To change the language in the app, follow Apple’s instructions to add the language to the Language & Region settings of the device. Then, follow these steps:

  • Open the device’s Settings app.
  • Scroll down and tap Todoist.
  • In Preferred Language, tap Language.
  • Tap the preferred language to use in Todoist.
  • Swipe up the bottom app bar to open the menu.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top right corner to open Settings.
  • Tap General.
  • Tap on Language and select any available language from the drop-down list.

Get help

If your language isn’t available yet, or you’re having trouble changing languages in Todoist, get in touch with us.

  • Instructions
  • Get help

Change your email address

Changing the email address you use with your Todoist account is quick and easy! Here is how:

Warning

If you’re using your Google, Facebook or Apple account to sign in, you’ll need to add a password to your Todoist account before you can change your email address. You can do this by going to Settings and selecting Account.

Furthermore, if you’ve enabled two-factor authentication for your account, you will need to get a code from your authentication app in order to change your email address. Learn more.

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Under your email address, select Change email.
  • Enter your new email address, and again to confirm.
  • Enter your password.
  • Select Change email.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Tap Account.
  • Tap your email address.
  • Enter a new email address, and again to confirm.
  • Enter your Todoist password.
  • Tap Done.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Select Account.
  • Select Email.
  • Enter your new email address, and again to confirm.
  • Enter your Todoist password. If you don’t have a password because you use your Google account to log in, you won’t see this option.
  • Tap the send icon. Note

You can only link one email address with your Todoist account.

FAQ

If you want to use an email from a different Todoist account, log in to the other account and change the address there first. This way the email will be freed up to re-use on the other account. Alternatively, if you don’t want to keep your second account, you can also delete it.

  • Instructions
  • FAQ

Change your Home view

When you open Todoist, make sure you see the tasks that are most important to you by setting your Home view.

The default Home view is your Today view, but you can change it to whatever you’d like:

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Click Settings.
  • Select the General tab.
  • Open the Home view drop-down menu.
  • Select your new Home view. You can select a default view such as Inbox or Upcoming, or choose any of your own projects, labels, or filters.
  • Click Update.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Tap General.
  • Tap Home view.
  • Select the view, project, label, or filter to open in Home View.
  • If you want this to be the Home view on your other devices too, toggle on Sync Home View.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Tap General.
  • Tap Home view.
  • Select your new Home view. You can select a default view such as Inbox or Upcoming, or choose any of your own projects, labels, or filters.
  • If you want this to be the Home view on your other devices too, check Sync home view.
  • Instructions

Change your name or avatar photo

Keep your Todoist up to date by changing your name or profile photo. Here’s how:

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Select Manage account. Your Todoist account settings will now open in a browser. Now you can:
  • Change your name by typing your name in the name field.
  • Change your avatar photo by clicking Change photo.
  • Remove your avatar photo by clicking Remove photo.
  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings. Now you can:
  • Change your name by typing your name in the name field.
  • Change your avatar photo by clicking Change photo.
  • Remove your avatar photo by clicking Remove photo.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Select Account. You can now:
  • Change your name by tapping Name. Type in your new name and tap OK.
  • Change your avatar by tapping your current avatar. You can then choose to either Take photo to take a photo and set it as your avatar, Choose photo to select a photo from your device, or Remove current photo to remove your current avatar.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Tap Account. You can now:
  • Change your full name by tapping your current name. Enter your new name and tap Done.
  • Change your avatar by tapping Edit under your current avatar. You can then either select Take Photo to take a photo and set it as your avatar, select Choose from Photos to select a photo from your device, or select Remove Current Photo to remove your current avatar.
  • Instructions

Change your password

Update your password on any of your devices and keep your Todoist account secure.

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Under Password, select Change password.
  • If you don’t have a password because you use your Google, Facebook, or Apple account to log in to Todoist, click Add Password and enter your new password.

  • Enter your new password twice to confirm the change.
  • Click Change password to save your changes.
  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Click the Account tab.
  • Click Manage Account. This will open your Todoist settings in a browser.
  • Under Password, select Change password.
  • If you don’t have a password because you use your Google, Facebook, or Apple account to log in to Todoist, click Add Password and enter your new password.
  • Enter your current password.
  • Enter your new password twice to confirm the change.
  • Click Change password to save your changes.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Tap Account.
  • Tap Change password.
  • If you don’t have a password because you use your Google, Facebook, or Apple account to log in to Todoist, tap Add Password and enter your new password.
  • Enter your current password.
  • Enter your new password twice to confirm the change.
  • Tap Done to save your changes.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Select Account.
  • Tap Password.
  • If you don’t have a password because you use your Google, Facebook, or Apple account to log in to Todoist, tap Add Password and enter your new password.
  • Enter your current password.
  • Enter your new password twice to confirm the change.
  • Tap the send icon to save the changes.

Create a Todoist account

Thanks for checking out Todoist. We’re very happy to have you with us!

You can easily get up and running with a new account in seconds:

Select Platform:

  • Open Todoist.
  • In the top-right corner, click Start for free.
  • Choose how you want to sign up to Todoist:
    • If you want to sign up with your Google account, click Continue with Google.
    • If you want to sign up with your Facebook account, click Continue with Facebook.
    • If you want to sign up with your Apple account, click Continue with Apple.
    • If you want to sign up with your email, enter your email address, add a secure password, and click Sign up with Email.
  • Open Todoist for iOS.
  • Choose how you want to sign up to Todoist:
    • Continue with Apple: sign up with your Apple account
    • Continue with Google: sign up with your Google account
    • Continue with Email : tap Sign up with Email to use your email address
    • Continue with more options: sign up with your Facebook account
  • Open Todoist for Android.
  • Choose how you want to sign up to Todoist:
    • Continue with Google: sign up with your Google account
    • Continue with Email: tap Sign up with Email to use your email address
    • Continue with more options: sign up with your Facebook account Quick tip

If you’re just starting with Todoist, be sure to check our Get Started Guide.

  • Instructions

Delete your Todoist account

If Todoist isn’t the right tool for what you want to achieve, and you don’t want to use it again in the future, you may choose to delete your account. Doing so will delete all of your Todoist data, and you will no longer be able to collaborate in shared projects or teams.

Warning

Account deletion is permanent and irreversible. If you choose to delete your account, you won’t be able to restore it or any data associated with the account.

Export your data

If you want a copy of your data for safekeeping, you have choices depending on your needs:

  • For a basic copy of your project data, export each of your projects as a CSV file. This will include all active tasks and specific attributes, like labels, dates, priorities, and comments.
  • If you don’t need all task attributes, use the Export to Google Sheets extension. It excludes deadlines, comments, attachments, and reminders, but it allows you to include your project’s completed tasks.
  • If you’re on a paid plan, download the latest backup of all your active projects and tasks. Completed tasks and archived projects aren’t included.

Leave or delete your team workspace

If you attempt to delete your Todoist account while you’re a member of a team workspace, you’ll see a prompt to either leave the team workspace or delete it.

If you’re the last admin, you won’t be able to leave, because a team workspace always needs at least one admin. This often applies if you created a team when you signed up and never added anyone else. You have two ways to continue:

  • Promote another member to admin, then leave the team workspace
  • Delete the team workspace, which permanently removes all team data, including projects, tasks, comments, and files Note

Team workspaces can only be managed in the Todoist web or desktop app. On iOS or Android, switch to the web or desktop app to promote an admin or delete the team workspace.

Once you’ve left or deleted the team workspace, you can delete your account.

Delete your account

Once you’ve removed yourself from any team workspaces, and have stored your data in a safe place, it’s time to delete your Todoist account:

Select Platform:

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com. If you’re having trouble logging in to your account, reset your account password.
  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Select Settings. If you logged in using Google or your Apple Account, add a Todoist password first.
  • Click Delete account.
  • Enter your password.
  • Click Delete account again to confirm. If you’ve set up two-factor authentication for your account, enter your authentication code to complete the process. After deleting your Todoist account, you’ll be redirected to the login page.

If you’re the last admin of a team workspace, leave or delete the team workspace in the Todoist web or desktop app first. This isn’t possible on iOS.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Tap Account. If you logged in using Google or your Apple Account, add a Todoist password first.
  • Tap Delete Account.
  • Tap Continue.
  • Enter your password.
  • Tap Delete to confirm. If you’ve set up two-factor authentication for your account, enter your authentication code to complete the process. After deleting your Todoist account, you’ll be redirected to the login page.

If you’re the last admin of a team workspace, leave or delete the team workspace in the Todoist web or desktop app first. This isn’t possible on Android.

  • Tap on Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.
  • Select Account. If you logged in using Google or your Apple Account, add a Todoist password first.
  • Tap Delete Account.
  • Enter your password.
  • Tap Delete to confirm. If you’ve set up two-factor authentication for your account, enter your authentication code to complete the process. After deleting your Todoist account, you’ll be redirected to the login page.
Request account deletion if you can’t log in

Every step above starts with logging in to your account. If you can’t log in, get in touch with us to request account deletion, and tell us which of these applies:

  • You’ve lost access to the email address on the account and can’t receive the password reset email
  • Someone else used your email address to create a Todoist account that you didn’t sign up for We’ll take care of it.

Cancel any paid subscriptions

If you’ve purchased a paid plan through direct billing, it will cancel automatically after deleting the Todoist account.

If you paid for Todoist through an in-app purchase with Apple or Google, it won’t cancel automatically and you may be charged for the renewal. Learn how to cancel the subscription in the App Store or Google Play store.

Evert · Head of Customer Experience

If you uninstalled or deleted the Todoist app before following these steps, it’s possible your Todoist account is still active. Make sure to log in to Todoist to check if you’ve deleted the account.

Remove a Todoist calendar feed after deleting your account

If you previously subscribed to a Todoist calendar feed, deleting your account won’t remove it from your calendar app. You’ll need to remove the calendar from your calendar app separately.

To remove it from Apple Calendar on iPhone or iPad:

  • Open the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
  • Tap Calendar.
  • Tap Accounts.
  • Tap the Todoist entry.
  • Tap Delete Account. For Google Calendar or Outlook, follow the steps in Remove the Todoist calendar from your calendar app.

Log in or out of Todoist

Use Todoist on the web, desktop, or mobile. All you need is your account email address and password, or a linked Google, Apple, or Facebook account. You can also log out from any device at any time. If you’ve enabled two-factor authentication, you’ll need your authentication app or a recovery code to log in.

Log in to Todoist

Note

If you’ve enabled two-factor authentication for your account, you will need to get a code from your authentication app to log in. Learn more.

Select Platform:

  • Open the Todoist app.

  • Click Log in.

  • Choose how you want to log in to your account (it should be the same option you used to create your account):

    • Click Continue with Google and choose the Google account associated with your Todoist account.
    • Click Continue with Facebook and connect to your Facebook account.
    • Click Continue with Apple and connect to your Apple account.
    • Enter your email address and password and then click the Log in button.

  • Open the Todoist app.

  • Click Continue in your browser.

  • You’ll be redirected to the login page in your browser. Choose how you want to log in to your account (it should be the same option you used to create your account):

    • Click Continue with Google and choose the Google account associated with your Todoist account.
    • Click Continue with Facebook and connect to your Facebook account.
    • Click Continue with Apple and connect to your Apple account.
    • Enter your email address and password and then click the Log in button.

  • Click Open Todoist on the pop-up notification. Open Todoist for iOS and choose how you want to log in to the Todoist account:

  • Tap Continue with Apple to log in with a Apple ID.

  • Tap Continue with Google to log in with a Google account.

  • Tap More sign-in options and select any of the following:

    • Continue with Facebook to log in with a Facebook account.
    • Log in with Email to log in with an email address and password.
    • Sign up with Email to create a new Todoist account. Open Todoist for Android and choose how you want to log in to the Todoist account:

  • Tap Continue with Google to log in with a Google account.

  • Tap Continue with Facebook to log in with a Facebook account.

  • Tap More sign-in options and select any of the following:

    • Log in with Email to log in with an email address and password.
    • Sign up with Email to create a new Todoist account.

Log out of Todoist

Select Platform:

  • Open the Todoist app.

  • Click your avatar in the top-left.

  • Select Log out. To log out of Todoist on your iPhone:

  • Open Todoist for iOS.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.

  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.

  • Tap Log out. To log out of Todoist on your iPad:

  • Open the Todoist app.

  • Tap the gear icon in the top-left.

  • Tap Log out.

  • Open the Todoist app.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.

  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.

  • Tap Log out.

Recover your account

When you first set up two-factor authentication, Todoist generates a set of recovery codes for your account. If you’ve lost access to your third-party authentication app, and you can’t get the one-time passcode, you can use any of these recovery codes to log back in to your account.

If you saved them, here’s how you’ll use one to log back in:

  • Open the Todoist login page on your web browser.
  • Enter your account email address and password.
  • Click Enter a recovery code here below the Authentication code field.
  • Enter one of your saved recovery codes. If you didn’t save your recovery codes, or they’re no longer working, request a recovery code from our team. Todoist will send a recovery code to your account email address.

Usage limits in Todoist

Usage limits help keep Todoist fast, stable, and reliable for everyone. To ensure peak performance, we apply specific caps to tasks, projects, and file sizes. Review this guide to understand these usage limits and the increased capacity you get with Todoist Pro or the Business plan.

Quick tip

Check out our pricing page to compare the features available on each plan.

Why place a 300 active task limit? Why cap projects to 500? These limits ensure Todoist stays fast, stable, and reliable for everyone. Having too many active tasks in a single project can slow syncing down and increase the risk of performance issues. It applies to all plans, including Todoist Pro and Business, so there’s no option to increase these limits. That said, we’re working to make our sync engine faster, so we can increase these limits.

Verify your Todoist account

Note

You will not need to verify your email address if you’ve used your Apple, Facebook or Google account to set up your Todoist account.

For security reasons, when you sign up for Todoist we will ask you to verify your email address.

Once you’ve created your Todoist account, you’ll automatically receive an email with a verification link (this link will expire after 24 hours). You can verify your account either by clicking or tapping the Verify email button in the email, or by copy-pasting the link in the email into a browser.

If you can’t find the email, please check that:

  • It hasn’t landed in your spam folder.
  • That you are checking the email you’ve used to set up your Todoist account. Warning

Upon signing up to Todoist, you have 7 days to verify your account. If you do not verify your account within 7 days, you will not be able to access your account. Instead, when you try to log in, you will see an option to re-send a verification email.

Make sure there are no typos in the email address you’ve used to sign up to Todoist. If you’ve made a typo, follow these instructions to change your email address.

If there’s a typo in your email address and you don’t manage to verify your account within 7 days, we won’t be able to recover your account for you, unfortunately.

If you still can’t find the verification email (or if the link in your verification email has expired), you can re-send it. Here’s how:

  • Log in to your Todoist account on any platform.
  • At the bottom of the screen, you will see a pop-up telling you that you need to verify your account. You can trigger a new verification email by clicking or tapping the Re-send option. Warning

If you select the Re-send option several times and end up receiving several verification emails, the verification links in the older emails may have expired, so make sure you use the link in the email you’ve received most recently.

FAQ

Please contact us. Make sure you contact us with the email address you need to have verified.

AI connections

Use ChatGPT with Todoist (MCP)

Want to manage Todoist without switching tabs 47 times? Connecting Todoist’s MCP (Model Context Protocol) server to ChatGPT lets you read, create, and update tasks and projects from a chat.

This is especially helpful for weekly reviews, planning a project, or turning a brain-dump into a clean set of next actions.

Note

You can also connect Todoist to ChatGPT using the official Todoist plugin. See Use ChatGPT with Todoist (plugin) for step-by-step instructions.

Check the requirements

  • You’ll need access to ChatGPT Developer Mode (beta) to add a custom plugin like the Todoist MCP server. This requires a paid ChatGPT plan. If you’re using a team workspace, your admin may control this setting.
  • You’ll be logging in with OAuth, which means you’re authorizing ChatGPT to access Todoist through the official Todoist MCP server.

Enable beta developer features in ChatGPT

  • Open ChatGPT Settings.
  • Go to Plugins.
  • Open Advanced Settings.
  • Turn on Developer mode (beta). Note

Developer mode is powerful (it enables “write” actions through connected tools), so only enable it if you’re comfortable reviewing and approving actions that can change your data.

Add the Todoist MCP server

  • In ChatGPT, go to Settings > Plugins.
  • Choose the option to add a custom plugin (wording varies slightly by plan and UI).
  • For the server URL, use: ai.todoist.net.
  • Continue to authentication. Quick tip

The Todoist MCP server is hosted using Streamable HTTP, so you don’t need to run anything locally. For full technical details, see the Todoist MCP documentation.

Log in to Todoist and approve access

ChatGPT will open a Todoist authorization screen. Log in and approve the requested permissions.

You’ll see exactly what Todoist access is being requested during OAuth. Take a quick look before approving.

What ChatGPT will have access to

Once connected, ChatGPT can use the Todoist MCP server to:

  • Read your Todoist tasks and projects.
  • Create tasks and projects.
  • Update tasks and projects (for example: rename, reschedule, move to a project). Warning

Because this connection supports “write” actions, ChatGPT can make changes to your Todoist data when you ask it to (or when it’s following your instructions). Developer mode is intended for people who understand the risks and want that extra power.

Examples of what you can do

Here are a few prompts that work well once you’re connected:

Category

Example prompts

Inbox triage

Look at my Todoist Inbox and suggest five quick wins I can finish today.

Turn these messy tasks into clearer next actions, and ask me questions only where you truly need more context.

Weekly review support

List my overdue tasks by project and suggest what to reschedule vs. drop.

Show me everything due in the next 7 days and help me choose a realistic plan.

Project planning

Create a project called “Website refresh” with sections for “Content,” “Design,” and “Launch” then add a first-pass task list.

Move anything tagged “waiting” into a “Waiting for” section and add a follow-up task for next Tuesday.

Natural-language task capture

“Add a task: ‘Call the dentist next week’ and put it in my Personal project.”

“Create a task for ‘Submit expenses’ every last Friday.”

Anything you can describe clearly, ChatGPT can usually translate into structured Todoist changes. Just skim before confirming.

Privacy and data handling

When you connect a plugin in ChatGPT, the data shared is handled according to the plugin’s terms and privacy policies, which you’ll see before enabling the plugin.

If you want extra peace of mind, consider using ChatGPT’s data controls. For example, opting out of having chats used to improve models, and being thoughtful about what you paste into any AI chat.

Disconnecting Todoist MCP

You can disconnect in two places:

  • In ChatGPT: open Settings > Plugins and remove or disable the Todoist plugin.
  • In Todoist: revoke access from Todoist’s Integrations settings (where you manage developer/integration access).

Troubleshooting

I don’t see Developer mode (beta)

It may not be available on your plan yet, or it may be disabled by your workspace admin.

I see a “lack of access permissions” error (work or company account)

If you finished logging in but ChatGPT still says it lacks access permissions, you’re most likely using a managed ChatGPT account (Business, Enterprise, or Edu) through your workplace or school.

On those plans, individual members can’t add custom plugins or turn on Developer mode by themselves. A workspace administrator has to allow it for your role first. Until they do, ChatGPT can keep refusing the connection even after you’ve logged in.

Here’s what helps:

  • Ask whoever manages your organization’s ChatGPT account to allow Developer mode and the Todoist plugin for your role, in ChatGPT’s admin settings.
  • Try connecting with a personal ChatGPT account to confirm the cause. If it works there, the block is your organization’s permission settings. Note

Because this is controlled on the ChatGPT side, it isn’t something we can enable for you from Todoist.

I can’t get the OAuth window to open, or it keeps failing

Try disabling strict pop-up blockers for the login flow and retry.

I see “Sorry, something went wrong” after I click Allow access

This usually means your browser didn’t send a small security token (a CSRF token) that Todoist needs to finish authorizing, most often because cookies for todoist.com are being blocked, or because the page sat open too long. It isn’t a problem with your account.

Try this, in order:

  • Use a normal browser window (not private or incognito) and allow cookies for todoist.com.
  • Log in to Todoist in that same browser first.
  • Turn off strict tracking protection, ad blockers, or privacy extensions for todoist.com, or try a different browser such as Chrome. (Microsoft Edge’s tracking prevention is a common culprit.)
  • Start the connection again and click Allow access without waiting too long.
  • Clear todoist.com cookies and try once more if it persists.
ChatGPT is connected but can’t see or change my tasks

First, make sure Developer mode is enabled and that the Todoist plugin is switched on for the current chat.

If ChatGPT still can’t read or update your tasks, reconnect from both sides:

  • In ChatGPT, go to Settings > Plugins and remove the Todoist plugin.
  • In Todoist, go to Settings > Integrations and revoke access for the ChatGPT connection.
  • Go back to Add the Todoist MCP server above and reconnect.
ChatGPT is missing my completed recurring tasks

Recurring tasks don’t show up in your completed tasks. Completing one reschedules it to the next occurrence instead of marking it done, and Todoist records that in your activity log.

To see everything you finished, ask ChatGPT for the activity log by name:

  • Name the activity log in your request, such as: Using my Todoist activity log, what did I complete yesterday?
  • Give it a date or a range when you want a specific period, such as: Check my Todoist activity log and list everything I finished this week. ChatGPT returns every completion in that period, recurring tasks included.

Your plan sets how much history is available. The Beginner plan keeps 7 days of activity, and Pro and Business keep your full history. You can browse the same history in Todoist reporting.

I get errors, or the connection drops mid-chat

The Todoist MCP server can occasionally have brief interruptions. If you get an unexpected error during a request, wait a few minutes and try again.

If it keeps happening, disconnect from both ChatGPT (Settings > Plugins) and Todoist (Settings > Integrations), then reconnect.

ChatGPT asks me to approve every change. Can I turn that off?

That prompt comes from ChatGPT, not Todoist. Because the Todoist plugin can change your data, ChatGPT adds a confirmation step before it writes anything. This isn’t a setting we control on the Todoist side.

You can still change how often ChatGPT asks. ChatGPT lets you set a permission level for the Todoist plugin, ranging from “Always ask” to “Never ask”:

  • In ChatGPT, open your settings and go to the Todoist plugin’s permissions.
  • Choose a less strict level, or “Never ask”, to reduce or remove the per-action prompts. Note

Because this is a safety step, ChatGPT may still pause on especially sensitive actions, and the exact options can depend on your ChatGPT plan.

Use Claude Code with Todoist (CLI and MCP)

Connect Todoist to Claude Code and manage your tasks without leaving your terminal. Once connected, Claude Code can create, read, and update your Todoist tasks and projects, great for staying in flow while you work.

There are two ways to connect: the Todoist CLI (the quickest, and what we recommend) or the Todoist MCP (Model Context Protocol) server.

Prefer a chat-first workflow instead? You can also connect Todoist to Claude via the Todoist connector. See Use Claude with Todoist (connector) for the instructions.

Set up the Todoist CLI (recommended)

The Todoist CLI lets Claude Code manage your tasks by running td commands right in your terminal.

Check the requirements
  • Node.js and npm installed on your machine.
  • Claude Code installed and authenticated.
  • A Todoist account to sign in to.
Install and connect

  1. Install the CLI

    npm install -g @doist/todoist-cli

Using a different coding agent? The Todoist CLI also installs skills for Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini, and more. See the Todoist CLI repo for the full setup.

  1. Install the Claude Code skill so Claude Code knows how to use it.

    td skill install claude-code

  2. Authenticate with Todoist

    td auth login

td auth login opens your browser to sign in with OAuth, then stores your token securely in your operating system’s credential manager (Keychain on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows, Secret Service on Linux). Once connected, just ask Claude Code in plain language and it runs the right td commands for you.

Quick tip

Want Claude Code to read your tasks but never change them? Run td auth login --read-only instead. In read-only mode, any command that would create, update, or delete data is blocked.

Set up Todoist MCP in Claude Code

Prefer to connect through the Model Context Protocol server instead of the CLI? You can. Once connected, you can create, read, and update Todoist tasks and projects without ever leaving your coding environment.

Check the requirements
  • A paid Claude plan: Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise, or Console. The free Claude.ai plan doesn’t include Claude Code access.
  • Claude Code installed and authenticated on your machine.
  • You’ll be signing in with OAuth, which authorizes Claude Code to access Todoist through the official Todoist MCP server. There are two ways to connect Todoist to Claude Code. The Todoist plugin is the quickest, so it’s the one we recommend. If you’d rather set things up yourself, you can add the server manually instead.
Connect with the Todoist plugin (recommended)

In Claude Code, run these two commands:

/plugin marketplace add doist/todoist-mcp
/plugin install todoist@doist

The first time you use a Todoist tool, Claude Code opens your browser so you can sign in with OAuth. Once you’ve approved access, there’s nothing else to set up.

Connect manually

If you prefer to add the server yourself, run this command in your terminal:

claude mcp add --transport http todoist [ai.todoist.net](https://ai.todoist.net/mcp)

Then open Claude Code, run /mcp, select Todoist from the list, and complete the OAuth flow in your browser.

Warning

Add the server only once. Running claude mcp add again creates a duplicate entry, which can cause sign-in loops. Run /mcp first to check whether Todoist is already connected.

What Claude Code will have access to

Once connected through either the CLI or MCP, Claude Code can:

  • Read your Todoist tasks and projects
  • Create tasks and projects
  • Update tasks and projects (for example: rename, reschedule, or move to a different project) Warning

Because this connection supports write actions, Claude Code can make changes to your Todoist data when you instruct it to. Review any changes before confirming them.

Examples of what you can do

Here are a few prompts that work well once you’re connected:

Category

Example prompts

Capture tasks from your code

Add a task to Todoist: ‘Fix the auth bug in login.js’ and put it in the Engineering project.

Create a task for ‘Write unit tests for the payment module’ and set it due this Friday.

Plan your work

List all my overdue Todoist tasks and help me decide what to tackle today.

Show me everything due this week and suggest what I can realistically finish.

Triage your inbox

Go through my Todoist Inbox and turn each item into a clear, actionable next step.

Move any tasks tagged ‘waiting’ into a ‘Waiting for’ section and add a follow-up task for next Monday.

Stay in flow

I’m working on the checkout feature, check Todoist and tell me if there are any related open tasks.

Add a task for every TODO comment in this file and put them all in the current sprint project.

Privacy and data handling

When you connect Todoist through MCP, your task data is shared with both Todoist’s servers and Claude. Data handling on Todoist’s side is governed by Todoist’s privacy policy; data that enters Claude’s context (your tasks, projects, and so on) is also subject to Anthropic’s privacy policy.

For extra peace of mind, review what permissions you’ve granted at any time by visiting Todoist’s Settings > Integrations.

Disconnect Todoist from Claude Code

If you connected with the CLI: run td auth logout to remove the saved token, then revoke access from Todoist’s Settings > Integrations.

If you connected with the MCP server, you can disconnect from two places:

  • In Claude Code: run claude mcp remove todoist in your terminal to remove the server.
  • In Todoist: revoke access from Settings > Integrations to revoke Claude Code’s access.

Tips for best results

A few habits will help you get the most out of Todoist in Claude Code:

Batch tasks when adding several at once

The Todoist MCP supports up to 25 tasks per call. Tell Claude to add them all together: “Add all of these in a single call.” Creating them one by one can exhaust Claude’s tool-call limit before your list is complete.

Use “reschedule” for recurring tasks

To move a recurring task to a new date, say “reschedule this task to date” rather than “change the date.” The reschedule tool keeps the recurrence pattern; the other one doesn’t.

Create team-folder projects first, then move them

The Todoist MCP can’t place a new project inside a workspace folder when it’s created. Ask Claude to create the project, then drag it into the right folder in Todoist.

Check your connection before opening a new session

If Claude stops responding to Todoist requests mid-conversation, run /mcp to check whether the connection’s still active. Reconnecting from there is faster than starting a new session.

Troubleshooting

The claude mcp add command isn’t recognized

Make sure Claude Code is installed and up to date. See the Claude Code documentation for installation instructions.

The OAuth browser window doesn’t open

Try running the Claude Code command again. If the window still doesn’t appear, check that your browser isn’t blocking pop-ups and retry.

The server shows in claude mcp list but Todoist tools aren’t available

Start a new Claude Code session after adding the server. MCP servers only load at session start, so an existing one won’t pick up new connections.

“No transport found for sessionId” error

Go to Todoist Settings > Integrations and remove all Claude Code entries. Then run /mcp in Claude Code, select Todoist, and sign in again. (Our team is aware of this issue and working on a fix.)

Multiple “Claude Code” entries in Settings > Integrations

This happens when claude mcp add runs more than once. Remove all Claude Code entries in Todoist Settings > Integrations, then reconnect once via /mcp.

Claude stops partway through creating a long task list

This is Claude’s tool-call limit, not a Todoist one. Ask Claude to batch the tasks: “Add all of these in a single call.” The Todoist MCP supports up to 25 tasks per call.

A recurring task lost its repeat schedule

This happens when Claude changes the date instead of rescheduling the task. For recurring tasks, say “reschedule this task to date” rather than “change the date.” If the recurrence was lost, set it again in the task’s date field.

Claude created a project outside the right team folder

The Todoist MCP can’t place a project inside a workspace folder when it’s created. Ask Claude to create the project, then move it to the right folder in Todoist.

Report a bug or request a feature

The Todoist MCP server is open source. You can report bugs, request features, or browse known issues in the official Todoist AI repository on GitHub.

Use Claude with the Todoist Connector

Want to plan, triage, and capture tasks without leaving your Claude conversation? Connect Todoist to Claude via the Todoist connector for a chat-first workflow. This lets Claude read, create, and update your Todoist tasks and projects without the context switching.

Note

Working in Claude Code instead? Learn how to connect Todoist to Claude Code through the Todoist CLI and MCP.

Check account requirements

To use Claude with Todoist, check if you meet all the account requirements:

  • Sign up for a Claude account on any plan.
  • Owner or Primary Owner on any Claude Team and Enterprise plan should enable connectors for their organization, so that members can add them.
  • Log in to Claude with OAuth, which gives Claude access through the official Todoist connector.

Set up the integration

The Todoist connector lets Claude read and update your tasks and projects directly from a conversation. You only need to set it up once for it to be available on all your devices.

Let’s start by setting up the integration:

Find Todoist in the Connector directory
  • Log in to Claude.
  • Click the plus button at the lower-left corner of the chat.
  • Click Connectors.
  • Click Add connector.
  • Select Browse connectors.
  • Search for Todoist in the Connector directory.
  • Click Connect.
Log in to Todoist and approve access

Follow the prompts to log in to your Todoist account. Review the requested permissions, and approve access. Once authorized, Todoist is ready to use in your Claude conversations.

Todoist tools load at the start of each conversation. If you’ve just connected, open a new chat. They’ll be ready to use.

Learn what Claude has access to

When set up correctly, Claude can use Todoist to:

  • Read your Todoist tasks and projects.
  • Create tasks and projects.
  • Update tasks and projects (for example: rename, reschedule, or move to a different project). Warning

The connection supports write actions, so you can prompt Claude to add, edit, or delete tasks in Todoist. Make sure to review all the changes before confirming them.

Limitations to the Todoist Connector

Claude handles most everyday Todoist actions through the connector. Here’s what it can do today, and the few things it can’t do yet:

Claude supports

Claude doesn’t support

Read, create, update, or complete tasks

Add or move a new project inside a team workspace folder

Read, create, or update projects

Reorder projects in the sidebar

Schedule or reschedule recurring or non-recurring tasks

Manage sections, labels, comments, or filters

Assign tasks in shared projects

Note

If you ask Claude to “change the date” on a recurring task, it’ll remove the repeat schedule. Use “reschedule” instead. For example, “Reschedule my Weekly Review to Friday” to keep the recurrence intact.

Try these Claude prompt examples

Anything you can describe clearly, Claude can usually translate into structured Todoist changes. Here are a few prompts that work well once you’re connected to Claude:

Category

Example prompts

Inbox triage

  • Look at my Todoist Inbox and suggest five quick wins I can finish today.

  • Turn these messy tasks into clearer next actions, and ask me questions only where you truly need more context. Weekly review support

  • List my overdue tasks by project and suggest what to reschedule or drop.

  • Show me everything due in the next 7 days and help me choose a realistic plan. Project planning

  • Create a project called “Website refresh” with sections for “Content,” “Design,” and “Launch,” then add a first-pass task list.

  • Move anything tagged “waiting” into a “Waiting for” section and add a follow-up task for next Tuesday. Natural-language task capture

  • “Add a task: ‘Call the dentist next week’ and put it in my Personal project.”

  • “Create a task for ‘Submit expenses’ every last Friday.” Large batch of tasks

Claude can add up to 25 tasks in a single action. If you’re working with a long list, be specific in your prompts.

  • Add all these tasks in a single call.
  • Add all these tasks to the Groceries project.

Learn about privacy and data handling

When you connect Todoist to Claude, your task data is shared with both Todoist’s servers and Claude. Data handling on Todoist’s side is governed by Todoist’s privacy policy; data that enters Claude’s context (your tasks, projects, and so on) is also subject to Anthropic’s privacy policy.

For extra peace of mind, review what permissions you’ve granted at any time by visiting Todoist’s Settings > Integrations.

Troubleshoot the integration

As you use the Todoist connector, you may encounter a technical issue or an error message in Claude. Here’s how to troubleshoot the most common issues with the Todoist connector, and how to resolve them:

Todoist doesn’t appear in the connector directory

If you’re on a Team or Enterprise plan, check with your workspace admin if connectors are enabled for your organization. An Owner or Primary Owner must enable connectors before members can add and use them.

OAuth connection failure between Claude and Todoist

Connection failures almost always happen during the OAuth login step. Follow these steps in this exact order:

  • Disable strict pop-up blockers, then try logging in again.
  • Check Settings > Connectors in Claude. Then, open a new chat to see if Todoist appears there. The connection may still have gone through even if you saw “Sorry, the page you’re looking for isn’t here anymore” right after approving access.
  • Check if the Owner or Primary Owner of your Claude team workspace approved the Todoist connector. When checking the connector, you’ll only see the “Requested” status until they manually approve it.
OAuth window doesn’t open or keeps failing

Disable strict pop-up blockers for the login flow and try again.

“Sorry, the page you’re looking for isn’t here anymore” error

After you approve access in the Todoist login window, Claude may show a “Sorry, the page you’re looking for isn’t here anymore” error.

Open Claude and go to Settings > Connectors to check whether Todoist appears as connected. If it does, open a new conversation and you’re ready to use it. If Todoist doesn’t appear, look for the Todoist connector in Claude. Then, click Connect to start the connection again.

Todoist connector shows “Requested” and won’t complete

If you’re a member of a Claude Team or Enterprise plan, you may see that the Todoist connector shows as “Requested”, but it doesn’t complete the setup. This is because individual connector requests need approval from your organization’s Owner or Primary Owner inside Claude before the connection can finish.

To resolve this, contact the Claude Owner or Primary Owner of your workspace, and ask them to approve the Todoist connector. Once approved, find Todoist in the Claude Connection directory and add Todoist to complete the connection.

There’s nothing to approve from the Todoist app.

Stuck at the Claude sign-up or login page

When setting up the integration, clicking Connect may take you to a Claude sign-up or login page. This happens when you’re not logged in to your Claude account.

To resolve this, open a web browser and log in to Claude. Then, open the Connection directory and try adding the Todoist connector again.

Claude says it has no Todoist tools, or the tools don’t appear

Todoist tools load at the start of each conversation, so open a new chat first if you’ve just connected or reconnected.

If a fresh chat doesn’t help, follow these steps:

  • Log in to your Claude account.
  • Click Settings > Connectors and check that Todoist still shows as connected. If it isn’t added as a connector, search and add Todoist.
  • Update to the latest version of Claude, especially if you’re using the Claude apps for iOS and Android. A recent update added an extra approval step, so you’ll need to allow Claude to discover connectors and give permission to use Todoist again. Note

Tools that still won’t load on the Claude apps for iOS and Android are a known issue, rather than in Todoist. Use Claude on the web browser or the desktop app in the meantime. If you’re still running into issues, contact Anthropic Support for help, since the fix needs to come from their side.

Claude created a project but it’s in the wrong place

The Todoist MCP can’t place a new project inside a workspace folder. After Claude creates the project, move it to the right folder manually in Todoist.

A recurring task lost its repeat schedule

This happens when Claude changes the date instead of rescheduling the task. For recurring tasks, say “reschedule this task to [date]” rather than “change the date to [date].” If the recurrence was lost, open the task in Todoist and set it again in the task date field.

Remove the integration

If you need to disconnect Todoist from Claude to troubleshoot an issue, or you no longer want to use the integration, here’s how to remove the integration:

  • Open Claude.

  • Click Settings > Connectors.

  • Select Todoist.

  • Click Disconnect. Then, switch to Todoist and disconnect the integration:

  • Log in to Todoist.

  • Click Settings.

  • Select the Integrations tab.

  • Select Claude.

  • Click Remove.

Use the Todoist plugin in ChatGPT

Add the official Todoist plugin in ChatGPT to manage your tasks without leaving the conversation. Once it’s connected, ChatGPT can read, create, and update the tasks and projects in your Todoist account, so you can plan your week, capture ideas, or tidy your Inbox right in the chat.

Note

Prefer to wire things up manually? You can also connect Todoist’s MCP (Model Context Protocol) server to ChatGPT.

Before you start

  • You’ll need a ChatGPT account.
  • You’ll need a Todoist account to sign in to. Note

Connect once and Todoist stays available everywhere you’re signed in to ChatGPT.

Connect the Todoist plugin

  • Open ChatGPT.
  • Click Plugins in the sidebar.
  • Search for Todoist. You’ll see the Todoist plugin.
  • Click the plus sign to connect the plugin. A window tab will open in your web browser.
  • Log in to your Todoist account.
  • Approve the requested permissions. Once the plugin is set up, type /todoist in any ChatGPT conversation to bring it up. Describe what you want in plain language.

Use the Todoist plugin

Once connected, ChatGPT can work with your Todoist account in multiple ways, including:

  • Read your tasks and projects.
  • Create new tasks and projects.
  • Update what’s already there, such as renaming a task, shifting its date, or moving it to another project. Warning

This connection can read and make changes to your data. ChatGPT acts only when you ask it to, but it’s worth checking each change before you confirm it.

Example prompts to try

Once you’re connected, plain language is enough to get things done.

Category

Example prompts

Plan your day

What’s overdue across my projects? Suggest three tasks that I should tackle first.

Pull everything due today and help me put it in a realistic order.

Capture quickly

Add “Email the venue about parking” to my Events project, due Thursday.

Create a recurring task to review my goals on the first of every month.

Shape a project

Start a project called “Q3 launch” with sections for Research, Build, and Review.

Move my unscheduled Marketing tasks into a “This month” section.

Tidy up

Find tasks with no date in my Work project and suggest deadlines.

Rename my vague Inbox tasks into clear next actions.

Quick tip

If you can describe it clearly, ChatGPT can usually turn it into the right Todoist action. Glance over its work before you confirm.

Privacy and data handling

Connecting the Todoist plugin means your data moves between Todoist and ChatGPT. On the Todoist side, the data is covered by Todoist’s privacy policy; once it reaches ChatGPT, it also falls under OpenAI’s privacy policy. In Todoist, open Settings > Integrations to review the permissions you’ve granted at any time.

Disconnect the Todoist plugin

If you no longer want to use the Todoist plugin in ChatGPT, here’s how to remove it:

  • From ChatGPT: open Settings > Plugins. Select Todoist, then click Disconnect.
  • From Todoist: open Settings > Integrations. Select ChatGPT, then click Remove.

Troubleshoot the Todoist plugin

The OAuth window doesn’t open or keeps failing

Disable strict pop-up blockers for the sign-in flow, and try again.

Completed recurring tasks are missing

Recurring tasks don’t show up in your completed tasks. Completing one reschedules it to the next occurrence instead of marking it done, and Todoist records that in your activity log.

To see everything you finished, ask ChatGPT for the activity log by name:

  • Name the activity log in your request, such as: Using my Todoist activity log, what did I complete yesterday?
  • Give it a date or a range when you want a specific period, such as: Check my Todoist activity log and list everything I finished this week. ChatGPT returns every completion in that period, recurring tasks included.

Your plan sets how much history is available. The Beginner plan keeps 7 days of activity, and Pro and Business keep your full history. You can browse the same history in Todoist reporting.

AI features

Capture tasks from text, images, and documents

Ever walked out of a meeting with notes scattered across three different apps, or snapped a quick photo of a whiteboard before someone erases it? Todoist can take all that unstructured content and turn it into actual tasks – pulling out dates, priorities, and more so you don’t have to.

Whether it’s bullet points from your meeting notes or that grocery list your partner scribbled on a napkin, just paste or upload it into Quick Add and Todoist handles the rest.

How it works

Select Platform:

Capture tasks from a file (image or document)
  • Open Quick Add.
  • Click the + button to open the More actions menu.
  • Select Scan file.
  • Add your file.
  • Click Add task(s).
Capture tasks from text (using copy/paste)
  • Open Quick Add.
  • Paste your text (multiple lines or >500 characters). This will open a prompt.
  • Click Scan text for tasks.
  • Click Add task(s).
Capture tasks from text (using the More actions menu)
  • Open Quick Add.
  • Click the + button to open the More actions menu.
  • Select Scan text.
  • Drop in your content.
  • Click Process text.
  • Click Add task(s). Note

In the Todoist desktop or web app, you can click the x next to a task to remove it individually before confirming.

Capture tasks from a file
  • Open Quick Add.
  • Tap the Attachment button.
  • Add your file.
  • Tap the scan icon next to the attachment.
  • Tap Add task(s).
Capture tasks from text (using copy/paste)
  • Open Quick Add.
  • Paste your text (multiple lines or >500 characters). This will open a prompt.
  • Tap Scan Text.
  • Tap Done to add all tasks. Note

You can swipe to selectively remove individual tasks before confirming.

Capture tasks from a file
  • Open Quick Add.

Capture tasks from text (using copy/paste)

You can swipe to selectively remove individual tasks before confirming.

What you can capture

📝 Text input

Paste anything – formatted text, bullet points, content from emails, or notes from other apps. Up to 25,000 characters at once.

📸 Images

Upload JPEG, PNG, or WebP files up to 7MB and 4000×4000px. Photos of typed text or clear handwriting work best.

📄 Documents

Upload PDF, MD, or TXT files up to 7MB.

Quick tip

To get the best results with images, use good lighting and get close enough that text fills most of the frame. Photos of whiteboards, handwritten notes, and typed documents all work – just make sure the text is clear and legible.

Privacy and security

Your data stays secure: Text and files are processed securely and aren’t stored or used for training. Only the resulting tasks and their details are saved in Todoist.

Note

This feature runs on Todoist Assist, which operates entirely on our secure infrastructure. Your data never leaves our servers, isn’t shared with third parties, and isn’t used to train any LLM models. Check our privacy policy for complete details.

Comparison with other capture methods

Text/File capture vs. Ramble

Ramble captures your spoken thoughts in real-time – you talk, it transcribes, and creates tasks as you go. Text and file capture works with content you’ve already gathered. Both help you dump unstructured information into Todoist quickly, just in different ways.

Use Ramble when you’re brainstorming or want to talk through your thoughts. Use text and file capture when you’ve got existing notes, photos, or content from other sources.

Feature not showing up?

Double-check that you are on a Pro or Business plan.

Tasks not being recognized properly?
  • For text: Try using bullet points or numbered lists for better recognition
  • For images: Make sure your file is under 7MB and the text is clear and legible
  • For handwriting: Results may vary depending on clarity – typed text generally works better

Dictate to add tasks with Ramble

Ramble is a voice-to-tasks feature in Todoist that lets you quickly add tasks using your voice. Speak naturally. Ramble listens, transcribes, and captures actionable tasks in real-time. This makes adding tasks on the fly fast and effortless, whether your thoughts are organized or not.

Note

Ramble captures your tasks in real-time as you talk, not after you finish. It’s a quick capture tool rather than a conversational assistant, so say each task clearly before moving to the next one.

Play

Add a task with Ramble

After your mic’s hooked up, here’s how to dictate and capture tasks with Ramble:

Select Platform:

Play

  • Click the waveform icon in Quick Add or the sidebar. If you’re using the desktop apps, you can also click the Todoist menu bar icon for macOS or app tray icon for Windows and Linux.
  • Speak what you need to do freely. Ramble will capture tasks in a preview mode as you talk.
  • Say phrases like “Actually, I meant…” to edit a task, or “Remove that” to delete a suggested task.
  • End the session by saying “that’s all” or clicking Add tasks in the preview. Nina · Customer Experience Specialist

Try out these keyboard shortcuts! Use ⇧ Shift + Q to open Ramble quickly while in the app. To use Ramble from anywhere and without opening Todoist, use Option ⌥ + Shift ⇧ + R on macOS or ⇧ Alt + Shift + R on Windows. If this is not your default shortcut, update it in Settings > Desktop.

Play

  • Tap the waveform icon in Quick Add. This opens Ramble.

  • Speak what you need to do freely. Ramble will capture tasks in a preview mode as you talk.

  • Say phrases like “Actually I meant…” to edit, or “Remove that” to delete a suggested task.

  • End the session by saying “that’s all” or clicking the checkmark button. Play

  • Tap the waveform icon in Quick Add. This opens Ramble.

  • Speak what you need to do freely. Ramble will capture tasks in a preview mode as you talk.

  • Say phrases like “Actually I meant…” to edit, or “Remove that” to delete a suggested task.

  • End the session by saying “that’s all” or clicking the checkmark button or add it as a quick setting tile.

  • Open the Todoist app on your Wear OS smartwatch.

  • Tap the Ramble button.

  • Speak your tasks freely. Ramble will capture them in a preview on your watch screen as you talk.

  • When you’re done, tap Done to submit your tasks to the Todoist Inbox. On Wear OS, all tasks are saved to your Inbox. You can move and refine them on your phone or other devices after capture.

Note

Ramble on Wear OS is currently in beta and only captures task name, date, and priority. If you run into issues or have ideas for improving the experience, share your feedback with us.

Note

When you’re in a project or label, Ramble will automatically apply the project or label to your tasks (you can still change this if you want to). Otherwise, tasks are added to your Inbox by default. You can select a different project before confirming.

Edit or delete tasks with Ramble

Ramble captures tasks in a preview mode as you talk. If you need to make changes, use phrases like “Actually, I meant…” to edit a task, or “Remove that” to delete it.

Plan usage

Ramble is currently an experimental feature that’s available to everyone, though usage limits apply based on your plan.

Beginner plan

Folks on the free or Beginner plan (as well as those on the Pro Legacy plan) can use Ramble with up to 10 sessions per month, which reset automatically on the 1st of each month (UTC). Each dictation counts as one session, even if you decide not to add the tasks to Todoist.

When you’ve reached your 10-session limit, Todoist will show a prompt inside Ramble. You won’t be able to start a new session until it resets at the start of the next month. Upgrading to Pro or Business removes this limit.

Your monthly Ramble count is shared across all devices. Whether you use Ramble on the web, desktop, mobile, or Wear OS, every session adds to the same total for your Todoist account.

Pro or Business plans

Todoist Pro and Business customers enjoy unlimited sessions as part of their subscriptions, though in rare cases, rate limiting may apply to keep Ramble running smoothly for everyone.

Share your feedback and help us improve Ramble.

System requirements

To access the latest Ramble features, including label selection on mobile and upcoming in-app guidance, make sure you’re on the minimum supported versions:

  • Web or desktop: 9250 or later
  • iOS or iPadOS: 25.11.17 or later
  • Android: 11962 or later
  • Wear OS: w12021 or later

How AI powers Ramble

Ramble is built on Todoist Assist, our AI-powered suite of productivity tools. When you use Ramble, advanced large language models (LLMs) work behind the scenes to:

  • Transcribe your speech accurately into text in real-time across 40+ languages.
  • Understand natural language to extract actionable tasks from your spoken thoughts.
  • Interpret task attributes like dates, deadlines, priorities, and durations from conversational phrases.
  • Learn from context to distinguish between tasks, edits, and deletions as you speak.
How is my data used?

When using Ramble, your input is processed securely and is not shared with third parties or used for training AI models. We may temporarily store usage data on our own secure servers to debug and improve the product. Todoist is SOC2 Type II certified, with enterprise-grade security and privacy controls. Check our privacy policy for more details.

Microphone access

Before jumping into Ramble, check if your microphone’s set up correctly:

  • First use: You’ll see a prompt to enable microphone access. Approve to start dictating.
  • Active microphone: In Ramble, you can see which mic is in use or switch to a different one, if needed.
  • Denied access: If you’ve denied access, follow the on-screen instructions to enable it in your system or browser settings.
  • No microphone detected: If no mic is found, connect one or check your system settings.

Access Ramble on mobile

Select Platform:

Keep Ramble within reach by adding the Ramble widget to your home screen or lock screen, or as a control on iOS.

If your iPhone has an Action button, you can assign it to open Ramble directly:

  • Open the System Settings app of your iOS device.
  • Tap Action Button.
  • Swipe left until you see the Controls option.
  • Tap Choose a Control…
  • Search for and select Ramble. Add the Ramble widget to your home screen, touch and hold the Todoist app icon, or add it as a quick setting tile.

Best practices when using Ramble

Bring your productivity full circle with these best practices when using Ramble:

Speak naturally but signal tasks clearly

Begin with actionable cues like “I need to…”, “I want to…” or imperative verbs, such as “Buy milk”. This helps Ramble spot tasks instantly. Ramble isn’t optimized for assistance requests such as “Can you plan my trip to Japan?”.

Improve speech recognition

Speak slower, closer to the mic, and minimize background noise.

Pause between each item on your list

When rattling off several tasks (“For the trip: book flights, renew passport, buy adapter”), pause slightly between each item to give Ramble room to create separate tasks.

Use quick corrections

If you misspoke or need to make edits, just say “Actually, make that…” or similar. Ramble will update automatically – no need to stop or undo manually.

You can also delete tasks as you Ramble on. For a phrase like “I need to buy apples”, you can follow with “Scratch that, I already have some” or “Forget the apples”.

Activate Ramble with Siri

You can activate Ramble using Siri on your iOS:

  • Open Shortcuts.
  • Tap the plus icon.
  • Search for Ramble.
  • Tap Open Ramble.
  • To trigger the shortcut, say “Hey Siri, open Ramble”.
  • Start rambling.

Troubleshoot issues with Ramble

If you’re having trouble with microphone access, dictation, or general errors with Ramble, check if it’s a limitation or follow these troubleshooting steps to resolve them.

Limitations

Ramble follows the same task limits as the rest of Todoist. If a project already has 300 active tasks, Todoist will let you know when Ramble can’t add more tasks there. You can choose another project or delete some of the existing tasks before trying again.

Ramble is quite the polyglot, and understands the following languages:

  • Arabic
  • Bengali
  • Bulgarian
  • Chinese (simplified and traditional)
  • Croatian
  • Czech
  • Danish
  • Dutch
  • English
  • Estonian
  • Finnish
  • French
  • German
  • Greek
  • Hebrew
  • Hindi
  • Hungarian
  • Icelandic
  • Indonesian
  • Italian
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Latvian
  • Lithuanian
  • Norwegian
  • Polish

  • Romanian
  • Russian
  • Serbian
  • Slovak
  • Slovenian
  • Spanish
  • Swahili
  • Swedish
  • Thai
  • Turkish
  • Ukrainian
  • Vietnamese Ramble isn’t supported when using the Todoist browser extensions. These extensions can’t reliably access your microphone due to the browser’s privacy and security restrictions.

To use Ramble, open Todoist in your web browser or desktop app. You can also use the desktop app’s global quick Ramble shortcut for faster access.

Ramble only works with an internet connection. Check if you’re online and try again.

Some regions (for example: Russia) may experience connection issues due to local internet provider limitations. Install and use a trusted VPN service to keep using Ramble.

There’s currently no option to turn off or disable Ramble, but you can choose not to use Ramble while using Todoist.

Speech recognition issues

Ramble catches a lot, but might struggle depending on speed, volume, and noise. We recommend speaking more slowly, closer to the mic, and minimizing background noise to improve recognition.

Ramble also works better with a list of things to do (“I want to plan a trip to Japan”), rather than a brainstorm or assistant request (“Can you please plan my trip to Japan?”).

Language detection issues

Ramble might misinterpret tasks dictated in your own language. To troubleshoot this, speak as clearly as possible. Go slower, enunciate, and see if results improve. If you’re still having issues, please share your feedback.

Microphone issues

Select Platform:

If you’re having issues with your microphone access, check your browser mic permissions:

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com.
  • Open the website settings. These are usually found on the left or right of the address bar.
  • Make sure to allow microphone access for Todoist.
  • Reload the web browser.
Check microphone permissions

If you’re having issues with your microphone access, make sure Todoist for macOS has access to your microphone:

  • Open System Settings.
  • Go to Privacy & Security.
  • Select Microphone.
  • Find Todoist in the list and make sure it’s enabled.
  • Reload Todoist for macOS.
Check system audio settings

Todoist uses your system audio to transcribe what you dictate. If you’re having audio issues, check the system audio settings:

  • Open System Settings.
  • Go to Sound. You’ll see your device’s system sound settings.
  • Check that output and input are properly set to the microphone you’re using.
  • Compare these settings with what’s used in your calls and make sure they match.
Check microphone permissions

If you’re having issues with your microphone access, make sure Todoist for Windows has access to your microphone:

  • Open System Settings.
  • Go to Privacy & Security.
  • Select Microphone.
  • Find Todoist in the list and make sure it’s enabled.
  • Reload Todoist for Windows.
Check system audio settings

Todoist uses your system audio to transcribe what you dictate. If you’re having audio issues, check the system audio settings:

  • Open Settings.
  • Open System and select Sound.
  • Check that input is properly set to the microphone you’re using.
  • Compare these settings with what’s used in your calls and make sure they match.
Check microphone permissions

If you’re having issues with your microphone access, make sure Todoist for Linux has access to your microphone:

  • Check your system’s privacy settings.
  • Allow microphone access for Todoist.
  • Restart Todoist for Linux.
Allow microphone permissions

If you installed Todoist for Linux using Snap, check if you’ve allowed Todoist to access your microphone. Open a terminal window and enter the following command: sudo snap connect todoist:audio-record

Check your microphone permissions

Make sure Todoist has permission to access your microphone:

  • Open the Settings app of your Apple device.
  • Scroll down and tap Apps.
  • Find and open Todoist.
  • Make sure Microphone is toggled on.
  • Switch to Todoist for iOS and use Ramble again.
Check your microphone permissions

Make sure Todoist has permission to access your microphone:

  • Open the Settings app of your Android device.
  • Tap Apps and choose to see all apps installed on your device.
  • Find and open Todoist.
  • Tap Permissions and select Microphone.
  • Select Allow only while using the app.
Check system microphone settings

It’s possible the microphone is blocked at the system-level on Android:

  • Open the Settings app of your Android device.
  • Tap Security & privacy and select Privacy controls.
  • Make sure the Microphone access option is toggled on.
  • Switch to Todoist for Android and use Ramble again. Note

These steps may differ depending on your Android device’s settings. If you’re not sure where the setting is located or if the interface is different, contact your device manufacturer.

Errors in Ramble

The connection to Ramble may have temporarily dropped and show an error. Wait a few seconds and try again. If the error persists, please share your feedback.

Introduction to Todoist Assist

Todoist Assist is our AI-powered suite of tools designed to work intelligently behind the scenes to enhance your productivity. By considering the specific context of your requests, Todoist Assist helps you automate task creation from emails and build complex filters using natural language. This allows you to focus more on your work and less on manual organization.

Play

Manage your privacy and data security

Todoist Assist uses tools powered by various, carefully selected large language models (LLMs), available through providers renowned for their high levels of security and privacy. Your information remains secure while it delivers intelligent productivity features.

  • Doist runs all AI functionality on secure infrastructure to ensure customer data stays protected within our environment.
  • We do not send your data directly to OpenAI. All processing flows through Doist’s secure infrastructure.
  • We work with AI providers that maintain strict data handling practices aligned with our privacy commitments. This includes models from top AI providers available via AWS Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI.
  • These providers have committed that data processed through their services will not be used to train their AI models.
  • You can control which features of Todoist Assist you want to use. In the future, we may introduce options that allow you to specify certain preferences that would be included with your interactions. This makes Todoist Assist more personalized to your needs. These preferences would be stored securely in your account, and only used to improve your direct experience with Todoist Assist.

Note

Some Todoist Assist features are available to all customers. Pro Legacy subscribers have access to Filter Assist only. Pro and Business subscribers have access to Filter Assist,Task Assist,and Email Assist. Check our pricing page for the most up-to-date information.

Todoist Assist supports your productivity

Todoist Assist works behind the scenes to help you achieve more without disrupting any of your existing workflows. Here are features that are built on Todoist Assist:

Email Assist

If you have a Todoist Pro or Business subscription, you can use Email Assist to automatically convert your forwarded emails. It will turn your email content – like due dates, notes, and more – into actionable Todoist tasks for all your projects.

To use Email Assist, go to the Advanced section of the General settings and turn it on. Then, start forwarding email to Todoist:

  • Open a project.
  • Click the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Email tasks to this project.
  • Click Copy email.
  • Forward your email to the unique email address. Pierre · Security Specialist

Email Assist is the only Todoist Assist feature that you can turn on or off for your account. All other features supported by Todoist Assist are optional. You can choose to use them or to ignore them completely.

Filter Assist

Filter Assist helps you create powerful filters without memorizing complex query syntax. Simply describe what you want to see in plain language, and Filter Assist will suggest the appropriate filter.

Note

Filter Assist is currently only available in English and Spanish.

To use Filter Assist:

  • Select Filters & Labels in the navigation menu.
  • Click the add icon next to Filters.
  • Click Try it in the Filter Assist banner at the top.
  • Describe which tasks you want to filter in the Filter request field.
  • Click Send.
  • Click Add filter.
Task Assist

Task Assist is a browser extension with several options to help you manage your tasks more effectively. It can suggest tasks to help you reach a goal, generate tips for completing a task, rewrite tasks to make them more actionable, and break complex tasks down into sub-tasks.

Note

Task Assist isn’t enabled in your Todoist account by default. To get started, set up the extension in Todoist on your web browser or the desktop apps.

Get in touch

Let Todoist Assist do the heavy lifting so you can focus on what matters. If you have any questions or would like to better understand how Todoist Assist operates, get in touch with us.
