Eisenhower Matrix with Todoist

The Eisenhower Matrix method used by US President Dwight D. Eisenhower is based on the task evaluation using the criteria important/unimportant and urgent/not urgent.

Play

This method visualizes tasks in an Eisenhower Decision Matrix (aka Eisenhower Box). The horizontal X-axis represents the level of urgency with the left side being the most urgent and the right side the least. The vertical Y-axis represents importance, with the lowest importance at the bottom, highest at the top. The result is four quadrants: Urgent and important, urgent but unimportant, important but not urgent, and unimportant and not urgent. You can place all your tasks within the boxes, giving you a clear understanding of what really needs to be done now and what can (and should) wait.

Set up an Eisenhower Matrix workflow in Todoist using labels

  • Create two labels: @important and @urgent.
  • Create four filters:
    • Urgent & Important with filter query: @urgent & @important
    • Important & Not urgent with filter query: @important & !@urgent
    • Urgent & Unimportant with filter query: @urgent & !@important
    • Unimportant & Not urgent with filter query: !@important & !@urgent
  • Add the appropriate labels to each new task:
    • Add @urgent & @important to tasks that need to be done immediately and personally
    • Add @important to tasks that have a date or a deadline and are done personally
    • Add @urgent to tasks that can be delegated
    • Don’t add either label to tasks that can be dropped
  • Take on important and urgent tasks first. Add a specific date to all your important but not urgent tasks. Delegate as many unimportant but urgent tasks as possible. Unimportant and not urgent tasks should be done last (or not at all).

Set up an Eisenhower Matrix workflow in Todoist using priorities

  • Create four filters:
    • Urgent & Important with filter query: P1
    • Important & Not urgent with filter query: P2
    • Urgent & Unimportant with filter query: P3
    • Unimportant & Not urgent with filter query: P4
  • Add the appropriate priorities to each new task:
    • Add P1 to tasks that need to be done immediately and personally
    • Add P2 to tasks that have a date or a deadline and are done personally
    • Add P3 to tasks that can be delegated
    • Add no priority (or P4) to tasks that can be dropped
  • Take on P1 tasks first. Add a specific date to all your P2 tasks. Delegate as many P3 tasks as possible. P4 tasks should be done last (or not at all).

Learn more

If you want to dive deeper to learn how to best decide which task to tackle first — and how to prioritize the rest — check out our Eisenhower Matrix productivity guide.

Get started with Todoist

New to Todoist? This guide walks you through the essentials for getting organized fast. Learn how to create a project, add tasks, set dates, break big goals into smaller steps, and prioritize your day. By the end, you’ll have everything you need to take control of your work and life.

Play

Start with a project

Todoist projects keep all your tasks organized so you can achieve your goals, both large and small.

Play

To create a project, select the + symbol next to My Projects in the navigation menu. Add your project’s name, pick a color, and choose to see it as a list, a board, or a calendar (available on the Pro or Business plan).

After setting up your project, you can decide how you’d want to use it:

  • Make a teaching plan
  • Track a marketing campaign
  • Share a grocery list Quick tip

Get started right away with a project template.

Add your first task

All projects begin with a single step, but don’t stop there. Add your tasks.

Play

Select Add task while in your new project. Write your task’s name. Then choose Add task.

Note

When you’re new to Todoist, the task name field shows example task names like “Fix bike tire this weekend” or “Read history chapter 5 in 10 days” to help you see how Todoist understands natural language. These examples stop appearing once you’ve completed 15 tasks.

The most achievable tasks tend to be:

  • Super specific and clear
  • Actionable
  • Less than an hour long

Stay on schedule

Todoist can auto-detect dates, nearly any way you write them.

Play

When you’re typing your task’s name, write out your task’s date, too.

Todoist understands things like:

  • Buy grapes today
  • Paint the deck this weekend
  • Edit marketing report Sept 15 at 2pm
  • Attend professional development class every 3rd Tues for 6 months starting in April Get the whole list of dates.

Split big tasks into sub-tasks

Small tasks are far easier to complete than big ones, so break large goals into manageable to-dos.

Play

Create a sub-task by selecting any task and choosing Add sub-task. Type your sub-task’s name and date, as usual.

Back in your project, you can use the arrow next to your main task to view or hide your sub-tasks.

Helpful hints:

  • Divide tough tasks into short, easy ones
  • Track all of your progress
  • Collapse for calm, expand to complete

Organize tasks into sections

Tidy up your long task lists with sections. You can neatly divide your project any way that works for you.

Play

Hover below your list of tasks and select the Add section line that appears.

Quick tip

  • Complete projects in stages
  • Try sections like To Do, Doing, Done. Here’s some section inspiration for you
  • Set a schedule by day, week, lunar cycle, whatever!

Add tasks to your Inbox

If you are not sure which project a new task should go in, add the task to your Inbox. This is the home for tasks without projects (yet), and the perfect way to get things out of your head.

Play

Find your Inbox at the top of the navigation menu. Any task that isn’t added to a specific project is added there by default.

Then, move tasks easily from your Inbox to projects. Select the task you’d like to move, and you’ll see the task view. Click Project on the right side, and choose the right project.

Plan your future

Find every task scheduled for today, this week, or any week in your Today and Upcoming views.

You’ll find both views below your Inbox in the navigation menu.

Play

  • Today view shows you all the tasks scheduled for today in all of your projects.
  • Upcoming view lets you see every task scheduled in the future.

Prioritize your day

It’s easy to get lost in your task list when there’s a lot on your plate. Keep your focus with color-coded priority levels.

To set priority levels, select a task. From your task view, use the flag icon to choose red priority 1, orange priority 2, blue priority 3, or white priority 4.

Your highest priority tasks will appear near the top of your Today and Upcoming views. That way, you know what to work on first.

Pro tips:

  • Pick only a few must-do tasks each day
  • Do your hardest task first
  • Reschedule any tasks you don’t check off

Set dates for big plans

Add a deadline to tasks with a firm deadline you need to plan ahead for. Deadlines are available on the Pro plan. The quickest way to add a deadline is to type it while you’re creating the task. Use curly brackets when you’re creating a new task to add a deadline. For example, typing {next Friday} will set the deadline for next Friday.

Quick tip

You can use dates to schedule when you plan to start working on a task. Use deadlines for tasks with a fixed, external deadline you can’t miss. For example, set a deadline for when your taxes are due and a date for when you plan to start. For recurring tasks, use a recurring date instead.

Complete your tasks

Small steps add up to big achievements over time. So take a moment to look back on all the progress you’ve made.

Play

Check things off your list by selecting the circle next to the task you have completed. You can uncomplete tasks, too.

To see every task you’ve checked off, click the three dots icon at the top of your project. Then, choose Completed tasks in the menu.

Todoist helps you:

  • Track your successes
  • Note the challenges
  • Reward yourself for a job well done! Quick tip

  • Downloads: With 10+ apps and plugins, Todoist is everywhere you are.
  • Templates: Tried-and-true (and totally editable) projects for work and life.

Getting Things Done (GTD) with Todoist

Getting Things Done (GTD) is a popular, five-step time-management method that’s based on the idea of getting everything out of your head and onto your to-do list. It reduces stress and forgetfulness by helping you focus on completing tasks rather than trying to remember them.

Play

Set up a GTD workflow with Todoist

Get up and running with GTD in Todoist by following these 5 steps:

  • Capture every task that comes to mind in your Todoist Inbox. Quickly type or dictate tasks as they occur to you using everyday language like “send invoice on May 3” or “water the plants every 4 days starting June 20 ending Sept 30.”
  • Clarify your captured tasks and make sure that they are actionable with concrete next steps. If not, delete them. If the task takes less than 2 minutes, do it right away (we suggest using a @two_minutes label for these tasks).
  • Organize your tasks from your Todoist Inbox into specific projects. Split complex tasks into more manageable action items using sub-tasks. Assign dates, deadlines, labels, and priority levels for even better organization.
  • Reflect on your progress often by reviewing your current, upcoming, and completed tasks to make sure you’re setting realistic dates and priority levels. Enable and review your Todoist Karma to determine your daily, weekly, and monthly productivity and adjust your workload as needed. Ensure you’re giving yourself time to complete tasks and clear your mind in between, as well.
  • Engage with your tasks by working on them! Be efficient by prioritizing tasks based on time available, your energy level, or a task’s urgent/low priority. Note

GTD and Getting Things Done are registered trademarks of David Allen & Co. Todoist is not affiliated with David Allen & Co. or Getting Things Done.

Learn more

How to collaborate with your team in Todoist

Once you’ve created a team in Todoist, you can start collaborating with others in a shared space. Team projects are accessible to everyone in your team by default, making it easy to share tasks and track progress. Use this guide to learn how to join projects, assign tasks, and keep everyone in sync. If you’re collaborating with a friend or family member instead, try sharing a personal project.

Just joined a team and not sure where to start? The Team Members - Find your way self-paced short course in the Todoist Toolkit is the fastest way to make Todoist work for you.

Create a team project

When you’re an admin or member of a team, you can create projects. Here’s how:

Select Platform:

  • Click the plus icon next to your team name.
  • Select Project.
  • Give your project a name and a description.
  • You can also customize your project with a color, access, folder, and layout.
  • Click Add to confirm. Note

Creating a team project from the workspace overview? Find those steps here.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Find your team name, and tap the plus icon next to it.
  • Select Add Project.
  • Give your project a name.
  • Tap Done to confirm.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Find your team name, and tap the plus icon.
  • Select Add project.
  • Give your project a name.
  • Tap the checkmark icon to confirm. Team projects are visible to everyone on the team by default. If you want to create projects that are visible to specific people, change the access of your project to Restricted. You can learn more in this article.

Join a team project

Quick tip

Tap the Projects I haven’t joined chip to get an overview of all projects you haven’t already joined.

Select Platform:

  • Click Invite. The number of people that can join a project depends on your team plan.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.

  • Tap the project.

  • Add people:

    • If you want to add your whole team, tap Everyone in [Team name].

  • Tap Invite to send the invitation. The number of people that can join a project depends on your team plan.

Accept project invites automatically

Accept project invites automatically from either people you’ve accepted invites from in the past, or members of your Todoist team:

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Click Settings.
  • Select the General tab.
  • Scroll down to the Advanced section.
  • Toggle Auto accept project invites on or off.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.
  • Select General.
  • Toggle Auto Accept Invites on or off.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.

  • Check or uncheck Auto accept invites to turn it on or off. If you’ve turned this option off, and a member sends a project invitation, a notification will appear in Todoist prompting you to accept it. There isn’t an option to decline an invitation. If you don’t want to join the project, leave the invitation unaccepted.

If you want to prevent project sharing with people that are outside of your team, change the person’s role to Guest.

Introduction to teams

Simplify and manage projects and tasks, no matter how small or large your team may be. Whether you’re collaborating across departments on an upcoming product launch, or you’re reducing the back-and-forth among your teammates, teams are built with the tools you need to organize shared work and keep track of everyone’s progress.

Play

Set up a team

Quick tip

Setting up Todoist for your team? The Set Up Your Team Workspace course in the Todoist Toolkit takes about 15 minutes and helps you build a workspace your team will feel comfortable in.

When you set up your team in Todoist, you’ll get one free team while on either the Beginner or Pro plans. Here’s how to get started in the web or desktop app:

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com.
  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Select Add a team.
  • Enter a team name. You’ll see a short form to share information about your team.
  • Select the most relevant answers in the form.
  • Choose between starting a free Business trial by clicking Continue to free trial, or setting up a free team by clicking start on the free plan.
  • Enter your teammates’ email addresses.
  • Click Add a team. When you upgrade a team to the Business plan, Todoist lets you create an additional free team.

Note

To set up, make changes to, join, leave, or delete a team in Todoist please open the web app or a desktop app. For now, these actions aren’t possible in the iOS or Android apps.

Edit a team

As you’re building your team, you realize you’ve got to add your company logo or get rid of that typo in your team name. To edit and make changes to your team:

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com.
  • Click your team name in the sidebar.
  • Click Settings at the top-right.
  • Make changes to your team, like adding your company logo or changing the team name.
  • Click Update to confirm.

Invite people to a team

Invite people to the team either by email or sharing an invite link:

Select Platform:

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com.
  • Click the team in the sidebar.
  • Click the Share icon at the top-right.
  • Use one of these two available options:
  • Invite by link: Copy an invite link and share with anyone to invite them to your team.
  • Invite by email: Enter the person’s email address, select their team role, and click Send invites. They’ll receive an email to join your team.
Invite a guest

If you’re inviting someone to the team without selecting their role, they will automatically be added as members (on the Business plan) or as admins (on the free team plan). If you’re inviting someone as a guest, follow these steps:

  • Log in to your Todoist account at todoist.com.
  • Click your team in the sidebar.
  • Click Settings at the top-right. You’ll see your team’s General settings right away.
  • Check if Prohibit external guests is turned off.
  • Open the project that you want to share with a guest.
  • Click the Share icon at the top-right.
  • Type the person’s email address.
  • Click the role menu and select Guest.
  • Click Invite. Once the person accepts the invitation, they’re automatically added to the team as a guest.

Invite people to the team through email:

  • Tap Browse and open the team project.
  • Tap the group icon.
  • Tap Invite via name or email and enter the person’s email address.
  • Select the desired team role.
  • Tap Done to confirm. When inviting someone to the team, they’ll automatically be added as members (on the Business plan) or as admins (on the free team plan). Learn more about each role here.

Invite people to the team through email:

  • Select the desired team role.
  • Tap the send icon to confirm. When inviting someone to the team, they will automatically be added as members (on the Business plan) or as admins (on the free team plan). Learn more about each role here.

If you received an invitation to join a team in Todoist, click the Join the team button in the email to confirm.

If you’re searching for the right team to join in Todoist:

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com.

  • Click Projects I haven’t joined at the top.
  • Find the project you’d like to join.
  • Click the three dots icon to the right of the project name.

Remove someone from a team

Admins are the only people who can remove someone from a team. If someone’s no longer part of your team, here’s how to remove them:

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com.
  • Open the team you would like to remove someone from.
  • Click the Members icon at the top-right.

Leave a team

If you’re no longer a member of a team, you’ve the option to leave the team in Todoist:

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com.
  • Click the team in the sidebar.
  • Click Settings at the top-right.
  • Click Leave team. Note

If you had your own Todoist Pro subscription before joining the team, it won’t be restored automatically when you leave, and your account returns to the Beginner plan. The unused time from that subscription is added to your account as credit, which is applied automatically when you upgrade to Pro again with a credit or debit card. Learn more in Cancel a Todoist subscription.

Delete a team

Warning

Admins are the only people who can delete a team.

If you’re an admin and you delete a team, it will immediately and permanently delete all your team data, including projects, tasks, comments, and files. This can’t be undone, and this action affects you and everyone else in the team.

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com.
  • Click the team you’d like to delete.
  • Click Settings in the top-right.
  • Click Delete team.

Best practices for teams

You’ve finally added every member to your team in Todoist. Here are some of our best practices to get started, so that everyone’s up to speed and on track with their work:

Use project or task comments to discuss with your team

Finding information can be tough when your company uses different communication channels. We recommend using project or task comments when exchanging ideas, giving updates or sharing feedback on the project.

Use filters to see just your team tasks

Create team filters that’ll show you just your team tasks, so you have a focused view of what your team has finished and what else needs to be done. Here are some examples for a team called “Doist”:

  • See what your teammates are working on this month: workspace: Doist & assigned to: others & due before: next month
  • Filter out everybody else’s tasks, so you can focus on your own: workspace: Doist & assigned to: me & next 7 days
  • Review all overdue team tasks: workspace: Doist & overdue
Add the Team tab to your navigation bar on iOS or Android

The Team tab gives you quick access to your team’s projects and tasks right from your navigation bar. Find out how to customize your Todoist navigation bar.

Install Todoist extensions that boost team productivity

Install nifty Todoist extensions to empower your team to brainstorm ideas or resolve issues with their work. Task Helper, for instance, lets you automate tasks that are part of your recurring processes. The Habit Tracker extension supports your team’s consistency by tracking how many days you’ve completed a recurring task. If you’re on the paid plans, you can install AI Assistant to utilize artificial intelligence to effectively break down your tasks, plan your projects, and more.

Invite or remove people from your Todoist team

Invite people to your Todoist team

Before jumping in, check if you’re an admin of the team. Then, learn how to invite people to your Todoist team:

Invite people by email

Select Platform:

  • Log in to your Todoist account on todoist.com.

  • Click your avatar at the top-left.

  • Select Settings.

  • Find the team you want to add users to in the sidebar.

  • Click People.

  • Click Invite by email.

  • Enter the email addresses of the users you’d like to invite and click Send invites.

  • Tap Browse and open the team project.

  • Tap the group icon.

  • Tap Invite via name or email and enter the person’s email address.

  • Select the desired team role.

  • Tap Done to confirm. To invite a person through a project:

  • Tap Browse and select the team.

  • Tap the project.

  • Tap the group icon.

  • Tap Invite via name or email and enter the person’s name or email address.

  • Select the desired team role.

  • Tap the send icon to confirm. To invite a person through the team settings:

  • Tap Browse and select the team.

  • Tap the add person icon.

  • Enter the person’s email address and tap the plus icon.

  • Tap Team role and select the desired role.

  • Tap Send invites. To share a link, tap Share invite link.

Invite people with an invite link

Select Platform:

  • Log in to your Todoist account on todoist.com.

  • Click your avatar at the top-left.

  • Select Settings.

  • Find the team you want to add people to in the sidebar.

  • Click People.

  • Make sure Enable invite link is toggled on.

  • Click Copy link. You can then send the URL to whomever you want to invite. After they click the link, they’ll have the ability to join your Todoist team.

  • Open Todoist for iOS and log in to your account.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-left.

  • Tap the team you want to add people to in the sidebar.

  • Tap the Add Person icon beside the team name.

  • Enter the person’s email address.

  • Tap Share Invite Link. The Apple share sheet will appear.

  • Choose how you’ll share the link with the person.

  • Open Todoist for Android and log in to your account.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-left.

  • Tap the team you want to add people to in the sidebar.

  • Tap the Add Person icon beside the team name.

  • Enter the person’s email address.

  • Tap Share Invite Link.

  • Choose how you’ll share the link with the person. When they tap the link, they’ll have the ability to join your Todoist team.

Remove people from your Todoist team

Make sure you only keep the right people in your Todoist team. First, check if you’re an admin. Then, learn how to remove people from the team:

  • Log in to your Todoist account on todoist.com.
  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Find the team you want to remove people from in the sidebar. Click People under the team name.
  • Find the person you want to remove and click their current role to the right of their name.
  • Select Remove from team.

Replace people in your Todoist team

If you want to replace someone, remove them first from your Todoist team. Then, invite the new person with their Todoist account email address.

Billing changes

If you decide to remove someone from your Todoist team, or if you want to replace an existing team member with someone else, we’ll automatically check if there’s any remaining time left on their subscription. Then, we’ll convert the value to an account balance for your Todoist team.

This balance will then be used to partially or completely cover your next invoice. None of the remaining time on their subscription will go to waste.

When your team size changes, a new invoice is generated for the proration. Invoices aren’t emailed, but team admins can view them anytime in the team’s billing settings.

Noteworthy

  • Tasks or task comments added by team members or guests aren’t impacted by the removal of their creator. For example, if you choose to remove a person from all shared projects, all tasks that were assigned to them will become unassigned.
  • When replacing a team member with someone new, you don’t need to manually change the previous team member’s email address. Todoist accounts aren’t designed to interchange between people, since they contain both personal and work-related tasks.

Keep your team aligned in Todoist

As teams grow, staying in sync gets harder. More projects, more people, more moving parts, and suddenly it’s not clear who’s doing what, whether things are on track, or where the bottlenecks are.

Todoist gives teams a clear picture of their work, right where it already lives. No check-ins, no status meetings, no extra overhead. This guide walks you through each of the visibility tools available, with links to dedicated articles where you can go deeper.

Quick tip

Rolling out Todoist to your team? The Run the Full Rollout course in the Todoist Toolkit covers launch day, the first two weeks, and what to do if momentum stalls.

Set up your team

Before you dive into the visibility tools, it’s worth making sure your workspace is set up to give everyone the right level of access.

Roles help you manage what people in your team have access to. There are three roles in a team: admin, member (Business plan only), and guest. When you create a team, you’re automatically set as the admin. You can also upgrade people in your team to admins.

Note

On the free team plan, everyone invited to the team is set as an admin. You can only change this by upgrading to Business.

Team projects are visible to everyone on the team by default, which means anyone can browse, preview, and join the projects relevant to their work without needing a direct invitation. This makes it easy for the whole team to stay aware of what’s happening across projects.

You can also set default access levels for your team so that new people automatically get the right permissions when they join.

Quick tip

If you want to create projects that are visible to specific people only, change the access of your project to Restricted.

Who did what, and when?

Reporting gives you a full record of your team’s activity across your team. It opens on your own completed tasks by default, but you can filter by workspace, project, person, event type, or date range to get the exact view you need.

Marco walks you through everything you can do in Reporting:

Play

Note

For the complete list of specific activities you’ll see, you can check out View Reporting in Todoist.

Is your project on track?

Insights gives you data-driven visibility into project health and how your team is progressing. See task completion trends, track overdue work, and spot patterns that help you course-correct before deadlines slip.

Denise takes you on a tour of Insights:

Play

Note

Insights is available on the Business plan. Team admins and members can view insights, while guests don’t have access.

See what everyone is working on

The People tab gives admins a full picture of what everyone on the team is working on. You can see each person’s assigned tasks and overdue count at a glance, sort by any column to quickly spot who might be stretched, and click into anyone’s task list (organized by project, priority, and due date) without having to ask.

Kaitlin takes you through the People tab:

Play

Note

The People tab is available to admins only.

Cut through the noise with team filters

When you need a focused view of exactly what your team is working on, team filters let you query across your entire workspace with precision. Create shared filters your whole team can use to find exactly what they’re looking for. Query by name, date, project, label, priority, and more to surface the tasks that need attention.

Dermot shows you how to create and use team filters:

Quick tip

Add a team filter to your Favorites for quick and easy access.

Manage team tasks in Todoist

You’ve just invited your team members to Todoist, and you’re ready to make progress on those long-standing project milestones. Learn and adopt these best practices to manage team tasks and collaboration in Todoist.

Kickstart teamwork with a few new projects

Choose one or two high-priority projects your team’s working on, and add these projects in your shared workspace. Start adding relevant tasks that come to mind, so your team members know what to work on soon as they open Todoist.

Quick tip

Don’t know where to start? Take a look at our gallery of pre-populated templates for teams.

Assign tasks to team members

Assign every single task in a project to a team member, so they know what they’re responsible for. In Todoist, you can only assign one person to a task, so there’s no doubt about who’s responsible for doing what.

Want to assign multiple people to the same task? Here are a couple of options:

  • If there are multiple steps to complete a task, break it down by adding sub-tasks. Then, assign each sub-task to a team member.
  • If several people need to complete the same task, duplicate the task and assign each copy to the responsible member.
  • Notify the relevant people in a task comment, so they’re fully aware of the status and progress of the work.

Sort or group tasks by Assignee

To get a clear picture of everyone’s workload, click Display at the top-right of the project and use either sorting or grouping options to see each person’s assignments.

Filter by assignee in team projects and custom filter views

In any team project you’re collaborating on, or in any custom filter view that contains team tasks, filter for tasks that are unassigned, assigned to you, or assigned to specific people:

Select Platform:

  • Click Display at the top-right.
  • Click Assignee in the Filter by section. Then, select:
    • No one to see tasks that aren’t assigned.
    • Only me to see tasks assigned to you.
    • Selected assignees to see tasks assigned to specific people. An Assignees menu will appear.
  • Click Choose assignees.
  • Select the names of people to see their assigned tasks.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Tap Display.
  • Tap Assignee in the Filter section. Then, select:
    • Anyone to see tasks assigned to anyone on the team.
    • No one to see tasks that aren’t assigned.
    • Only me to see tasks assigned to you.
    • Select assignees to see tasks assigned to specific people.
  • Tap Select assignees.
  • Tick the boxes next to people’s names to see their assigned tasks.
  • Tap Done.
  • Tap back to Display.
  • Tap Done to confirm.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Tap Display.
  • Tap Assignee in the Filtered By section. Then, select:
    • No one to see tasks that aren’t assigned.
    • Only me to see tasks assigned to you.
    • Selected assignees to see tasks assigned to specific people.
  • Tap Selected assignees.
  • Tick the boxes next to people’s names to see their assigned tasks.
  • Tap OK.
  • Tap Save to confirm.

Create team-specific filters

These filter recipes help you see what’s been assigned, giving you a clear picture of who’s working on what:

Filter query

What it shows

Helpful for…

assigned to: [Member name]

All tasks assigned to a specific teammate

Seeing one person’s workload across all projects

assigned to: others or !assigned to: me

All tasks assigned to anyone except you

Seeing what’s been delegated across the team

Workspace: [Team name] & assigned to: me & next 7 days

All tasks assigned to you in your team due this week

Planning your collaborative work for the week

Workspace: [Team name] & assigned by: me

All tasks you’ve assigned to anyone else on your team

Keeping track of progress on the things you’ve delegated

Workspace: [Team name] & overdue

All overdue tasks in your team

Spotting blockers and adjusting plans early

Workspace: [Team name] & assigned to: others & next 7 days

Tasks due this week for everyone else on the team

Spotting where the team has bandwidth to help

assigned to: [Member name] & due before: +4 weeks

A single teammate’s workload for the next four weeks

Checking a teammate’s load before assigning more

##[Folder name] & assigned to: me & due before: date

Your own tasks within a team folder by a given date

Focusing on your work in a team folder

Filter your team’s tasks

Let’s say you’re working with a team called Doist, and you’ve got a task that needs to be taken care of. You’ll want to know who may have the bandwidth to help out. You can try out this filter to see what’s on everybody’s plate in the next 7 days:

  • Tap the Add icon next to Filters.

  • Workspace: Doist & assigned to: others & next 7 days
  • Tap Done at the top-right to save your new filter.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Tap the Add icon next to Filters.
  • In the Name field, add a self-explanatory filter name. For example, Doist's upcoming tasks.
  • In the Query field, add the filter query:

To get an even better visualization of everybody’s tasks, customize your view by changing the project layout to board and group by Assignee.

If you’re on the Todoist Business plan, you’ve access to the calendar layout in Todoist. Apply the calendar layout to any of your team-specific filters, so you can get a bird’s eye view of your teammates’ deadlines. Switch between the Week to Month views, so you can see what’s due this week or what needs wrapping up before the month ends.

Schedule tasks with dates or deadlines

Play

Schedule dates or deadlines to tasks, so it’s easy to plan and prioritize work for the team. In the task name, write a date in natural language (for example: Write team update tomorrow) and the smart Quick Add will recognize, highlight, and add the date when you save the task. Natural language dates can also be as complex as every 3rd Thursday starting Aug 5 and ending April 10.

Quick tip

Check out more date examples you can use to schedule tasks.

If you’re tracking milestones, use deadlines to set when the task is due. This also reduces the risks of bottlenecks in a project.

For example, if you’re adding a task to submit the monthly finance report, select the date you intend to start working on the draft. Then, set a deadline for when the report is due for submission.

Add context in task descriptions

Use task descriptions to share links to documents and as many relevant details as you can. Instead of wasting time hunting down information, your teammates will be able to just get started. Descriptions stay organized at the top of your task view and are visible underneath the task in the project list.

Ask questions, share files, or share updates in task comments

Ask questions, attach important files, and provide status updates right inside your tasks as comments. Actionable information stays in context with the task itself, instead of having that information spread out across external messaging apps.

Don’t forget to notify your teammates to make sure they’re informed about a new comment or a file they may need to get work done.

Check and measure your team’s progress

Use Reporting to see all activity in a project, from changed dates to new comments added to tasks. This wealth of information helps you make informed decisions about what to adjust, remove, or focus on, so the project reaches the finish line without missing a deadline.

Move a personal project to your team

Sometimes you work on a personal project, only to later realize you need to work on the project with your team. When that happens, you can simply move your project from your personal projects to your team.

Warning

If you moved a personal project to your team by accident, learn how to move it back to My Projects.

Select Platform:

  • Click My Projects in the sidebar.
  • Hover your mouse over the project you wish to move.
  • Click the three dots icon that appears to the right of the project.
  • Click Project actions.
  • Select Move.
  • Select the Workspace you want to move your project to.
  • Select the Access and Folder.
  • Click Permanently move.
  • Confirm Permanently move.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open the project you wish to move.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Tap Project actions.
  • Select Move.
  • Tap Workspace.
  • Select the workspace you wish to move your project to.
  • Select the Access and Folder.
  • Tap Permanently Move.
  • Confirm Permanently Move.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open the project you wish to move.
  • Tap the three dots icon in the top-right.
  • Tap Project actions.
  • Select Move.
  • Tap Workspace.
  • Select the workspace you wish to move your project to.
  • Select the Access and Folder.
  • Tap Permanently Move.
  • Confirm Permanently Move.

Move a shared project

If you’re moving a project that has been shared with someone who isn’t a part of the team you are moving the project to, they’ll receive an invitation to join the project as a guest. They won’t have access to any other projects in the team unless they’re either added to those projects or invited to the team itself.

Move a parent project

If you move a parent project from your personal projects to a team, Todoist will create a folder where your parent project and its sub-projects will be added to. The folder will automatically have the same name as the parent project, which you can change afterwards.

All projects are on the same level in teams. This means that the projects you move to the team will no longer be nested as parent and sub-projects.

The organization of your folders and projects will appear the same to all of your team members. It is up to team admins how to sort team projects. This means you’ll all have the same reference point when talking about your folders and projects.

Get in touch

If you’re having trouble moving a personal project to your team, get in touch with us.

  • Move a shared project
  • Move a parent project
  • Get in touch

Move a team project to your personal projects

You just realized that a team project is better suited as a personal project. 🫢 If you’re a team admin, here’s how to move a project out of your team workspace and to your list of personal projects.

Select Platform:

  • Find your team name in the sidebar.
  • Click the team project.
  • Click the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Move.
  • Select Permanently Move in the workspace menu.
  • Confirm Permanently Move.
  • Tap a team project in the menu.
  • Tap the three dots icon in the top-right.
  • Select Move.
  • Tap Workspace.
  • Select My Projects.
  • Tap Done.
  • Tap Permanently Move to confirm.
  • Tap a team project in the menu.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Move.
  • Tap Workspace.
  • Select My Projects.
  • Tap the checkmark icon to confirm.
  • Tap Permanently move to confirm again. Note

Moving large projects may take some time to complete. When this happens, Todoist sends out a notification to let you know when the team project completes its journey to your My Projects workspace.

Limitations to moving team projects

Team projects contain valuable information that should be kept solely within the team. Here are several limitations to keep in mind before creating or moving team projects:

Move a project to a different team workspace

It’s not currently possible to move a project between team workspaces. This helps keep your project’s data safe, and ensures it stays with the team it was created for.

Move a team task to a personal project

It’s only possible to move an entire team project, along with all of its tasks, to your personal projects. Moving individual tasks out of a team project isn’t supported.

Non-admins: Move a team project

If you’re not a team admin, and you try to transfer a team project to your personal projects, you’ll see a notification to ask an admin to move the project for you.

The admin can move the project to their personal projects, subsequently share it with you, and then leave the project, if desired.

Plan your day with the Today view

The Today view in Todoist lets you start your day with focus by presenting every task scheduled for today across all your projects. By reviewing, time blocking, or rescheduling these tasks, you can create a realistic plan to tackle your goals and stay productive without feeling overwhelmed.

Note

Only tasks with a date appear in Today and Upcoming. A task added without a date won’t show up in either view. To find it, open its project directly or use a filter.

Set task priorities

What are the 3 most important tasks you need to complete today? Mark those as priority 1 so they’ll show up at the top of your Today view in red. Work on those first when you’re still fresh and energized.

Time block tasks

Time blocking takes the guesswork out of when you have to work on a specific task. Here’s how to do it in the calendar layout:

Select Platform:

  • Click Display at the top-right.
  • Select the calendar layout.
  • Click the Plan button at the top-right.
  • Drag a task to a specific hour in the calendar. This automatically creates a time slot for the task.
  • Hover your cursor at the bottom of the task until you see the down cursor.
  • Pull down to adjust the duration of the task. Touch and drag any all-day tasks into the calendar to time-block them into your schedule. This adds a time and duration to the task automatically.

Note

Interested in what you can achieve with the calendar layout? Check out our article to learn about its features and capabilities. This layout’s included in the Todoist Pro and Business plans.

Reschedule tasks

Have too many scheduled for the day? It’s overwhelming to see a list a mile long and know you can’t possibly get it all done. Keep your Today view focused and realistic by rescheduling some tasks for later in the week.

Sergio · Customer Success Specialist

If you do all your planning work in the morning, this would be a great time to clean up your Today view.

Apply Today view best practices

As you get the hang of planning your day regularly, the Today view becomes a great tool to create a routine that sets you up for success. Here are some tips and best practices to try:

Apply sorting or grouping options

If you’ve got quite a list for today, sort or group tasks based on criteria that make the most sense to you. Group by project or sort by dates – it’s that easy!

Use the Plan sidebar

Keep tasks from slipping through the cracks by checking the Plan sidebar in the calendar layout. You’ll see overdue, all-day, and time-blocked tasks you can review and manage in the calendar.

Postpone tasks that need more time

Give yourself permission to truly end your workday and start fresh tomorrow. Instead of letting overdue tasks snowball from one day to the next, postpone them to tomorrow or later in the week, so you can end every day at Todoist Zero. It’s not cheating – it’s about being flexible and rolling with the punches.

Quick tip

Postponing an overdue recurring task always moves it to tomorrow. Learn how to postpone or reschedule tasks in Todoist.

If you’re using the list layout, you can also drag your tasks to the bottom of the Today view to postpone them for tomorrow. Just make sure sorting and grouping options are turned off.

Build a habit

When you make a habit of organizing your Today view first, you’ll never waste time deciding what to work on next. After finishing a task, just open your Today view again, click the circle to mark it complete, and move on to the next item on the list.

Quick tip

If you’re excited to learn more about how to conquer your day, check out our Complete Guide to Planning Your Day!

Plan your week with the Upcoming view

The Upcoming view gives you a bird’s eye view of your week while letting you organize your upcoming tasks all in one place. Review your plans for days, weeks, or even months ahead – all up to two years!

Review your upcoming tasks

See every task scheduled for the next 7 days (and beyond) across all your projects.

Quick tip

If you’re a Todoist Pro or Business customer, you can display your tasks in a calendar layout, either by month or by week.

Select Platform:

  • Click Upcoming in the sidebar.
  • Scroll through the list to see tasks scheduled for any date in the future.
  • Click the left and right arrow buttons at the top-right to view a different week.
  • Click the Today button at the top-right to get back to today’s date.
  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap Upcoming.
  • Scroll down the list to see tasks scheduled for any date in the future.
  • Swipe right to left on the week picker at the top to display a different week.
  • Tap any day of the week to see the tasks scheduled for that day.
  • Tap the calendar icon at the top-left to get back to today’s date.
  • Tap the current month at the top-left to select a past or future date. You’ll see tasks scheduled for that day.
  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap Upcoming.
  • Scroll down the list to see the tasks scheduled for any date in the future.
  • Swipe right to left on the week picker at the top to display a different week.
  • Tap any day of the week to see the tasks scheduled for that day.
  • Tap the calendar icon at the top-left to get back to today’s date.
  • Tap the current month at the top-left to select a past or future date. You’ll see tasks scheduled for that day. Note

If you’re using the Todoist for Android widget or Todoist for WearOS, the Upcoming display only shows the next 7 days and doesn’t include the week picker at the top.

Schedule your tasks

Schedule dates in minutes, so you know exactly what’s coming up.

Select Platform:

Click Upcoming in the sidebar. Schedule a task based on your current layout:

  • List: Scroll down the task list or use the week picker at the top to jump to any date in the future. Then, click Add task to create a task for that selected day.
  • Board: Scroll through the day columns or use the week picker at the top to jump to any date in the future. Then, click Add task at the bottom of the selected day column to create a task.
  • Calendar (paid): Click the Plan button button to open the Plan sidebar. Drag a task to a date in the calendar to schedule it. Expand or shorten the task to add a duration.
  • Note
  • The Plan sidebar shows overdue, all-day, time-blocked, and unscheduled tasks with a deadline (up to 7 days ahead). Click any task or drag and drop it into the calendar to reschedule it.
  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap Upcoming.
  • Scroll down the task list or use the week picker at the top to go to any date in the future.
  • Drag the Dynamic Add button from the bottom-right to the day where you’d like to create and schedule a new task.
  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap Upcoming.
  • Scroll down the task list or use the week picker at the top to go to any date in the future.
  • Drag the Dynamic Add Button from the bottom-right to the day when you would like to create and schedule a new task.
  • Quick tip
  • Touch and hold any date in the week picker to quickly add a task to that day. Evert · Head of Customer Experience

With the Calendar integration, you can time block tasks around your Google Calendar events, so you can easily manage your workload for the week. This way, you can create a weekly plan you can commit to.

Reschedule your tasks

Reschedule tasks to free up fully booked days in the week. In Todoist, drag a task across the Upcoming view and to its new date. This ensures your schedule is manageable and doable.

Select Platform:

Existing tasks: Drag the task to its new date or hover your cursor over the task. Click the scheduler icon and pick a new date.

Overdue tasks: Click Reschedule at the top-right.

Quick tip

If you use the calendar layout, you can also drag tasks from the Plan sidebar to reschedule your overdue, all-day, or time-blocked tasks.

Existing tasks: Drag the task to its new date, or open the scheduler to choose a new date.

Overdue tasks: Tap Reschedule at the top-right.

Quick tip

A “busy” dot icon under a date in the scheduler indicates that you have one or more tasks scheduled on that day. Dates without the dot indicator are free of tasks.

Existing tasks: Drag the task to its new date, or open the scheduler to choose a new date.

Overdue tasks: Tap Reschedule at the top-right.

Quick tip

A “busy” dot icon under a date in the scheduler indicates that you have one or more tasks scheduled on that day. Dates without the dot indicator are free of tasks.

Show or hide future occurrences

If you’ve subscribed to Todoist Pro or Business, you’ll have access to the calendar layout in the Upcoming view. From there, choose whether you want to see or hide all future occurrences of your recurring tasks in the calendar.

On web or desktop, click Display in the top-right. Then, turn Future occurrences on or off. This option is not currently available on the mobile apps.

Note

If the list or board layout is applied to the project, you’ll only see the next recurrence of the task.

Best practices for the Upcoming view

As you get the hang of planning your week in advance, the Upcoming view becomes a great tool for looking back at what you’ve achieved, and proactively scheduling tasks for the following week. Here are some tips and best practices to try:

Time block tasks

Schedule time slots in your day to complete important tasks in Todoist. If you’ve subscribed to Todoist Pro or Business, you can apply the calendar layout and quickly drag the task into the calendar to time block. This adds a time and duration to the task, making it easy to visualize and create a plan you can stick to. You can also color tasks by priority, label, or project to tell different kinds of work apart at a glance.

Postpone tasks that need more time

If a task needs more time to complete, postpone it to next week using the Postpone option in the task scheduler.

Select Platform:

If you’ve subscribed to Todoist Pro or Business, and you’re using the calendar layout on the Todoist web or desktop apps, you’ll find a list of your overdue tasks in the Plan sidebar, so you can easily reschedule to a future date.

Review upcoming appointments

It’s nice to get a sense of which appointments are coming up, so you can plan your week accordingly. This is especially useful if you’ve set up your calendar to sync with Todoist.

Add a date and time to any tasks that are time-sensitive. If you’re on the paid plan, add additional reminders to make sure you don’t forget them.

Create a recurring task for weekly reviews

Do you prefer reviewing your progress on Friday evenings, or planning for upcoming work on Sunday mornings? Create a recurring weekly task to “Plan for the week”, so it becomes a part of your schedule.

Pomodoro with Todoist

The Pomodoro Technique developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s uses a timer to break down work into 25-minute intervals separated by 5-minute breaks. Each of these intervals is called a “pomodoro” (after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer originally used to track them). After you’ve completed four sprints, take a longer break (15-30 minutes) to refresh for your next series of sprints.

Play

Set up a Pomodoro workflow in Todoist

  • Create a “Pomodoro” project in Todoist and within it create 8-10 recurring Pomodoros (1st Pomodoro, 2nd, 3rd, etc.).
  • In your Today view, arrange all your daily tasks underneath each Pomodoro. Estimate how long each task would take to complete. If a task takes more than 30 minutes, break it up into smaller sub-tasks.
  • When you start working on a Pomodoro, set a timer (traditionally to 25 min.). After completing each pomodoro, mark it as done and take a short break (3-5 min.). Once you complete four pomodoros, take a longer break (15-30 min.) to refresh for your next session. Sergio · Customer Success Specialist

Try one of the Pomodoro-optimized time management apps that integrate with Todoist, such as Toggl Track.

Learn more

If you want to learn more about how to beat procrastination with this productivity method, check out our detailed Pomodoro Technique productivity guide. It goes into the history of the technique, the three rules for maximum productivity, quick tips, and more!

See what your team is working on with the People Tab

The People Tab gives you a bird’s-eye view of everyone’s workload – all in one place, without digging through individual projects.

See who’s assigned what, spot overdue tasks at a glance, and get the context you need to keep work moving as a team.

Note

The People Tab is currently available only for admins.

How to access

The People Tab lives right in your team workspace overview, next to the Projects tab.

  • Click your team name in the left sidebar.
  • At the top of the workspace, click the People Tab. That’s it – you’ll see a list of everyone on your team along with their current tasks.

What’s included in the People Tab

  • Name: The name and avatar of each person on your team.
  • Role: Each person’s role – Admin, Member, or Guest. Roles determine what each person can access in the team workspace. Learn more about team roles. Quick tip

You can invite new people to your team directly from this view by clicking the Invite button in the top right.

  • Assigned: The total number of tasks currently assigned to this person across all team projects. It’s a quick way to gauge who’s carrying a heavy load and who might have more capacity. Click the Assigned task value to open a detailed view of assigned tasks grouped by projects.
  • Overdue: The number of tasks that are past their due date. Use this column to catch bottlenecks early and check in with teammates who may need support. Click the Overdue task value to open a detailed view of overdue tasks grouped by project.

Assigned and Overdue views

After you click into the Assigned or Overdue task volumes for a person from the People Tab, you’ll be taken to a detailed view. From here, you’ll see all current tasks assigned to that person organized by project (column headers). Tasks within each project are automatically sorted by priority, then date.

If you share a project with that person, you’ll be able to edit the tasks that you see in these detailed views. If you don’t, you won’t be able to edit the tasks, but you can comment on them to ask questions, provide feedback, or request more information.

Given the detailed and interactive nature of the Assigned and Overdue views, we recommend using this view as the backdrop for 1-on-1 conversations with your team.

Note

In the Assigned and Overdue columns, you’ll see each person’s tasks from projects that you share with them or projects with public access that you haven’t joined yet (view-only). You won’t be able to see someone’s tasks from private projects or projects with restricted access if they are not shared with you.

How to sort and search in the People Tab

To find a specific person in the list, start typing their name or email address using the Search people icon in the top-right corner of the tab.

To sort the list by name, role, or the number of assigned or overdue tasks, click the respective column title. Click one more time to reverse the order.

People sidebar

To look at each person’s list of tasks or the projects they’re working on in more detail, simply click their name in the tab. A sidebar will appear on the right showing their assigned and overdue tasks, and the projects they’re actively working on (at least 1 task is currently assigned to them).

Team roles and access

Roles help you manage what people in your team have access to. There are three roles in a team: admin, member (a role available on the Business plan), and guest.

Play

Admin

When you create a team, you’re automatically set as the admin. You can also upgrade team members to admins. On the free team plan, everyone invited to the team is set as an admin by default, you can only change this by upgrading to Business.

As an admin, you’ll have full access and control over the team, and can:

  • ✅ Browse, preview, and join any visible projects in the team
  • ✅ Create new projects in the team
  • ✅ Invite or remove people from the team
  • ✅ Update roles for people in the team
  • ✅ Manage guests
  • ✅ Update the team-wide settings
  • ✅ Delete the team permanently
  • ✅ Manage team billing
  • ✅ Have ownership over the data added to the team workspace
Admin-exclusive features

As an admin, you have exclusive access to the following features:

  • Log in to your Todoist account at todoist.com.

  • Click your team name on the sidebar.

  • Click Members at the top-right. A list of team members will appear.

  • Find the person you want to turn into an admin.

  • Click the role next to their name. A menu with a list of roles will appear.

  • Select Admin.

  • Log in to your Todoist account at todoist.com.

  • Click your team name on the sidebar.

  • Click Members at the top-right. A list of team members will appear.

  • Find the person who you want to change their role.

  • Click the role next to their name. You’ll see a menu with a list of roles.

  • Select their new role. The Member role can’t be changed to the Guest role because members are part of the whole team, while guests have access only to specific projects. To switch from Member to Guest, remove the member from the team. Then, invite them to specific projects as a guest.

  • Log in to your Todoist account at todoist.com.

  • Click your team name on the sidebar.

  • Click Members at the top-right. A list of team members will appear.

  • Find the person you wish to remove.

  • Click the role next to their name. A menu with a list of roles will appear.

  • Select Remove from team. Select who can edit newly created projects in your team. You can choose between giving your whole team access to new projects by default, or you can set the default access level to restricted.

  • Log in to your Todoist account at todoist.com.

  • Click your team on the sidebar.

  • Click Settings at the top-right.

  • Click the Access menu below the Default access level section.

  • Select between two access levels:

    • Restricted: Only invited collaborators can edit new projects.
    • Team: Everyone in your team can edit new projects.

  • Click Update to confirm. Default collaborators are automatically added to any new project created in your team. Here’s how to select people as default collaborators:

  • Log in to your Todoist account at todoist.com.

  • Click your team on the sidebar.

  • Select Settings at the top-right.

  • Click the Default collaborators field below the Default access level section.

  • Add any team member you want to assign as a default collaborator. Manage guest access from the Members settings. You can upgrade a guest to a member, or remove them from projects in your team.

Guest access is turned on by default, but you can turn it off:

  • Click your team in the sidebar.
  • Click Settings at the top-right.
  • Turn Prohibit external guests on.

Member

As a member, you can collaborate with the whole team, but your access to high-level settings is limited:

  • ✅ Browse, preview, and join any visible projects in the team
  • ✅ Create new projects in the team
  • ✅ Invite people to the team
  • ❌ Remove people from the team
  • ❌ Update roles for other people in the team
  • ❌ Manage guests
  • ❌ Update the team-wide settings
  • ❌ Delete the team permanently
  • ❌ Manage team billing
  • ❌ Have ownership over the data added to the team workspace Note

The member role is only available on the Business plan. On the free team plan, anyone invited to the team is automatically set as an admin.

Guest

A guest is a person outside the team who’s invited to a specific project. Guests are free of charge and won’t appear on the invoice.

As a guest, you’ll only have access to the projects you’re invited to, and can’t do any of the following:

  • ❌ Browse, preview, and join any visible projects in the team
  • ❌ Create new projects in the team
  • ❌ Invite or remove people from the team
  • ❌ Update roles for other people in the team
  • ❌ Manage other guests
  • ❌ Update the team-wide settings
  • ❌ Delete the team permanently
  • ❌ Manage team billing
  • ❌ Have ownership over the data added to the team workspace Note

Guests don’t inherit the team’s Business plan, so paid features like deadlines aren’t available to them, even within the projects they’ve been invited to.

Time blocking in Todoist

Plan and time-block tasks with ease in Todoist. When you know what’s up next and what to reschedule, you can tackle high-priority work without letting crucial information slip through the cracks.

Select the calendar layout

Let’s get started by selecting either the day or week calendar layout in Todoist:

Time block in the day calendar

Play

If you’re using the Today view:

Select Platform:

  • Log in to the Todoist web app or the desktop apps.

  • Open the Today view.

  • Click the layout button at the top-right.

  • Select Calendar. The day calendar will display all-day tasks and calendar events at the top. Calendar events and tasks with a date, time, and duration will appear in their designated time slots below.

  • Tap Today in the tab bar.

  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.

  • Tap View at the top-right.

  • Select Calendar. The day calendar will display all-day tasks and calendar events at the top. Calendar events and tasks with a date, time, and duration will appear in their designated time slots below.

  • Tap Today in the navigation bar.

  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.

  • Tap View at the top-right.

  • Select Calendar. The day calendar will display all-day tasks and calendar events at the top. Calendar events and tasks with a date, time, and duration will appear in their designated time slots below.

Time block in the week calendar

Play

If you’re using the Upcoming view:

Select Platform:

  • Log in to the Todoist web app or the desktop apps.
  • Open the Upcoming view.
  • Click the layout button at the top-right.
  • Select Calendar.
  • Select the Week layout. You’ll see all your events and tasks for the week. The week calendar will display all-day tasks and calendar events at the top. Calendar events and tasks with dates, time, and duration will appear in their designated time slots below.

The week calendar layout shows three rolling days (seven days in landscape mode) where you can manage scheduled events and tasks. Here’s how to turn it on in Todoist:

  • Tap Upcoming in the tab bar.

  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.

  • Select View.

  • Select Week.

  • Tap Done. You’ll see all your events and tasks for the week. The 3-day/week calendar layout shows three rolling days in portrait mode or seven rolling days in landscape mode. Here’s how to turn it on in Todoist:

  • Tap Upcoming in the tab bar.

  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.

  • Select View.

  • Select 3-day or Week (depending on device orientation).

  • Tap Save. You’ll see all your events and tasks for the week. Quick tip

Need to add or manage tasks after the current week? The week calendar lets you see scheduled tasks up to two years in the future.

Time-block a task

To start time-blocking, add a date, time, and duration to your task. It’s easiest to drag the task to the correct day and time, but you can also manually edit the task’s Date field.

Drag to the calendar

When dragging an all-day task to your schedule, Todoist automatically adds the date, time, and a 30-minute duration to the task. If you’re creating a brand new task, click the time slot in the calendar. This opens Quick Add with a 30-minute duration added automatically to the task.

Use natural language

You can also time block using Quick Add’s natural language input. Enter the task’s date, time, and duration using natural language. It can be something as simple as tomorrow at 10:00 AM for 25 minutes or as complex as next Friday 2:00 PM for 90 minutes.

Change the task date

If you prefer to change the task date manually, click the Date field in the task view to open the task scheduler. Then, select a day or date on the mini calendar, or add a time and duration in the Time field.

Adjust the duration

The default task duration of 30 minutes isn’t enough to write a solid monthly report for your board meeting or finish a noteworthy thesis paper. Adjust the duration by clicking the edge of a task and dragging it downwards in the calendar. If you’ve synced your calendar app to Todoist, it’ll sync and display the same duration.

Sync tasks and events

Stay on top of your schedule by setting up the Calendar integration and syncing Todoist to your go-to calendar app.

Sync tasks to your calendar app

Once the integration’s up and running, you’ll see a “Todoist” calendar in your calendar app. Your all-day tasks are at the top, while scheduled tasks are in their designated time slots. You’ll always know what’s coming up, even if you aren’t actively using Todoist.

Sync events to Todoist

Events you’ve already scheduled in your calendar appear in Todoist in the colors they use in your calendar app. This helps prevent overlapping tasks with events or appointments. Your tasks are colored separately, by priority, label, or project. Learn how to color tasks in the calendar layout.

Sergio · Customer Experience Specialist

Learn how to use time-blocking to do weekly reviews!

Plan for unscheduled or backlogged tasks

Not sure what to tackle this week? Open the Upcoming view and click the Plan sidebar on the right side. You’ll see all of a project’s overdue tasks, all-day tasks, and tasks that only have deadlines. When you drop any of these tasks into the calendar, Todoist automatically adds the date, time, and duration to it.

Add any new tasks to the calendar

Did an idea strike you while you were at a 3 PM meeting? Open the day or week calendar and click a time slot. Quick Add opens automatically with the date, time, and automatic reminder pre-populated for you.

Bonus: Start a weekly review

Set aside one dedicated hour to review what you’ve accomplished at the end of the week, so you can hone in on what to focus on the following week. It’s a great way to tackle each week with clarity and intention.
