Todoist glossary

New to Todoist or need a quick refresh? This guide brings together the features, terms, and concepts that matter most, with simple explanations to help you get the most out of Todoist.

Note

Please note that certain features may not be available in all Todoist pricing tiers or plans.

Jump to: What is Todoist? · Add and manage tasks · Organize your work · View your work · Collaborate · Teams · Power features · Plans and programs · Mobile · Your Account

What is Todoist?

Todoist is a to-do list and task manager that helps you organize your work and life in one place. Capture tasks on any device, group them into projects, schedule them with dates, deadlines, or reminders, and share them with teammates, friends, or family when you need to.

Tasks

An item on a list. Tasks represent individual actions or to-dos you need to complete. You’ll find out how to add, edit, duplicate, move, complete, uncomplete, or delete a task in Introduction to tasks.

Projects

A list of tasks organized together. Projects help you group related work by area of focus or goal. You can learn all about projects in our help center article, Introduction to projects.

Note

You can create personal projects or team projects.

Inbox

Default place for ideas or tasks until they’re added to a project. Consider the Inbox as a quick capture space for any task that comes to mind before sorting and organizing them into their respective projects.

Home view

Main page to begin Todoist. Your starting point when you open the app. You’re able to change your home view in a few quick steps.

Add and manage tasks

Quick Add

Used to add a task rapidly. Quick Add opens a floating task entry field, so you can capture and schedule tasks quickly from anywhere in Todoist. Attach files and assign task attributes, like labels or priority, without leaving Quick Add. Start using Task Quick Add or customize Quick Add in Todoist.

Smart date recognition

Used to recognize, highlight, and add dates in task names. Also called natural language date parsing, this feature lets you type dates conversationally like “tomorrow at 3 PM.” You can turn smart date recognition on or off.

Date

The field in Todoist where you can schedule when a task should happen. Can include both the calendar date and a time. Here’s how to add a date to your task.

Deadline

The latest day by which a task must be completed. A deadline creates urgency tracking, and is different from a date (which is when you plan to work on something).

Duration

An estimate of how long a task will take to complete. Requires a date and time to be set before it can be added. The maximum duration is 24 hours.

Recurring

Tasks that happen more than once. You can set tasks to recur daily, weekly, monthly, or on a custom schedule. Find out more about recurring dates.

Priority

Rank of importance for tasks. Priority levels are p1 through p4, with p1 being the highest priority. Get started by setting a priority to a task.

Description

Additional text under the task name. Task descriptions provide details about what needs to be done and can include formatted text, links, and attachments. Give it a try, and add a task description in Todoist.

Reminders

Used to remind yourself or teammates about a task. Reminders alert you at a specific time to help ensure you don’t miss important deadlines. Todoist offers several types of reminders:

Automatic reminders: A reminder that’s added by default whenever a date and time is scheduled to a task, based on your Reminders settings

Custom reminders: A reminder based on a specific date and time, or the amount of time before a task is due

Recurring reminders: A reminder that notifies you on a recurring basis (for example: ev Tuesday 7:00)

Location reminders: A reminder that notifies you when you’ve arrived at a specific location. Learn more about location reminders

Complete/uncomplete

To check off or reopen a task. Completed tasks are marked as done and move out of your active lists. Here’s how to complete a task, and this is how to uncomplete one.

Schedule/reschedule/unschedule

To add a date, change a date, or delete a date from a task.

Postpone

To shift or adjust a task to the next occurrence.

Duplicate

To create a copy of a task. If you want to reuse the details of a task, you can save time and effort by duplicating the task and any of its active sub-tasks.

Move

To relocate tasks or projects to different locations within Todoist. For example, you can move a personal project to your team, or move a team project to your personal projects. You can also move a task.

Organize your work

Sections

Used to split projects into parts. Sections help you organize tasks within a project into logical groups by status, priority, or phase. Get the steps in Introduction to sections.

Sub-tasks

Tasks nested under a parent task. Sub-tasks help you break down complex work into smaller, actionable steps. You’re able to turn an existing task into a sub-task, or a sub-task into a parent task. Find out more about sub-tasks and the best practices in Introduction to sub-tasks.

Sub-projects

Projects nested under a parent project. Sub-projects help you organize related work hierarchically. For example, you might create “parent” projects called “Home” and “Health” and then organize various sub-projects underneath each one.

Note

Sub-projects are only available for personal projects. Use folders in your team.

Labels

Tags that help batch similar tasks together. Labels let you categorize and find related tasks across different projects. Examples include @email, @waiting, or @quick. Take a look at Introduction to labels for more ideas, or how to add, edit, and delete a label.

Filters

Saved task searches. Filters let you create custom views that display tasks matching specific criteria using queries to search across all your projects. This helps you narrow down your lists according to task name, date, project, label, priority, date created, and more. Check out our Introduction to filters to find out how.

Favorites

Used to highlight your important items in the navigation menu. Here’s how to add a project, label, or filter to favorites in Todoist.

Template

Set of ready-to-use tasks, sections, and dates what you can use or re-use in any new project. If you’re working with others in a shared project, you can create a template where tasks are already assigned to a specific person.

Sort

To arrange items by characteristics. Sorting options let you organize tasks by name, date, date added, deadline, priority, manually, or others. You can sort or group your tasks in Todoist.

Group

To collect tasks with the same attribute into separate sections. Grouping options let you organize tasks by date, date added, deadline, priority, or label. Find out how to group your tasks in Todoist.

Archive/unarchive

To move a project out of or into an active project list. Archived projects are preserved for future reference and can be restored at any time. You can also archive or unarchive a section.

View your work

Display

A menu of display options to apply to your project. Apply or reset any sorting options, grouping options, or layout changes to your Todoist project or view. The Display icon is located at the top-right of any project or view.

List layout

View of a project as a list. The traditional format for viewing tasks. If you prefer a straightforward list, you can use the list layout in Todoist.

Board layout

View of projects in column form. Board layout displays tasks in a Kanban-style format with columns.

Calendar layout

View of a project, label, filter, Today, or Upcoming as a calendar. Calendar layout displays your tasks by date.

Task view

Detailed view of all information associated with a task. Find out how to use the task view to manage tasks in Todoist.

Today view

View of all tasks with dates scheduled for today. Today view helps you focus on what needs to be done right now.

Upcoming view

View of all tasks with dates. Upcoming view displays your tasks organized by date over the coming days and weeks. Go ahead and plan your week with the upcoming view.

Productivity view

View for goals, Karma, and completed tasks. Check out how to use the Productivity view in Todoist.

My Projects

The section of your sidebar containing your personal projects. This is where you organize tasks for individual use or collaboration with friends and family.

Search

The search bar is a field to enter keywords or search queries in order to find items. You can pull up specific tasks, projects, filters, labels, and comments. Find out how to search in Todoist.

Collapse/expand

To hide or view content (tasks, sub-tasks, sub-projects) with an arrow.

Drag and drop

To move an item by clicking and dragging it to a new location.

Three dots menu

The menu that appears when you tap or click the three dots icon. Used to find more options.

Multi-select toolbar

A toolbar that appears at the bottom of the web or desktop app when selecting multiple tasks.

Collaborate

Personal projects

Projects you create for your own use or for collaborating with friends and family. Examples include household chores, family vacations, and party planning. Personal projects appear in the My Projects section of your sidebar.

Note

You may see “personal workspace” in older content. This has been replaced by “personal projects” or “My Projects”.

Share

To invite people to a project. You can share both personal projects (with friends and family) and team projects (with teammates and guests).

Here’s how to decide between casual or work collaboration in Todoist.

Assign

To delegate a task to a specific person. In shared projects, you can assign tasks to yourself or others to clarify ownership and responsibility.

Note

You can only assign a single person to a task in Todoist. We believe in the concept of having a Direct Responsible Individual, which ensures that a single person is always clearly responsible for any given task.

Comments

Text attached to tasks or projects. Comments let you add context and files, collaborate with others, or track progress.

Reporting

A history of edits and updates to tasks and projects. Information is organized by date and filtered by project, person, or event type. Here is how to view Reporting in Todoist.

Notifications

A gentle reminder about something new. Notifications inform you about task assignments, comments, reminders, and other updates. You can choose which notifications you receive from Todoist.

Teams

Team

A group of people collaborating on work-related projects in Todoist. Each team has its own shared space with projects, templates, admin controls, and one central bill.

Team workspace

The team workspace is the overview area where members can browse, preview, and join team projects. It shows all team projects in one place, along with team templates and activity summaries.

Team projects

Projects created within a team for collaborating with teammates on work-related tasks. Examples could include meeting agendas, employee onboarding, product roadmaps, and client work. Team projects appear in your team section of the sidebar.

Folders

A way to group related team projects together in a team workspace. Folders help teams organize projects by department, client, or initiative. They serve a similar purpose to sub-projects, but are designed for team collaboration rather than personal use.

Admins

People with an admin role who can manage team settings, delete the team, and manage other people in the team.

Members

People with a member role who have full access to all data within the team but don’t have the permissions to manage team settings, delete the team, or manage other people in the team.

Guests

People outside of your organization that you want to collaborate with on select team projects. Guests have limited access and can only see the specific projects they’re invited to.

People

An overarching term for everyone in a team, regardless of their role (admin, member, or guest).

Power features

Ramble

Ramble is a voice-to-tasks feature in Todoist that lets you quickly add tasks using your voice.

Todoist Assist

A set of AI-powered features in Todoist that helps you work more efficiently by offering smart suggestions and automating tasks, including tools like Email Assist, which turns forwarded emails into tasks, and Filter Assist, which helps you create filters using natural language.

Karma

A productivity scoring system designed to help you build habits and stay motivated. Karma tracks your progress and celebrates your wins as you complete tasks, hit your daily goals, and maintain your streaks. Karma levels span from Beginner all the way to Enlightened.

Streaks

A consecutive series of days achieving your daily task goals. Streaks are tracked in your Karma and Productivity view to help maintain momentum.

Vacation mode

Used to pause Karma points and maintain streaks when you’re away. You can turn on or off vacation mode in Todoist.

Week start

Begin your week on this day in the Upcoming view or the Calendar layout of a project. Select your preferred week start in Settings > General.

Time block

A scheduled period of time dedicated to specific tasks or activities. Learn more about time blocking in Todoist.

Integrations

Connections between Todoist and other apps and tools you use. Browse all available integrations in the Todoist integrations gallery.

Keyboard shortcuts

Combination of keystrokes used to perform a task quickly without using your mouse. Find out how to use keyboard shortcuts in Todoist.

Markdown

Used to add formatting elements to text.

Emoji

Small digital icons used to visually represent emotions, objects, ideas, or actions in text. Emoji can be added to comments and anything you can name: tasks, sections, projects, labels, and filters.

Theme

You’re able to change color themes to personalize the look and feel of your Todoist app.

Avatar

Profile picture associated with your Todoist account. You can change or remove your avatar photo.

Plans and programs

Plan

The specific features and pricing tiers Todoist offers, such as Beginner, Pro, or Business, detailing what you receive at each level. Choose your path to productivity by comparing the plans.

Beginner plan

Free plan for solo users.

Pro plan

Paid plan for individuals. The Pro plan unlocks advanced features and increased usage limits. When you’re ready to upgrade, you can get started with Todoist Pro.

Business plan

Paid plan for teams. The Business plan includes all Pro features for every person in your team, plus team-specific features like the team workspace, permissions, central billing, and collaborative tools. Get started with Todoist Business today.

Beta features

Features that are in the final stages of development and testing. Beta features may appear in your Todoist without requiring opt-in and can be used immediately if visible. They may change or be discontinued based on feedback and real-world usage.

Experimental features

Early-stage features that explore new ideas and require opt-in through your Todoist settings. Experimental features are available for early testing and feedback, may be less stable than officially released features, and can change significantly or be discontinued based on what is learned during development.

Experimentalists

People who have joined the pre-production testing group. To subscribe or unsubscribe, you can follow the steps here.

Backups

An archive of Todoist tasks, dates, time, deadlines, projects, comments, and file attachments recorded in the .csv file format. Up to 21 backups are created every time you log in and make changes to your tasks and projects.

Reload

Use the Reload button to clear local data and resolve sync-related issues in the Todoist web or desktop apps. Make sure to create or download a backup of your data beforehand.

Todoist Partner Program

Programs that reward content creators, publishers, coaches, and other productivity-focused partners for introducing Todoist to new users. These programs support different types of partners in promoting Todoist and growing alongside the platform. Find out more, or apply to become a Todoist partner here.

Mobile

Navigation bar

Used to quickly access the views you use most often in Todoist. Here’s how to customize the Todoist navigation bar.

Dynamic Add button

Button used on mobile to add tasks, sub-tasks, and sections in specific views by touching and dragging it in place. This is how to use the Dynamic Add button in Todoist on mobile devices.

Context menu

An additional menu on mobile that appears for more options upon long press. Find out more about context menus with Todoist for iOS.

Your Account

Account

The account that a person logs in to access all the Todoist product features. In Settings, the Account tab is where you can change your account name or delete your account. You can also set up two-factor authentication for extra security.

Email address

The email address used to log in to your Todoist account. You may receive notifications at this exact email address for custom reminders, billing notices, or task notifications for your shared projects. You can change your email address.

Password

A sequence of characters, usually made up of letters, numbers, and symbols, someone enters to gain access to the Todoist account. You can change your password.

Two-factor authentication

Layer of security to your Todoist account that requires a one-time password generated by a third-party authentication app you install on your mobile device. You can set up two-factor authentication for extra protection.

Use folders to organize team projects

If your team has a long list of projects, use folders to better organize them in Todoist. They’re the perfect way to group and arrange projects according to your preferred criteria: by department, product cycle, client, and more. Everyone on your team will see how folders and projects are organized, so nothing slips through the cracks.

Note

Folders are available on every plan, including the Beginner plan, as long as you have a team workspace. They aren’t available for personal projects.

Play

Add a folder

Select Platform:

  • Click your Todoist team in the sidebar.
  • Click Add in the right-hand side.
  • Select Add folder.
  • Enter a name for your folder.
  • Click the Include projects menu to add projects to your folder. Otherwise, move to the next step.
  • Click Add.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap your team name. You’ll see an overview of your team projects.
  • Tap the plus icon next to your team name.
  • Select Add Folder.
  • Give the folder a name.
  • Tap Include projects to proactively add existing projects to your folder. Otherwise, move to the next step.
  • Tap Done at the top-right to confirm.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap your team name. You’ll see an overview of your team projects.
  • Tap the plus icon next to your team name.
  • Select Add folder.
  • Give the folder a name.
  • Tap Include projects to proactively add existing projects to your folder. Otherwise, move to the next step.
  • Tap the checkmark icon at the top-right to confirm. Note

If you’ve added multiple folders, they are all listed in the same order. There’s no option to move or nest folders within another folder.

Move a project to a folder

Select Platform:

Move a single project to a folder
  • Click the team your project belongs to in the sidebar.
  • Hover your mouse over the project you want to move.
  • Click the three dots icon next to the project name.
  • Hover your mouse over Organize into folder.
  • Select Move into folder.
  • Click the Folder menu and select the folder.
  • Click Move to confirm.
Move two or more projects to a folder
  • Click the team your projects belong to in the sidebar.
  • Hover your mouse over any one of the projects you want to move.
  • Click the three dots icon next to the project name.
  • Hover your mouse over Organize into folder.
  • Select Move into folder.
  • Click the Include projects menu and select two or more projects.
  • Click the Folder menu and select the folder.
  • Click Move to confirm.
  • Open the project you want to move into a folder.
  • Tap the three dots icon in the top-right.
  • Tap Move into Folder.
  • Select the folder you want to move your project to.
  • Open the project you want to move into a folder.
  • Tap the three dots icon.
  • Tap Move into folder.
  • Select the folder you want to move your project to.
  • Tap Move in the bottom-right corner. Dermot · Customer Experience Specialist

Anyone on a Todoist team can sort team projects alphabetically (A-Z) or in reverse (Z-A), while admins have the option to sort projects manually. To sort projects, including those inside folders, click the Sort menu above the projects list and select Manual, A-Z, or Z-A. You’ll see how projects are sorted both in the team dashboard and on the sidebar.

Edit a folder

Select Platform:

  • Click your team name in the sidebar. On the right side, you’ll see a list of projects and folders you’ve joined.
  • Click the three dots icon to the right of the folder.
  • Select Edit and make the necessary changes.
  • Click Save to confirm.
  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap the team your folder belongs to.
  • Tap the three dots icon beside the folder.
  • Select Edit and make the necessary changes.
  • Tap Done in the top-right to confirm.
  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap the team your folder belongs to.
  • Tap the three dots icon beside the folder.
  • Select Edit and make the necessary changes.
  • Tap the checkmark icon in the top-right to confirm. Note

You have to be a team admin or member to edit a folder. Learn more about roles, their permissions, and their restrictions.

Delete a folder

Select Platform:

  • Click your team name in the sidebar. On the right side, you’ll see a list of projects and folders you’ve joined.

  • Click the three dots icon to the right of the folder.

  • Select Delete.

  • Click Delete to confirm. When you delete a folder, your projects are moved out of that folder and back into the projects list.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-left.

  • Tap the team your folder belongs to.

  • Tap the three dots icon to the right of the folder.

  • Select Delete.

  • Tap Delete to confirm. When you delete a folder, your projects are moved out of that folder and back into the projects list.

Use team filters with your team

As your team’s workspace fills up with tasks, finding the right information needs to stay fast and effortless. That’s where team filters come in.

Team filters are shared, customizable views of tasks that use query syntax to surface exactly what your team needs. You can collectively narrow down task lists by name, date, project, label, priority, date created, and more – ensuring everyone stays aligned and focused on what matters.

Add a team filter

Note

If you see different tasks in your filter from a team member, this may be because you and your team member are part of different projects.

Select Platform:

  • Select Filters & Labels in the sidebar.
  • Click the + icon next to the team you want to add the filter in.
  • Create your filter:
    • Enter the filter name in the Name your filter field.
    • (Optional) Use the Location drop-down menu to change the location of your filter.
    • Enter the filter query in the Query field. Check out these filter query examples.
    • (Optional) Open the Color menu to choose a different filter color.
    • (Optional) Click the Favorite toggle to add the filter to your favorites.
  • Click Add to save your filter.
  • Tap Done at the top-right to save your new filter.
  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Tap the Add icon next to the team workspace you want to add a team filter for.
  • Create your filter:
    • Add a name for your filter.
    • Tap the Color menu to choose a different filter color.
    • Tap the Favorite toggle to add the filter to your favorites.
    • Enter the filter query. Check out these filter query examples.
  • Tap the checkmark icon at the top-right to save your team filter. Quick tip

If you want to make sure you only view tasks from your team workspace, you can add workspace: team name to your query. For example, if you want to view all tasks that are due today in your Doist workspace, you can create a team filter with the query today & workspace: Doist.

Edit a team filter

Select Platform:

  • Select Filters & Labels in the sidebar.
  • Find the filter you want to edit and hoover your mouse over it.
  • Click the pencil icon to the right of the filter name. Then, make changes to your filter.
  • Once you’re done making your changes, click Save.
  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Tap the filter you wish to edit.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Edit and make your changes.
  • Tap the checkmark icon to confirm.

Delete a team filter

Select Platform:

  • Click Filters & Labels in the sidebar.
  • Right-click the filter or click the three dots icon beside the filter name.
  • Select Delete to remove the filter.
  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Tap the filter you wish to delete.
  • Tap the three dots icon.
  • Select Delete.

Use the Inbox in Todoist

The Inbox is the default home for every new task in Todoist. It’s designed to help you get ideas out of your head quickly so you can stay focused on your current work. Once you’re ready, review your Inbox to organize, schedule, or add tasks to specific projects.

Play

Add a task

To add a task to your Inbox, grab the nearest Todoist app — on your desktop, phone, watch, or otherwise — click or tap the Add task button, enter the task name, and save the task. Any task that isn’t added to a specific project will be added to your Inbox by default.

Select Platform:

Prioritize urgent tasks

Flag the most important tasks in your Inbox using task priorities, so you won’t forget to finish them first. You can also sort or group tasks by priority, so you have more visibility over your most urgent tasks.

Process your Inbox regularly

Set aside a few minutes each day or week to process all the tasks that have been collected in your Inbox. To get more organized, move your tasks to their relevant projects. Then, add a date, so you’ll remember to come back to them later.

Select Platform:

Rachel · Customer Experience Specialist

On the web and desktop apps, you can drag a task to a different project in the navigation menu.

Not sure what to put in a project and what to keep in the Inbox? Learn about the difference between the Inbox and a project.

Delete unnecessary tasks

It’s okay to decide that a task doesn’t actually warrant your attention. You can delete the task, or perhaps move it to another project.

Work with others in Todoist

Todoist provides a versatile platform to work on tasks and projects with friends, family, or your team. Whether you’re managing household chores in personal projects or coordinating roadmaps in a team, this guide explains how to choose the right project type and maximize productivity with others using shared features.

Work with family and friends in personal projects

Whether you’re planning a weekend getaway or organizing a family reunion, you can share a personal project with friends and family to keep everyone on the same page. Open the project, click Share at the top-right, then enter the person’s name or email address to invite them. Learn more about collaborating with friends and family.

Work with your team in team projects

Whether you manage a small project with a few teammates or coordinate across departments, team projects keep everyone’s work visible in one shared space. Open the project, click Share at the top-right, then add people by name, email, or invite your whole team at once. Learn more about working with your team.

Compare personal and team projects

The limits that apply to different types of projects also reflect how they’re best used. Depending on who you’re working with, you can choose between personal projects and team projects. While both allow you to share tasks and stay organized, they serve different purposes and offer different levels of control.

Feature

Personal projects

Quick tip

If you’d like to learn more about how upgrading your plan affects your project limits, check out Todoist limits for tasks, projects, files and more.

Guest vs. sharing a personal project

When someone invites you to work with them, what you can access depends on the type of project.

If you’re invited to a personal project, you can view and edit everything in that project. The features you can use depend on your own plan, not the plan of the person who invited you. If they have a paid plan and you don’t, their paid features won’t be available to you in the shared project. The same is true in reverse: if you have a paid plan and they don’t, your paid features won’t be available to them.

If you’re invited to a team project from outside the team, you join as a guest. Guests can access only the specific project they’re invited to, and don’t get the team’s paid features, like deadlines. Guest and member are team roles. Teams can invite guests on both the Beginner and Business plans. To learn more, see Team roles and access.

Note

If your team is on the Business plan, team members (not guests) also get all Pro features in their personal projects.

How many people you can invite

The number of people you can invite depends on the type of project and your plan. For the current project limits, see Usage limits in Todoist.

Add files and links to Todoist from your mobile devices

Whether you want to add an image, file, link, or other attachment to your Todoist, you can do so without even opening the app. Here’s how:

Upload a file to Todoist

Select Platform:

  • Open the photo or file that you’d like to upload to Todoist.
  • Tap the share sheet icon.
  • Select Todoist from the share sheet.
  • Enter a name for the task. Assign a due date or add it to a project, if needed.
  • Tap the submit icon to save your task.
  • Open the photo or file that you’d like to upload to Todoist.
  • Tap Share.
  • Tap the Todoist icon in the share sheet.
  • If you want to attach the file to an existing task:
    • Select Todoist Comment.
    • Select a project and pick a task.
    • Add a comment.
    • Tap the send icon to attach the file.
  • If you want to attach the file to a new task:
    • Select Todoist Task.
    • Enter a name for the task. Assign a due date or add it to a project, if needed.
    • Tap the send icon to save your task.

Add a link to Todoist

Select Platform:

  • Open the link in a browser.
  • Tap the share sheet icon under the address bar.
  • Select Todoist from the share sheet.
  • Enter the name of the task. Assign a due date or add it to a project, if needed.
  • Tap the submit icon to save your task. Note

If the Todoist icon is missing in the Share menu, restart your device and share a file or link again.

  • Open the link in a browser.
  • Tap the address bar to highlight the link.
  • Tap the share icon.
  • Tap Todoist in the share sheet.
  • If you want to add the link as a comment to an existing task:
    • Select Todoist Comment.
    • Select a project and pick a task.
    • Tap the send icon to add the comment.
  • If you want to add the website as a new task:
    • Select Todoist Task.
    • Make changes to the task, if needed (for example: edit the task name or select a project).
    • Tap the send icon to save the task.

Add an attachment to a Todoist task

Select Platform:

  • Open Quick Add.
  • Tap Attachment.
  • Choose between Camera, Last Photo Taken, Photo & Video Library, Files, or Record Audio.
  • Select the file you want to attach.
  • Save your task.

Add task via voice command on Apple Watch

Get tasks out of your head and onto your to-do list fast by dictating them to your Apple Watch.

  • Open the Todoist app by tapping the Todoist logo on your Apple Watch face.
  • Scroll up and tap Add Task.
  • Tap the microphone icon in the bottom-right corner of your watch face.
  • Say the task details and tap OK.
  • On the next screen, you can select the task’s project.
  • When you’re finished, tap Save.

Add tasks to Quick Note on your iPad

Warning

You can only use this feature on an iPad running iPadOS 15 or later. This isn’t available on macOS or iOS devices.

If you like to make notes, you may want to link to one of your Todoist tasks within a note.

The good news is, if you have Todoist installed on an iPad, you can add links to your Todoist tasks in your Quick Note notes!

  • Open Todoist on your iPad and go to the project that has the task you want to add to a Quick Note.
  • Swipe up from the bottom-right corner of your display to open Quick Note.
  • Add whatever text you would like to have in your note.
  • With Todoist open in the background, tap the task you want to add to your note.
  • Select Add link +. A link to your task is now added to your note.

Customize the Todoist navigation bar

Customize the navigation bar by adding views often used in your Todoist account. Access these views quickly, so more time is spent getting work done.

Play

Any view added to a tab in the navigation bar is automatically removed from the Browse menu.

Select Platform:

  • Tap Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.
  • Select Navigation.
  • Tap Add to add the new tabs to the navigation bar.
  • The Tab Bar options are Inbox, Today, Upcoming, Filters & Labels, Search, Browse, or Team.
  • Tap Edit at the top-right corner.
  • Drag tabs by the drag handles to rearrange the order, or remove tabs from the navigation bar.
  • Tap the checkmark icon to confirm.
  • Tap Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Select Navigation bar.
  • Tap Add to add the new tabs to the navigation bar.
  • Drag tabs by the drag handles to rearrange the tab order.
  • Tap the three dots icon and choose either Select navigation item to add a tab, or Remove to remove a tab from the menu. If you want to restore the default options, press RESTORE DEFAULTS.

Note

If you uninstall or log out of Todoist on iOS or Android, your navigation bar will reset to the default tabs: Inbox, Today, Upcoming, Team (if you’re part of an active workspace) and Browse. After logging back in, you’ll need to re-add your preferred views to the navigation bar.

How to change your swipe actions

Todoist for iOS and Android allow you to change your Swipe actions at any time to decide which action you want to perform when swiping left or right over your task. When customizing your Swipe actions, you can choose from Complete, Schedule, Delete, Reminders, or Select (Android only).

Here’s how:

Changing your swipe actions

Select Platform:

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Tap General.
  • Scroll down to Swipe actions at the bottom of the screen.
  • Choose whether you want to Select, Complete, Schedule, or Delete a task when swiping left or right. Quick tip

If you’re using the Android app, you can view your project list at any time by dragging your finger from the bottom of the screen to the top of the screen.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Tap General.
  • Scroll down to Swipe Actions at the bottom of the screen.
  • Choose from Complete, Schedule, Reminders or Delete a task when swiping left or right. Quick tip

Use a two-finger swipe to quickly select tasks. You can also long press a task in list layout, or use the three dots menu in the top-right in each view.

Use a Todoist widget on an Apple device

Turn your Apple device into your productivity center with the Todoist widget. Whether you’re checking your list on your iPhone or managing projects on your Mac, the Todoist widget lets you add tasks quickly, check your goals, and see what’s due for today.

Add a Todoist widget

Add the widget to your desktop, home screen, or lock screen, so you can quickly check what’s next, no matter where you go.

Select Platform:

Todoist widgets are supported on Macs running macOS Sonoma (14) or later. If your Mac meets this requirement, follow the steps in this Apple Support article to add the Todoist widget to your desktop or Notification Center.

The MacOS widget provides an overview of your tasks. When clicking on the widget, it automatically opens your Todoist app.

Add a home screen widget

  • Touch and hold anywhere on your Home Screen until your apps start to wiggle.

  • Tap the Add button on the top-left.

  • Scroll down and tap the Todoist icon. A menu will open where you can swipe to choose the widget you want to add — Tasks, Productivity, or Add Task:

  • Tasks widget: Available as a small, medium, or large widget. This widget gives you a compact overview of all tasks in a certain view, like Today or Upcoming, or a project, filter, or label.

  • Quick tip

  • On iOS 17, you can complete tasks directly from the medium and large Tasks widget.

  • Productivity widget: Available as a medium widget. This widget gives you an overview of your current productivity stats, like how close you are to reaching your daily or weekly goals, as well as your current Karma score.

  • Add Task widget: Available as a small widget. This widget lets you open Quick Add from your iOS Home Screen, so you can quickly add a new task to Todoist.

Add a lock screen widget

If your device is running iOS 16 or above, you’ll be able to add widgets to your Lock Screen.

  • Touch and hold the Lock Screen.
  • Tap Customize.
  • Tap Lock Screen.
  • Tap Add Widgets.
  • Scroll down and select Todoist.
  • Tap or drag the widget you want to add:
    • Tasks: View tasks from your task list of choice.
    • Today’s Progress: Check in on today’s progress.
    • Next Task: View the next upcoming task from your Today view.
    • Add Task: Add tasks quickly to Todoist.
    • Task Goal: View your daily or weekly task goals.
    • Productivity: View your productivity stats.
  • Tap the Close button.
  • Tap Done in the top-right. If this is your first time customizing a Lock Screen on your device, you’ll need to pick a wallpaper for your Lock Screen. If you’ve added a customized Lock Screen before, you can edit an existing Lock Screen.

If the Todoist widget doesn’t appear when you swipe right on your Lock Screen, learn how to view widgets when your iPad is locked.

  • Touch and hold the Home Screen until your apps begin to jiggle.
  • Tap the Add button at the top-right.
  • Scroll down and select Todoist.
  • A menu will open where you can swipe to choose the widget you want to add — Tasks, Productivity, or Add Task:
    • Tasks widget: View tasks from your task list of choice.
    • Quick tip
    • On iPadOS 17, you can complete tasks directly from the Tasks widget!
    • Add Task widget: Add tasks quickly to Todoist.
    • Productivity widget: View your productivity stats.
  • Tap Add Widget.
  • Move the widget to where you want on the Home Screen.
  • Tap Done at the top-right. Note

If you’ve used Todoist on another device, the Todoist widget may take up to 15 minutes to finish syncing data. To sync data right away, open the Todoist app.

Change the widget settings

If you need something other than your Today list, here’s how to change the settings of the Todoist widget, so it displays information that’s most useful to you.

Select Platform:

On macOS, you can only change the Todoist widget size. Press ⌃ Control and click the Todoist widget. Then, choose your preferred widget size.

Change the Tasks widget settings
  • Unlock your iOS device.
  • Touch and hold the Tasks widget. A context menu will pop up.
  • Tap Edit Widget.
  • Tap View.
  • Select the view you want from the menu that pops up.
  • Tap the screen outside of the widget to save your changes. Quick tip

If you select Project, Label, or Filter, the widget will prompt you to specify which project, label, or filter to set as your view.

Change the Add Task widget settings
  • Unlock your iOS device.
  • Touch and hold the Tasks widget. A context menu will pop up.
  • Tap Edit Widget.
  • Tap View.
  • Enter the task name, project and section, due date, priority level, or label for any task you create with the widget.
  • Tap the screen outside of the widget to save your changes. Note

The color of the Todoist widget will change based on the theme of your Todoist app, unless you’ve turned on Dark mode. If you’ve turned on Dark mode for your device, the Todoist widget will automatically match Dark mode.

Remove a Todoist widget

If you no longer want to use the Todoist widget, or you’d like to replace your current widget, here’s how to remove it:

Select Platform:

Follow the steps in the Apple support article to remove the Todoist widget from your desktop or Notification Center.

Remove a home screen widget
  • Touch and hold the widget to open the context menu.
  • Tap Remove Widget.
  • Tap Remove to confirm.
Remove a lock screen widget
  • Unlock your screen using Face ID or Touch ID.
  • Touch and hold the screen.
  • Tap Customize.
  • Tap Lock Screen.
  • Tap the widget you want to remove.
  • Tap the minus icon at the top-left of the widget.
  • Tap Done at the top-right to confirm.
  • Touch and hold the widget to open the context menu.
  • Tap Remove Widget.
  • Tap Remove.

Use context menus with Todoist for iOS

Apple introduced context menus in iOS 13 and later to make it easier and quicker for users to interact or make changes to items.

In Todoist, there are context menus for tasks, projects, filters, or labels. Touch and hold an item on your iOS device, and you’ll see several quick actions.

Tasks

To see the context menu for a task, make sure you’re in a project or view that uses the list layout.

Then, touch and hold the task to open the context menu. You’ll see the following options:

  • Select Task lets you select either a single task or multiple tasks for editing.

  • Schedule opens a schedule window where you can set a due date and time for your task.

  • Move to… lets you move your task to another project and/or section.

  • Priority lets you set the priority level for your task.

  • Duplicate Task creates a duplicate of the selected task.

  • Copy Link to Task copies the task’s link to your clipboard.

  • Delete Task deletes the selected task. In shared projects, you’ll see the following options:

  • Assign lets you assign the task to yourself or a collaborator.

  • Complete Forever lets you complete a task and end its recurrence.

Projects

Long press the project you wish to edit to open the context menu. A menu will pop-up with the following options:

  • Edit lets you edit your project’s name and color.
  • Share lets you add collaborators to your project or remove current collaborators.
  • Duplicate lets you create a copy of the project.
  • Add to Favorites lets you add the project to your Favorites. If the project’s already added to your Favorites, you’ll see Remove from Favorites instead.
  • Archive Project moves the project to your archive. In shared projects, you’ll see the option Leave Project, which lets you leave the shared project.

Filters

Long press the filter you wish to edit to open the context menu. A menu will pop up with the following options:

  • Edit Filter opens a window where you can edit the filter’s name and color, as well as its filter query.
  • Copy Link to Filter copies the filter’s link to your clipboard.
  • Add to Favorites lets you add the filter to your Favorites. If the filter’s already added to your Favorites, you’ll see Remove from Favorites instead.
  • Delete Filter deletes the selected filter. Quick tip

If you’re using a mouse or a trackpad with an iPad running on iPadOS 13.4 or later, you can also open a context menu by right-clicking on a task, project, label or filter.

Labels

Long press the label you wish to edit to open the context menu. You’ll find the following options:

  • Edit Label opens a window where you can edit your label’s name and color.
  • Copy Link to Label copies the label’s link to your clipboard.
  • Add to Favorites lets you add the label to your Favorites. If the label’s already added to your Favorites, you’ll see Remove from Favorites instead.
  • Delete Label deletes the selected label. If you’re making changes to a shared label, you’ll only see the Edit Label and Delete Label options.

Get help

The context menu may appear even when you just want to drag and reorder a task, project, label, or filter. This is a limitation that may impact all iOS apps that use context menus. As a workaround, touch and hold a task, project, filter, or label. Then, move it slightly to the right to close the context menu.

Use Live Text to scan and add text as tasks in Todoist for iOS

As you’re reading today’s feature article, or the next chapter in your self-help book, you spot valuable insights you want to save as a Todoist task. If you have supported Apple device, you can use Live Text to scan text from images or videos, and quickly turn them into tasks.

  • Check if Live Text is turned on for your Apple device.
  • Open your phone camera and focus on the text.
  • Tap the Live Text icon that appears at the bottom-right of screen. It’ll zoom in to the selected text.
  • Tap and select the text you want to turn into a Todoist task.
  • Tap the chevron icon.
  • Select Share.
  • Select Todoist. This opens Quick Add with the task name pre-filled with the selected text.
  • Add any additional task details, like a date, priority, or reminder.
  • Tap the submit icon to add the task.

Use Shortcuts with Todoist for iOS

We all have Todoist actions that we repeat often, like adding a task to your grocery project. Sometimes, it can get repetitive to constantly add it to the same project and set the same date.

Play

The good news is that if you’re using an iOS or iPadOS device running on iOS 17 or later, you can now create time-saving Shortcuts that let you do your most common Todoist actions without having to repeat every step, every time.

For instance, you can create a shortcut that helps you quickly add a task to your shopping list by just saying “Add to shopping”. Activate the shortcut and your device will ask you for the task’s name, then automatically move the task to your “Shopping” project, and set its due date for Saturday (or whatever date and project works for you).

Quick tip

If you have set up a schedule for a Sleep Focus, you can add Todoist Shortcuts to your Wind Down screen:

  • Open the Health app.
  • Tap Sleep.
  • Tap Full Schedule & Options.
  • Tap Wind Down Shortcuts.
  • Choose the Todoist Shortcuts you want to add to your Wind Down screen. You can choose between four shortcuts: Open Todoist, Open Upcoming, Add Task, and Open Today.

Create a shortcut that uses Todoist actions

  • Open the standalone Shortcuts app.
  • Tap Create Shortcut or the + symbol at the top of the screen.
  • Search for the Todoist action Create Task.
  • Set Task Name. If you select Ask Each Time, you will be asked for the task’s name whenever you use this Shortcut.
    • If you add your own task name, such as Buy Milk, a task with this name will be added whenever you use this Shortcut.
    • The Task Name field doesn’t automatically recognize dates or other task details, so use the dedicated fields in the next step to add them.
  • You have a few options for the due date, project, priority and labels for the new task: You can make Siri ask you for the information when you create the task, or you can explicitly set each field (like setting the project to “Shopping”).
  • (Optional) If you toggle Show when run you’ll be notified whenever the shortcut has run.
  • Tap Next in the top-right corner.
  • Enter the name for your new shortcut and tap Done. Note

Due to an Apple Shortcuts limitation, running a Todoist shortcut may open the app instead of creating the task in the background. The task is still created successfully.

Once your shortcut is created, you can activate it by asking Siri. You can also activate it from the Share Sheet, Today Widget, from the Shortcuts app, use the shortcut in an automation, and more. Here are a few examples to start with:

  • Ask Siri to “Get ready for my trip” which can automatically add tasks for every item in your packing list to your “Travel” project.
  • Tell Siri about a “New bill”, and your device will ask you for the name of the bill, and when it’s due, and then move the new task to your “Bills” project.
  • Create an automated shortcut that triggers every time your phone connects to your Home Wi-Fi, and adds a task to take out the trash.
  • Create an automated shortcut that triggers every morning at 9am on weekdays, and adds a task to eat breakfast, a task to feed the dog, and a task to pick up your favorite coffee. Quick tip

If your Apple device is on iOS 14 or later, you can customize the double or triple tap on the back of your iPhone to launch a specific shortcut:

  • Make sure you’ve already created the shortcut using the instructions in this article.
  • Open the Settings app.
  • Select Accessibility.
  • Select Touch, then Back Tap.
  • Choose either Double Tap or Triple Tap.
  • Select the shortcut you want easy access to.

Siri shows an error when you run a Todoist shortcut

If Siri returns a generic error when it tries to create a task through a Todoist shortcut, the shortcut might not be enabled for Siri. This setting lives on the individual shortcut in the Shortcuts app, and it’s separate from the Todoist toggle in the Settings app (under Apple Intelligence & Siri, then Apps, then Todoist). If reinstalling Todoist or toggling the integration in Todoist’s settings hasn’t helped, turn the per-shortcut setting on:

  • Open the Shortcuts app.
  • Find your Todoist shortcut and tap the info (i) icon.
  • Turn on Use with Siri. Run the shortcut with Siri again to confirm the task is created.

Use Siri with Todoist

Hey Siri, remind me to “Buy a present tomorrow 5:00 PM” in Todoist.

Easy-peasy, right? Dictate tasks with just your voice, so you can capture and view your todos without needing to pull up your device. Siri’s especially handy when you’re driving or if you’ve got both your hands full.

System requirements

To use Siri with Todoist, upgrade your Apple device to iOS 11 or later. To use Siri with Apple Intelligence, upgrade your Apple device to iOS 18 or later.

If you’re using a macOS, Apple Watch, or CarPlay device, there’s no option to use Siri with Todoist.

Keywords to use with Siri

Here’s a handy list of keywords to use with Siri:

  • [Project name] list
  • Task or tasks
  • Item or items
  • Add [task name]
  • Remind me to [task name]
  • In Todoist
  • Show me all the tasks for Note

Siri doesn’t recognize the words project or projects. Instead, use list to add a task to a project.

Set up Siri

If you’re using your device without Apple Intelligence, you can start using Siri with Todoist right away. If you’re using Apple Intelligence and Siri, here’s how to set it up:

  • Open the Settings app of your Apple device.
  • Tap Apple Intelligence & Siri.
  • Scroll down and tap Apps.
  • Select Todoist.
  • Select Apple Intelligence & Siri.
  • Make sure to turn on the Use with Siri Requests option.

Create a task with Siri

To get started, say “Siri” or “Hey Siri”, and use natural language to add tasks to Todoist. Here are examples of sentences to try, so that Siri understands exactly what you want to do:

Action

Commands

Tips

Add tasks

  • Add [task name] in Todoist
  • Add a task named [task name] in Todoist
  • Remind me to [task name] in Todoist When you add a task without a project, it will be added to your Todoist Inbox.

Add tasks to a project

  • Add [task name] to my [project name] list in Todoist
  • Add “Buy milk” to my Groceries list in Todoist
  • Remind me to [task name] to my [project name] list in Todoist To add a task to an existing project, say the project name followed by list in Todoist. Siri doesn’t recognize the words project or projects.

Add due dates and due time

  • Add [task name] at date at time in Todoist
  • Add [task name] at time to my [project name] list in Todoist
  • Remind me to [task name] date at time in Todoist If you don’t specify the date, but it recognizes the time and it isn’t overdue, the task is scheduled for today. If you specify the time, but it’s overdue, Todoist adds it to the task name as plain text.

View a task with Siri

Can’t remember if you’ve already added a task to Todoist? Ask Siri to pull up a list of tasks by date, project, or both. Here are a few examples:

  • Show me all the tasks for date in Todoist
  • Show me all the tasks for the next 7 days in Todoist
  • Show me all the tasks for date between time and time in Todoist
  • Show me the [project name] list in Todoist Dermot · Customer Experience Specialist

You’ll need to say “in Todoist” at the end of any Siri request, so she understands what to do.

Use Siri shortcuts

Use Siri shortcuts to save time by automating certain Todoist actions you do repetitively, like adding an item to your grocery list without needing to specify the latter every time. Learn how to use Todoist with Shortcuts.

View tasks using Siri

Easily ask Siri to pull up a list of tasks by date or project, or both. Here are a few examples of voice commands you can use:

  • Show me all the tasks for today in Todoist
  • Show me all the tasks for the next 7 days in Todoist
  • Show me all the tasks for today between 10am and 12am in Todoist
  • Show me the shopping list in Todoist

Use Siri Shortcuts with Todoist

Use Siri Shortcuts to save time working on often repeated Todoist actions, like adding an item to your grocery list without having to select the project list every time. Read all about how to use Todoist with Shortcuts.

Use Siri in a different language

You can use Todoist with Siri in any of the supported languages included in iOS. However, it can be a bit unpredictable, so it helps to vary your pronunciation of the word “Todoist” or the speed and way you speak.

If your language is supported, but Siri’s having trouble adding or retrieving Todoist tasks for you, check out these example phrases from Apple Support for adding tasks or viewing tasks with Siri. Otherwise, you can use Todoist with Shortcuts to bypass the need to say “in Todoist” when speaking to Siri.

Use the Dynamic Add button in Todoist

On mobile devices, use the Dynamic Add button to create a task, sub-task, or section in Todoist. Touch and drag the button anywhere in projects, the Today view, or the Upcoming view.

Note

  • The Dynamic Add button doesn’t create a project, filter, or label.
  • The button only works if a project or view uses the list layout and if there aren’t any applied sorting or grouping options.

Add a task in the Today, Upcoming, or project views

Select Platform:

  • Touch and drag the Dynamic Add Button to where you want to create the new task.
  • Enter the task name and add any details.
  • Tap the submit button to save the task.
  • Touch and drag the Dynamic Add Button to where you want to create the new task.
  • Enter the task name and add any details.
  • Tap the submit button to save the task.

Add a sub-task

To create a sub-task, check if the project is using the list layout.

Then, drag the Dynamic Add Button below the parent task and slightly to the right of the list.

Add a section to a project

Select Platform:

  • Touch and drag the Dynamic Add Button in any direction. A section icon will appear at the bottom-left of the screen.
  • Drag the Dynamic Add Button over the section icon.
  • Enter the name of the new section.
  • Tap the submit button to save the section.
  • Touch and drag the Dynamic Add Button all the way to the left of the screen.
  • Drop it between sections or below an existing section. You will see “Add section” when you’ve moved it to a place where a section can be created.
  • Enter the section name.
  • Tap the submit button to save the section.

Use Todoist Controls on iOS

Optimize your workflow with custom Todoist Controls on iOS. You can add Controls to quickly create new tasks and open your most visited views in the Control Center, your Lock screen or by customizing Action Buttons on your Apple device.

Note

Todoist Controls are available on iOS 18 and later versions.

Add a Todoist Control to Control Center

Play

  • Swipe down from the top-right corner of your Apple device to open the Control Center.
  • Tap the plus icon at the top-left corner to add or customize a control. You can also touch and hold the screen for a few seconds.
  • Tap Add a Control at the bottom of your screen.
  • Search for Todoist and choose from the following controls:
    • Add task: create a new task and select its task attributes, like task name or due date.
    • Open view: change the current view by choosing any of the available options from the list.
  • Drag the bottom-right corner of the control to resize it.
  • Swipe up from the bottom of the screen to close the Control Center.

Add a Todoist Control to Lock Screen

Play

  • Lock your device.
  • Long-press the lock screen.
  • Tap Customize at the bottom of your screen.
  • Select Lock Screen. You’ll see your existing controls at the bottom of the screen.
  • Tap the minus icon to remove existing controls.
  • Tap the plus icon to add a Control.
  • Search for Todoist.
  • Select either the Add task or Open view control.
  • Tap Done at the top-right to save changes.

Control for Action Button

Note

Note

This feature is available only on iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max and iPhone 16 series.

  • Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  • Search for Action Button.
  • Swipe left until Controls is selected.
  • Tap Choose Control.
  • Search for Todoist.
  • Select Add task or Open view control.
  • Configure control in the popup view and tap outside of it when done.

Use Todoist on Apple Watch

Todoist for watchOS gives you full control of Todoist right from your Apple Watch. You can add new tasks, check and complete your tasks, set custom complications and more.

Play

Set up Todoist for watchOS

To get started, install Todoist on the Apple Watch:

  • Check that Todoist is installed on the iOS device.
  • Open the Watch app on the iOS device.
  • Tap My Watch at the bottom of the screen.
  • Scroll down to Available Apps.
  • Tap Install beside Todoist.

Add a task

Add new tasks in Todoist for Apple Watch:

  • Open the Todoist app on the Apple Watch.
  • Scroll up and select Add task.
  • Add a task by using the keyboard or tapping the microphone icon at the bottom-right and dictating the task name. A menu will appear where you can choose the project.
  • Tap OK at the top-right to confirm. Your watch will recognize dates too, so you can say things like today, next Saturday, or May 31.

Add or change a task date

Add a due date or change the existing due date of a task:

  • Open the Todoist app on your watch.
  • Choose the view where the task is located.
  • Tap the task you’d like to reschedule.
  • Tap the calendar icon in the top-right.
  • Select one of the preset dates or dictate it using Siri.
  • Go back to one of your views.

Complete a task

Complete a task on your watch with a tap:

  • Open the Todoist app on your watch.
  • Open the view containing the task you want to complete.
  • Tap the circle next to the task you’d like to complete. Warning

Todoist for watchOS requires that the Apple Watch is in range of your Apple device to be able to update information, such as adding new tasks, changing dates, or completing tasks.

Use Todoist complications on your watch face

Stay updated with Todoist at a glance by using any of these watch complications:

  • Utilitarian Large shows the next task.
  • Graphic Rectangular shows the next task and how many tasks are due today and overdue.
  • Graphic Circular shows the completed percentage of today’s tasks.
  • Graphic Bezel shows the completed percentage of today’s tasks.
  • Graphic Corner shows the completed percentage of today’s tasks.

Troubleshoot issues with Todoist for watchOS

Notifications won’t appear on your Apple Watch when it’s locked (for example, when it’s been removed from your wrist). In that case, they’ll be delivered to your iPhone instead.

If you’re having trouble syncing Todoist with the watchOS app, follow these steps:

  • Delete Todoist for watchOS on your Apple Watch

  • Log out of Todoist for iOS. Then, log back in.

  • Restart your phone.

  • Reinstall Todoist for watchOS. If you see a “Log in to Todoist” prompt in Todoist for watchOS, even though you’re already logged in to Todoist on your Apple device, follow these steps:

  • Delete Todoist for watchOS on your Apple Watch.

  • Log out of Todoist for iOS. Then, log back in.

  • Restart your phone.

  • Reinstall Todoist for watchOS.

Login & Account Access

Add a valid email address if you log in with Apple or Facebook

If you’ve signed up to Todoist with an Apple or Facebook account and chose to not share the email address associated with it, we automatically assign a unique but invalid @users.todoist.com address to identify your Todoist account. You’ll see it listed under account settings.

This means that you can’t receive email notifications about updates in Todoist. We also won’t be able to reach out if you get in touch with us via the help center.

To ensure you don’t miss any important information, update your account with an active and valid email address. You’ll still be able to log into Todoist with your Google, Apple, or Facebook credentials.

Add an account password

If your Todoist account is associated with a @users.todoist.com address, add a password to your Todoist account:

  • Open a web browser.
  • Log in to your Todoist account: todoist.com
  • Click your avatar.
  • Select Settings & Account.
  • Click Add Password.
  • Enter a strong 10-15 character password for your account. This ensures it passes Todoist password security measures.

Change your email address

After successfully adding a password to your Todoist account, change your Todoist email address and replace it with an active and valid email address.

Note

If you’ve turned on two-factor authentication in Todoist, you’ll need a one-time passcode from your chosen authentication app to change your email address.

For Apple: Check if Todoist is registered to your Apple Account

If you’re using Apple to sign in to Todoist, your Todoist account may be registered to the email address associated with your Apple Account. You may be asked to check or confirm this when contacting Todoist about an issue or bug. Here’s how you can check:

  • Open the System Settings app on your Apple device.
  • Tap your name.
  • Select Sign in with Apple.

Can I merge several Todoist accounts?

It’s not possible to merge separate Todoist accounts at this point.

Alternative solution

If you’d like to transfer your data (active tasks, projects, and labels in current use) from one account to another, you can do so by exporting and importing projects. Simply backup all the data in your account as CSV files and then import them into to your other account. Your completed tasks, filters, labels not in current use, and Karma progress will not be transferred.

  • Instructions
  • Alternative solution

CSRF token error messages

If you’re seeing a CSRF error message when logging into your Todoist account, don’t panic. You can find some simple solutions below:

Invalid or missing CSRF token

This error message means that your browser couldn’t create a secure cookie, or couldn’t access that cookie to authorize your login. This can be caused by ad- or script-blocking plugins, but also by the browser itself if it’s not allowed to set cookies.

To address this issue, follow these steps.

Chrome

  • Open Chrome Settings.
  • In the Privacy and security section, click Cookies and other site data.
  • Scroll down to Sites that can always use cookies and click Add.
    • Copy and paste [*.]todoist.com and click Add.
    • Copy and paste [*.]cloudfront.net and click Add.
  • Click See all cookies and site data.
  • Search for todoist.
  • Delete all Todoist-related entries.
  • Reload Chrome and log into Todoist.

Firefox

  • Open Firefox Settings.
  • On the left, select Privacy & Security.
  • Under Cookies and Site Data click on Manage Exceptions.
    • Copy and paste https://todoist.com and click Allow.
    • Then copy and paste https://cloudfront.net and click Allow.
  • Click Save Changes.
  • Click Manage Data.
  • Search for todoist and select Remove All Shown.
  • Click Save Changes.
  • Click Remove to confirm.
  • Reload Firefox and log into Todoist.

Safari

  • Open Safari Preferences from the drop-down menu in the navigation bar or by typing Cmd + , (⌘,).
  • Click the Privacy tab.
  • Check that Cookies and website data is not set to Block all cookies.
  • Click Manage Website Data to see all locally stored website data.
  • Search for todoist and remove all Todoist-related entries.
  • Reload Safari and log into Todoist.

CSRF tokens mismatch

This error message is caused by privacy extensions. If you are running any privacy extensions such as Ghostery or Privacy Badger, make sure to add todoist.com as a trusted website.

Get in touch

If you’ve followed the steps above and you’re still running into a CSRF issue, get in touch with us.

Regain access to your Todoist account

If you’ve lost access to your Todoist account because your email account has changed, your third-party login isn’t working, or there’s a typo in the email address, don’t fret. This guide will walk you through your options to recover your Todoist account.

Check if you’re still logged in on any of your devices

Open Todoist on any of your devices and see if you’re still logged in. If you are, you can take a screenshot of your Todoist Account Settings:

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Click the Account tab.
  • Take a screenshot of your Todoist account settings.
  • Get in touch with us about recovering your account, and attach the screenshot to your message.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap Settings at the top-right.
  • Select Account.
  • Take a screenshot of your Todoist account settings.
  • Get in touch with us about recovering your account, and attach the screenshot to your message. If you’re not logged in to your Todoist account on any of your devices, continue to the next step.

Provide a copy of your Pro or Business plan receipt

If you upgraded to Todoist Pro or Todoist Business, a receipt of your payment is sent to your Todoist account email address. Use the search feature of your email app to find any emails from Todoist with the subject line “Your [plan type] receipt”.

If you upgraded using an in-app purchase with Apple or Google, you’ll find your receipts in your App Store or Google Play Store account.

Then, take a screenshot of the receipt. Get in touch with us about recovering your account, and attach it to your message.

Provide payment details of the upgrade or renewal

If you upgraded through direct billing with Todoist, but you can’t find a copy of your receipt, you may have access to the payment card associated with the upgrade or renewal. Get in touch with us about recovering your account, and provide the following:

  • Last four digits of the card that was charged
  • Payment card brand (for example: Visa, Mastercard, JCB)
  • Expiry date of your card
  • Exact amount that was charged
  • Date of the last charge Please don’t share your full credit card number or security code. Our team will check and verify that you’re the rightful owner of the Todoist account.

Update your account password and email address

After verifying that you own the Todoist account, you’ll receive a special link to change the password of your account. Enter a strong password and save it in a safe place, so you’ll always have access to your account.

Then, change the account email to an active email address you currently use.

Stef · Customer Experience Specialist

Watch out for typos! Check that you’ve entered your email address correctly before saving your changes in Todoist.

Start over: No proof of account ownership

If you’ve lost access to your Todoist account, and it was solely on the free plan, we won’t be able to verify account ownership and help you recover your account. The best way to move forward is to sign up for a new Todoist account with an active email address and strong password.

If you need any help setting up a new Todoist account, get in touch with us.

  • Instructions
  • Check if you’re still logged in on any of your devices
  • Provide a copy of your Pro or Business plan receipt
  • Provide payment details of the upgrade or renewal
  • Update your account password and email address
  • Start over: No proof of account ownership

Troubleshoot login issues with the Todoist desktop apps

When logging in to the Todoist desktop apps, a new browser tab opens automatically where you’ll enter your account credentials. If you find yourself in a constant login loop between the browser and the app, see an error message, blank screen, or if Todoist becomes unresponsive, follow the steps in this guide.

Use the latest version of Todoist

Select Platform:

If a new version is available, you’ll see a pop-up in Todoist to restart and update automatically. If you need to manually reinstall and update Todoist for macOS, follow these steps.

Right-click the Todoist icon in the system tray. Then, select Quit Todoist. The new version will automatically be installed once the app is closed.

If you need to manually reinstall and update Todoist for Windows, follow these steps.

If you need to manually reinstall Todoist for Linux to get the latest version, follow these steps.

Check if pop-ups are allowed

Since the location of these settings change frequently, check the browser help page for the latest steps to turn on pop-ups:

  • Google Chrome: Block or allow pop-ups
  • Microsoft Edge: Block pop-ups
  • Firefox: Pop-up blocker settings, exceptions, and troubleshooting
  • Safari: Allow or block pop-ups in Safari on Mac

Change the default browser

Change the default web browser temporarily to see if there is a browser-specific issue. Check the support article for your operating system:

  • macOS: Change the default web browser or email app on Mac
  • Windows: Change your default browser in Windows.
  • Linux: Change which web browser opens websites by default

Use the magic link

The magic link lets you create a unique URL that authenticates your Todoist account credentials and log in to the desktop apps. Use this link if the prompt to open the Todoist app doesn’t appear, or if you’re experiencing other login-related issues.

Clear application data

If the log in page is unresponsive or isn’t displaying properly, here’s how to clear application data in the desktop apps:

Select Platform:

  • Open Todoist for macOS.

  • Click Todoist in the main menu at the top-left.

  • Select Clear application data. Todoist for macOS will restart and the login page will appear.

  • Open Todoist for Windows.

  • Click the down arrow of the Windows tray menu at the bottom-right.

  • Right-click the Todoist app icon.

  • Select Clear application data. Todoist for Windows will restart and the login page will appear.

Reinstall Todoist and delete application files

Select Platform:

Learn how to uninstall Todoist for macOS and remove all application files. Then, download and reinstall the app.

  • Uninstall the Todoist app.
  • Press Windows + R.
  • Enter %APPDATA%/Todoist. This will open the Todoist app folder.
  • Delete the contents of the folder.
  • Reinstall the Todoist app. Learn how to uninstall Todoist for Linux using either Snap or AppImage.

Enable Application Loading Recovery

Select Platform:

  • Open Todoist for macOS.
  • Click Help in the menu bar at the top of your screen.
  • Hover over Troubleshooting.
  • Select Enable Application Loading Recovery. You’ll receive a message saying that the changes have been applied, and that the app will close.
  • Click OK.
  • Reopen the app. If it worked, everything should look as expected. If it didn’t work, there will be an error message. Take a screenshot of the error message.
  • Click Help in the menu bar at the top of your screen once more.
  • Hover over Troubleshooting.
  • Select Download logs.
  • Click Save on the pop-up.
  • Contact us to share the screenshotand download logs, so we can help troubleshoot this issue.
  • Open Todoist for Windows.
  • Right-click the Todoist icon in the system tray at the bottom-right corner of your screen.
  • Hover over Troubleshooting.
  • Select Enable Application Loading Recovery. You’ll receive a message saying that the changes have been applied, and that the app will close.
  • Click OK.
  • Reopen the app. If it worked, everything should look as expected. If it didn’t work, there will be an error message. Take a screenshot of the error message.
  • Click Help in the menu bar at the top of your screen once more.
  • Hover over Troubleshooting.
  • Select Download logs.
  • Click Save on the pop-up.
  • Contact us to share the screenshotand download logs, so we can help troubleshoot this issue. Note

Your logs help us understand what went wrong. They don’t contain any personal information and are completely safe to share.

Get in touch

  • Todoist app(s) where you’re experiencing the issue
  • App version number
  • Login method (for example: email and password or Google account)
  • Screenshots of any errors or warning messages in the app
  • Any other troubleshooting steps you’ve tried to resolve the issue

Troubleshoot two-factor authentication issues in Todoist

You’re trying to use two-factor authentication (2FA) with your Todoist account, but you’ve run into a slew of problems: the one-time password isn’t working; you can’t actually turn on 2FA; or you’ve lost your authenticator app, and with it, your codes for Todoist. If you’re experiencing any of these issues, learn how to regain access to your account again.

Verify your Todoist account

If you’re having trouble turning 2FA on for your account, make sure you’ve verified your Todoist account.

If you followed the steps, but didn’t receive a verification email, check your spam or junk folders, or get in touch with us so we can help you verify your account.

Enter the correct one-time passcode

If you’ve finished setting up 2FA, but the one-time passcode isn’t working and you can’t log in, check if:

  • You’re entering the code as it appears on your device.
  • You’re entering the code before it expires.
  • Your device’s clock settings are correctly synced to your third-party authentication app. If your one-time passcode is still not working, it’s time to request a recovery code.

Request a recovery code

The recovery code is a backup method for logging in to your Todoist account, in case you lose access to your third-party authentication app. It’s composed of 8 alphanumeric characters and generated either in your 2FA settings or manually by Todoist.

If you’ve lost access to your authentication app, or your one-time passcodes aren’t working, request a recovery code from our team.

The recovery code will arrive in the Inbox of your account email address.

Enter the recovery code

After receiving the recovery code, here’s how to use it when logging in to Todoist:

  • Open a web browser.
  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com.
  • Enter your account email address and password. If you use Google, Apple, or Facebook to log in, use your login credentials.
  • Click Enter a recovery code here below the Authentication code field.
  • Enter your recovery code. You’re now logged back in to your Todoist account.

Turn 2FA off in Todoist

To start over with your authenticator app, request another recovery code to turn 2FA off in Todoist. You can send another message using the contact form, or reply to your existing recovery code conversation with our team in the “My Tickets” section of the Help Center.

Turn 2FA back on for your account

After turning 2FA off with the second recovery code, create a fresh entry in your authentication app, and turn 2FA back on in Todoist.

Get in touch

It’s frustrating when you’re locked out of your Todoist account. If you’ve followed all the steps in this guide, but you’re still having trouble with logging back in or setting up 2FA with Todoist, get in touch with us.

  • Instructions
  • Verify your Todoist account
  • Enter the correct one-time passcode
  • Request a recovery code
  • Enter the recovery code
  • Turn 2FA off in Todoist
  • Turn 2FA back on for your account
  • Get in touch

Use the Magic Link to log in to Todoist

The magic link is a unique URL that authenticates your account credentials, so you can successfully log in to the Todoist desktop apps.

Use the magic link if the prompt to open Todoist doesn’t appear, or if you’re experiencing login issues with the desktop apps:

Note

Update Todoist to 8.17.0 or later to use the magic link when logging in to the app. If you’ve not installed it yet, download the Todoist desktop app.

  • Open the Todoist desktop app.
  • Click Continue in your browser.
  • Enter your Todoist account credentials. You’ll see a prompt to open the desktop app.
  • Click Cancel to close the prompt.
  • Click Try using a magic link in the login page.
  • Click the copy icon beside the magic link.
  • Switch to the Todoist app.
  • Click use a magic link.
  • Paste the magic link.
  • Click Log in.
