Use Llama Life with Todoist

Llama Life is a fun (yet powerful!) focus tool that helps you work through lists, not just make them. Llama Life uses a concept called time-boxing, which is the practice of setting a fixed amount of time (using a countdown timer) to each individual task. This creates the mental space to focus on one task at a time.

When you connect Llama Life to Todoist, you can easily sync your Todoist tasks that are due today into Llama Life, so you can transform them into manageable, bite-sized chunks of productivity.

Setting up the integration

  • Open Llama Life.
  • At the top left, select Settings.
  • Select Todoist Integration, then Connect to Todoist.
  • This will open a window where you’ll be asked to give Llama Life permission to read your Todoist tasks.
  • Once the permission is given, a new window will open.
  • In the top right, select Preset List.
  • Under the Todoist Today option, select Load.
  • That’s it! You can now start using the integration.

Using the integration

  • In Llama Life, you can reorder your tasks by dragging-and-dropping them into place.
  • For each task, you can add/edit a duration in minutes. If no duration is added, it will default to 25 min.
  • The task at the top of your list is automatically loaded into the timer. This task should be your current focus.
  • When you’re ready to begin the task, start the timer by clicking the play button.
  • When a task is complete, simply click Complete.
  • This integration is one-way. This means that when you complete a task in Llama Life, the task will not also be completed in Todoist. Quick tip

In Todoist, you can add a number at the end of the task name and the number will automatically convert into minutes in Llama Life. For example, if you type Write journal 60, one hour will automatically be assigned to this task in Llama Life. For more information on how to use all Llama Life features, please visit their website.

FAQ

Simply open the Preset Lists option and select the Edit option under Todoist Today.

If you no longer want to use Llama Life with Todoist, here’s how to remove the integration:

  • Open the Todoist web app.
  • Click your Profile photo in the top-right corner.
  • Select Integrations.
  • Next to Llama Life, click the X icon.
  • Select Disconnect.

Notion is an all-in-one workspace where you can write documents, plan project deadlines, and collaborate with others. To make work in Notion even more organized, you can embed Todoist. Review your projects or check for upcoming tasks side-by-side with your notes.

Warning

The Notion integration isn’t fully supported on mobile and desktop devices. To use it without issues, open Notion with a web browser and log in to your Todoist account.

Set up the integration

Troubleshoot login issues

If your web browser prevents cross-site tracking or blocks third-party cookies, the integration won’t recognize you logging in to Todoist. You’ll need to turn this setting off in your web browser to log in successfully.

Warning

Although allowing cross-site tracking or third-party cookies isn’t recommended due to privacy and security concerns, doing so won’t affect your Todoist data. We encourage proceeding with extreme caution.

Embed a specific view

You can embed a specific view (for example: a project, filter, or label view) in Notion. To set this up, open your preferred view in the Todoist web app, copy the link in the address bar, and add it to the Embed block in Notion.

Remove the integration

Use the Export to Google Sheets extension with Todoist

The Export to Google Sheets extension allows you to document and report on work in progress. With this extension, you’ll be able to export active and completed tasks, including due dates, task priority, creation date, description, section, and assignee.

Set up the extension

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com or the desktop apps.
  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Click Integrations in the side menu.
  • Click Browse at the top of the Integrations settings.
  • In the list of available integrations, select Export to Google Sheets.
  • Click Add.
  • Click Confirm. When running the extension for the first time, you’re asked to sign in to your Google account and for read-only access to application data.

Use the extension

  • Click the three dots icon in the top-right of any Todoist project. This opens the project menu.
  • Click Export to Google Sheets.
  • Use the checkboxes to select which task fields (including due date, priority, creation date, description, section, and assignee) to export and if you want to include all completed tasks.
  • Click Export.
Limitations

Running into issues while exporting your data to Google Sheets? Here are some of the known limitations with the extension.

If you’re exporting a project with a large number of active or completed tasks, the extension may time out and return an error screen. When this happens, wait for a few minutes for the export to complete, and check the output at Google Sheets. If, after an extended period of time, the export has not appeared, get in touch with us for help.

Any active recurring task is considered as uncompleted by this integration. Only after you choose to complete it forever, will it show up as a completed task.

Remove the extension

  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Integrations.
  • Click Export to Google Sheets.
  • Select Remove.
  • Click Remove to confirm.

Use the Trello Power-Up with Todoist

Trello Power-Ups allow you to add additional features to the integrations you use with Trello. By adding a Power-Up for your integration between Todoist and Trello, you’ll be able to easily create Todoist tasks from your Trello cards with a single click.

Warning

There’s currently no official import tool to transfer your data from Trello into a Todoist account. If you’re looking to use Todoist in a similar way to how you use Trello, try the Board view feature.

Set up the Power-Up

  • Go to Trello’s site for the Power-Ups.
  • Click Add Power-Up.
  • Select the board for which you want to enable the Power-Up in the dropdown menu.
  • Click Add.
  • The Power-Up is now enabled! Click Go to board to start adding tasks.

Use the Power-Up

After adding the Todoist Power-Up to your Trello board, you’ll find an Add to Todoist button on each of your cards. This will send a task straight to your Todoist Inbox.

  • Open a card on your Trello board.
  • Click Add to Todoist on the right-hand side of the card.
  • If this is your first time using the Power-Up, you’ll be asked to sign in to Todoist and allow access. The Power-Up will add a task straight to your Todoist Inbox with the name of the card as the task name. Any other card details, like the due date or label, aren’t included in the task. You’ll need to add these manually to the task in Todoist.

Quick tip

Whenever you want to go back to your Trello card, click the link in the name of your Todoist task. This will open the card on your Trello board.

Remove the Power-Up

If you no longer want to use the Power-Up, here’s how to remove it from your board:

  • Open your Trello board.
  • Click the Todoist icon in the board menu. This will open the Power-Up menu.
  • Click Disable. The Power-Up will now be removed from the board and will no longer appear on your cards.

Create more workflows

If you want to create more workflows between Trello and Todoist, use one of these third-party integrations:

Notifications & Connection

Troubleshoot connection issues with Todoist

A blank screen, the infinite loading wheel, a jumble of formatted text – a few examples of connection issues that could keep you from accessing Todoist and getting your work done. Here are several possible reasons for these connection issues, along with suggestions to resolve them.

Limitations

There may be network-related limitations in place that are keeping you from accessing Todoist. Here’s how to work around them:

Corporate networks

If you’re using a corporate network, your IT department may have implemented restrictions on the websites you can access, Todoist included. Consider reaching out to them to request access to Todoist.

Country restrictions

If you’re traveling to a country that has restrictions on certain websites, Todoist may not load for you because of the country-specific sanctions in place. You can use your preferred VPN service to access Todoist.

If you’ve ruled these limitations out, and you’re still having trouble logging in or connecting to Todoist, here are several suggestions:

Check your internet connection

Your internet connection may be unstable or experiencing temporary issues. Check your internet connection using speed test checks like Fast or Ookla. Then, try accessing other websites or apps. If you can’t access any website, use an alternative internet connection or get in touch with your internet service provider for help.

Open Todoist in an incognito or private window

Some connection issues come from browser settings or extensions rather than Todoist itself. Open Todoist in an incognito or private browser window to test this. If Todoist works there, the issue is likely with your browser settings or extensions. Try disabling extensions next before clearing your browser cache.

Disable browser extensions or plugins

Your favorite browser extension or plugin might be in conflict with the Todoist web app. To check this, disable browser extensions or plugins one by one, reloading the Todoist web app each time to see if the issue is resolved. If you identified the problematic extension or plugin, consider removing or updating it.

Clear browser cache and cookies

Web browsers store some web app content locally to optimize performance. This is commonly referred to as caching. However, incorrectly cached items may cause misformatted pages or prevent you from accessing Todoist. Clear your browser’s cache and cookies, then try reloading the app.

Clearing your browser cache and cookies can remove locally stored, unsynced changes. If you’ve recently made changes to tasks while offline, make sure Todoist has finished syncing before clearing. If you’re unsure, troubleshoot syncing issues in Todoist first.

Add Todoist to the web browser safe list

If you’ve applied security measures to your web browser, these may block access to your Todoist account. Add Todoist to your web browser safe list to stay secure and get work done.

  • Click the three dots icon. This opens the menu.
  • Click Settings.
  • Select Privacy and security.
  • Click Third-party cookies.
  • Scroll to the Sites allowed to use third-party cookies section and click Add.
  • Type [*.]todoist.com and click Add.
  • Type [*.]cloudfront.net and click Add.
  • Reload the browser.
  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com.
  • Open Firefox’s Settings.
  • On the left, select Privacy & Security.
  • Under Cookies and Site Data, click the ManageExceptions… button.
  • Type todoist.com and click Allow.
  • Type cloudfront.net and click Allow.
  • Click Save Changes.
  • Reload the browser.
  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com. There’s no option to safe list third-party sites on Safari. You can only activate cookies for every third-party site like Todoist, or completely block third-party cookies.

Read more about managing cookies on Safari.

There’s no option to safe list third-party sites on Microsoft Edge. You can only activate cookies for every third-party site like Todoist, or completely block third-party cookies.

Read more about how and why Microsoft Edge works this way.

Turn off firewall or antivirus software temporarily

Firewall or antivirus software may be blocking your access to the Todoist web app. Temporarily disable them and try accessing the app again. If the issue’s resolved, allowlist todoist.com or add it as an exception in your firewall or antivirus software settings.

Get in touch

If you’ve followed all these suggestions, and you’re still having trouble accessing Todoist, get in touch with us with the following information:

  • Web browser and version
  • Operating system and version
  • Exact error message you’re seeing, or a screenshot of the page

Troubleshoot notifications not received from Todoist

Are you having trouble with your notifications? Did you add a reminder to your task, but it’s not showing up on your device?

If you’re not receiving notifications from Todoist, follow these troubleshooting steps and you’ll have your notifications pop up in no time.

Limitations

There may be device-specific limitations that are keeping you from receiving Todoist notifications. Here are the most common limitations:

Focus Assist in Windows blocks Todoist notifications by default. If you want to receive notifications in Priority mode, click Windows Settings > System > Focus Assist > Customize your priority list > Add an app. Then, add Todoist.

Restart both Todoist and your device

  • Log out of Todoist on your device. Then, log back in.
  • Turn your device off, then back on.

Update Todoist to the latest version

Version updates may include fixes and improvements to Todoist features, like notifications.

Learn how to update Todoist to the latest version based on the device or platform.

Keep Todoist open

Select Platform:

If you’re using Todoist on a web browser, make sure it’s open in at least one browser tab.

If you’re using Todoist on a desktop app, make sure you’re logged in and the app is open or minimized. Don’t close the app.

If you’re using Todoist on a mobile app, make sure you’re logged in and the app is open or minimized. Don’t quit the app.

For macOS: Reset notifications

If notifications aren’t received when using Todoist for macOS, reset the notification settings:

  • Check that Todoist for macOS is on the latest version.
  • Open System Settings.
  • Select Notifications from the side menu.
  • Scroll down to find Todoist.
  • Right-click Todoist and select Reset Notifications… This reverts Todoist notifications to the default settings.

Turn off app blockers and Do Not Disturb mode

If you’re using app blockers or app cleaners, quit these apps to turn them off.

If your device has Do Not Disturb mode, and you want to receive Todoist notifications while it’s turned on, follow the steps associated with your device and platform:

Select Platform:

Follow Apple’s instructions to turn off Focus on macOS.

Follow Microsoft’s instructions to turn off Do Not Disturb on Windows.

Follow Apple’s instructions to turn off Focus on iOS.

Follow Google’s instructions to turn off Do Not Disturb.

Turn off battery optimization for Todoist

Select Platform:

Follow Apple’s instructions to turn off battery-saving mode.

Follow Microsoft’s instructions to turn off battery-saving mode.

Follow Apple’s instructions to turn off battery-saving mode.

Follow Google’s instructions to turn off battery-saving mode.

Check if Todoist notifications are enabled for your device

Select Platform:

Each browser has its own steps to turn on web notifications. Click the browser you’re using for the latest instructions:

  • Chrome
  • Firefox
  • Edge
  • Safari Quick tip

Make sure you’ve also turned on notifications in your operating system’s settings.

  • Click the Apple icon in the top-left.

  • Select System Preferences.

  • Select Notifications.

  • Select Todoist.

  • Make sure either Banners or Alerts is selected. When using Todoist for macOS, make sure you’re allowing notifications in Focus.

  • Press the Windows key.

  • Select Settings.

  • Click System.

  • On the left, select Notifications.

  • Make sure that Get notifications from apps and other senders is turned on.

  • Scroll down until you find Todoist and make sure it’s turned on. Quick tip

You can customize the type of notifications you’d like to see in Todoist.

  • Tap the Settings app of your Apple device.
  • Tap Notifications.
  • Scroll down and select Todoist.
  • Toggle Allow Notifications and Time-Sensitive Notifications on. These settings ensure you receive push notifications without delay.
  • Select one or more alerts to display Todoist notifications. If you’re not receiving push notifications specifically for location reminders, check the Location Services settings on your device as well.

Quick tip

When using Todoist on iOS, you should also:

  • Make sure you have background refresh enabled for Todoist by opening your device’s Settings app, selecting Todoist, then check if the Background App Refresh option is enabled.
  • If you regularly use mobile data (rather than WiFi), you should make sure that mobile data is enabled for Todoist: Open your Settings app, select Mobile Data, then scroll down until you find Todoist.
  • Tap the Settings app of the Android device.
  • Select Notifications.
  • Tap App notifications.
  • Select Todoist.
  • Toggle All Todoist notifications on. Note

These steps may differ depending on your Android device’s settings. If you’re not sure where the setting is located or if the interface is different, contact your device manufacturer.

Then, send a test notification:

  • Open the Todoist web app or desktop app.
  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Click the Reminders tab.
  • Click either Test web (on the web app) or Test desktop (on the desktop app). If you’re testing push notifications on your mobile device, click Test mobile.

Check if your reminders are set up correctly

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Click the Reminders tab.
  • Turn on one or more notification types to receive:
    • Desktop notifications to get notifications on the desktop computer.
    • Mobile notifications to get notifications on the mobile device.
    • Emails to receive a reminder through the account email address. Quick tip

If you want to get a notification for all tasks with a due time, scroll up to the Automatic reminders section in the Reminders tab. Then, choose when Todoist will send an automatic reminder.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Tap Reminders.
  • Tap Remind Me Via, select the type of notification you’d like to receive:
    • Mobile Notification to get notifications on your mobile device.
    • Desktop Notification to get notifications via your computer’s operating system.
    • Email to receive a reminder through the account email address. Quick tip

When you snooze a reminder on iOS, you can choose to be reminded again at a later time. Tap When snoozed… and select an interval from the list.

To get a reminder for all tasks with a due time, tap Automatic Reminders and select a relative time from the list.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Select Reminders.
  • Tap Remind Me Via, select the type of notification you’d like to receive:
    • Mobile push notification to get notifications on your mobile device.
    • Desktop push notification to get notifications via your computer’s operating system.
    • Email to receive a reminder through the account email address. Quick tip

When you snooze a reminder on Android, you can choose to be reminded again at a later time. Tap When snoozed… and select an interval from the list.

To get a reminder for all tasks with a due time, tap Send automatic reminders… and select a relative time from the list.

Update outdated task links in Todoist

Todoist has improved task links with a new format. While old links still work, they will soon expire. Todoist updates these automatically where possible, but links saved outside the app like bookmarks or iOS shortcuts require manual updates. If a link is outdated, Todoist will prompt you to update it so you can continue accessing your tasks.

Update task links

If you open an outdated task link, you’ll see a dialog in Todoist that prompts you to choose one of the following:

  • Click the Copy link button to replace the old one.
  • Add a Todoist task as a reminder to update the task link later. Replace the outdated link with the new link before saving it or sharing it with your team.

If you prefer to update the task link later, Todoist will add a task for it to your Inbox. This option pre-fills Quick Add with the following:

Task name:

Update link

Task description:

Replace old link with the updated URL

Update the Todoist iOS widget

If you have a Todoist widget that uses outdated links, and you’ll interact with that widget, Todoist for iOS will open and show a dialog that prompts you to choose one of the following:

  • Click the Show home screen button, so you can remove and re-add the widget.

  • Add a Todoist task to update the widget for later. If you can’t find a Todoist widget, check the following locations:

  • Home Screen

  • Lock Screen (iOS 16+)

  • Today View (the left-most screen)

  • Smart Stacks

  • Focus Modes

  • Control widgets (Control Center, Lock Screen, and the Action Button) Remove and re-add the Todoist widget to your home screen, so you have a clear and accurate picture of your task lists.

If you prefer to remove and re-add the widget later, Todoist will add a task for it in your Inbox. This option pre-fills Quick Add with the following:

Task name:

Update widget

Task description:

Remove and re-add the Todoist widget

Update the Todoist shortcut on iOS

If you have a Todoist shortcut that uses outdated links, you’ll see a dialog in Todoist that prompts you to choose one of the following:

  • Click the Open Shortcuts button. This opens the Shortcuts app for iOS, so you can delete and re-add the shortcut.
  • Add a Todoist task to update the shortcut for later. Delete and re-add the Todoist shortcut to the Shortcuts app for iOS, so it runs smoothly whenever you need it.

If you prefer to delete and re-add the shortcut later, Todoist will add a task for it in your Inbox. This option pre-fills Quick Add with the following:

Task name:

Update shortcut

Task description:

Delete and re-add shortcut using Todoist.

Set up two-factor authentication for your Todoist account

You want to feel safe and secure in everything you do in life, particularly when it comes to your personal data. That’s why we’ve implemented several security measures to protect your Todoist account.

About two-factor authentication

Two-factor authentication or 2FA adds an extra layer of security to your account by requiring you to use a third-party authentication app when logging into your account.

After entering your account email address and password, Todoist will ask for a 6-digit one-time passcode. Your preferred third-party authentication app generates this passcode for you.

Melis · Customer Experience

If you don’t already have an authentication app, like Authy or Google Authenticator, make sure to install one on your mobile device.

If you’ve enabled 2FA on your account, you’ll be prompted to use a one-time passcode for a variety of actions:

  • Log in to your Todoist account
  • Turn off 2FA
  • Change your email address in your Todoist account
  • Download a backup of your account
  • Delete your Todoist account
  • View your recovery codes Todoist supports authentication apps installed on your mobile device. If you don’t already have an authentication app, like Authy or Google Authenticator, make sure to install one before setting up 2FA for your account.

Turn on two-factor authentication

Select Platform:

  • Log in to Todoist in a browser.
  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Click Settings.
  • Select Account in the left-hand menu.
  • Click the toggle below Two-factor authentication.
  • Scan or copy the secret code you see to your authentication app.
  • Enter the verification code. You’ll see a confirmation notice that verification is complete.
  • Click Continue in the bottom-right side.
  • Scroll down to Save your recovery codes and click Copy all codes. Save these in a secure place, so you can get back in if you ever lose access to your account.
  • Click Continue.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Select Account.
  • Tap the Require 2FA toggle.
  • Copy the secret code you see to your authentication app.
  • Enter the verification code in Todoist.
  • Tap Done in the top-right corner, and you’ll see Verification successful.
  • Scroll down to Save your recovery codes and tap Copy all codes. Save these in a secure place, so you can get back in if you ever lose access to your account.
  • Tap Done in the top-right corner.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Select Account.
  • Tap the Two-factor authentication toggle.
  • Copy the secret code you see to your authentication app.
  • Enter the verification code in Todoist, and you’ll see Verification successful.
  • Scroll down to Save your recovery codes and tap Copy all codes. Save these in a secure place, so you can get back in if you ever lose access to your account.
  • Tap Done in the top-right corner. 2FA is now enabled on your account. If you don’t see your 2FA settings, learn how to troubleshoot this issue.

Note

If someone tries to sign in to your Todoist account after you’ve set up 2FA, you may still receive a login alert about an unauthorized attempt. However, without the 2FA code, they won’t be able to access your account.

Turn off two-factor authentication

Select Platform:

  • Log in to Todoist in a browser.
  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Click Settings.
  • Select Account in the left-hand menu.
  • Scroll down to Two-factor authentication and toggle the setting Off.
  • Enter a one-time passcode from your authentication app.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Select Account.
  • Use the toggle under Two-factor authentication to disable 2FA.
  • Enter a one-time passcode from your authentication app.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Select Account.
  • Use the toggle to the right of Two-factor authentication to turn off 2FA.
  • Enter a one-time passcode from your authentication app. Warning

If you no longer have access to your third-party authentication app to get the one-time passcode, learn how to request a recovery code. Then, toggle two-factor authentication off, click Click here to use a recovery code instead, and enter the code to turn off 2FA.

Strengthen your Todoist account password

Are you trying to log in to Todoist, but you’re running into an error message about your password being exposed in a data breach, or not passing our security checks?

When logging in to your Todoist account, or when changing your password, your email address and password are checked against the Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) database. This service tracks all publicly disclosed data breaches. If your email and password combination is found in these breaches, it’s considered insecure and the error message will appear when trying to log in to the account. Here’s how to strengthen your Todoist account password and protect your data:

Note

You can check if your credentials have been compromised using either the HIBP: Email or HIBP: Pwned Passwords databases. If your email or password is found in one of these data breaches, an error message will appear in Todoist when you log in, reset your password, or sign up for an account.

Choose a strong password

When choosing the new password, we recommend the following best practices:

  • Use a strong password of at least eight characters.
  • Use a good mix of letters, numbers, and special characters.
  • Check the HIBP database if the password is secure.
  • Save your new password in a password manager, so you always have access to your account. Stef · Customer Experience Specialist

Most password managers include a password generator that can create strong passwords for you. After selecting your password, the password manager will automatically save the password, so you can get on with your day!

Change your account password

To make sure you got all the new locks in place, follow these steps:

Select Platform:

If you’re not able to log in because your email address and password were found in a breach, click Forgot your password? under the Log in button to reset your password.

  • Open your Account settings.

  • Click Change password.

  • Enter your current account password.

  • Enter your new account password.

  • Enter the new password again to confirm.

  • Click Change password. If you’re not able to log in because your email address and password were found in a breach, tap Forgot your password? under the Log in button to reset your password. This will open a new tab in your mobile browser.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.

  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.

  • Select Account.

  • Tap Change Password.

  • Enter your current account password.

  • Enter your new account password.

  • Enter the new password again to confirm.

  • Tap Done. If you’re not able to log in because your email address and password were found in a breach, tap Forgot your password? under the Log in button to reset your password. This will open a new tab in your mobile browser.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.

  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.

  • Select Account.

  • Tap Password.

  • Enter your current account password.

  • Enter your new account password.

  • Enter the new password again to confirm.

  • Tap the send icon.

Get help

If you’re still having issues with logging in after adding a strong password for your Todoist account, get in touch with us.

Todoist privacy and security

Your Todoist account holds your tasks, projects, and personal data. Here’s how we protect your information and how you can keep your account safe.

How is my data protected?

All data transmitted between your device and Todoist is encrypted using TLS (Transport Layer Security). Data at rest is also encrypted. Todoist data is stored on secure cloud infrastructure, and Doist complies with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and other applicable data protection laws.

For full details on our security measures, data storage locations, compliance certifications, Data Processing Agreement (DPA), and sub-processor list, visit our Trust Center.

How do I secure my account?

There are a few steps you can take to keep your account safe:

  • Use a strong, unique password. Here’s how to strengthen your Todoist account password.
  • Add an extra layer of protection with two-factor authentication (2FA). Learn how to set up two-factor authentication.
  • Lost access to your authenticator app or can’t log in? Check out how to troubleshoot two-factor authentication.

Can I export or delete my data?

You have full control over your data:

  • Todoist creates automatic daily backups you can download at any time. Check out how to download or restore backups.
  • You can delete your account and all associated data whenever you’d like. Here’s how to delete your Todoist account.

I can’t log in to my account

If you’re having trouble logging in, try these steps:

  • Reset your password and check your inbox (including spam) for the reset email.
  • Make sure you’re using the correct email address. If you signed up with Google or Apple, use that method to log in instead.
  • Try logging in via the web app to rule out device-specific issues. For more help, check out how to log in or out of Todoist.

Why am I being asked to reset my password?

Todoist checks email addresses and passwords against the Have I Been Pwned database during login. This is a database that tracks publicly disclosed data breaches. If your credentials appear in a known breach, Todoist considers that login insecure and will ask you to reset your password.

To resolve this:

  • Reset your password.
  • Choose a strong, unique password you don’t use anywhere else. You can also check whether your email or password appears in any known breaches on the same site. If your password is listed there, you won’t be able to use it to log in to Todoist.

What should I do if I suspect unauthorized access?

If you notice unexpected activity on your account or believe someone else may have gained access, take these steps to secure it:

  • Log in to your Todoist account via the web app at todoist.com.
  • Click your avatar in the top-left corner.
  • Go to Settings.
  • Select the Integrations tab > Developer.
  • Click Issue a new API token and confirm by clicking OK. This logs you out of all active sessions across all devices. You’ll need to log back in with your password afterward.

Once you’ve done that, strengthen your Todoist account password to make sure you’re using something unique to Todoist. We recommend using a password manager to generate a unique, hard-to-guess password.

If you no longer need your account or didn’t create one intentionally, you can delete your Todoist account.

Someone created an account with my email

Todoist requires email verification before an account can be activated. If someone used your email to create an account, it can’t be accessed or used without clicking the verification link sent to your inbox.

If you didn’t verify the account, it remains inactive and no one can log in or use it. If you’d like the inactive account removed entirely, get in touch with us and we’ll delete it for you.

I can’t access the email linked to my account

If you’re still logged in to Todoist on any device, you can change your email in Settings > Account. Follow the steps in change your email address.

If you’re not logged in on any device, get in touch with us and we can verify your identity through the payment method associated with the account. Be ready to confirm details like the last 4 digits of your card, recent charge amount, or plan name. Free plan users without access to their email will need to create a new account with a different email address.

Troubleshoot missing projects, tasks, comments, or other data

If you notice missing data, like projects, tasks, or comments, this is usually a sync issue. Your data is safe but may not have synced to the device you’re currently using.

Follow the steps in troubleshoot syncing issues in Todoist to resolve it. You can also download or restore backups at any time since Todoist saves daily backups automatically.

Is this email really from Todoist?

Todoist only sends emails from addresses ending in @todoist.com or @doist.com. If you receive a suspicious email claiming to be from Todoist, don’t click any links in it. Get in touch with us with a screenshot and we’ll confirm whether it’s legitimate.

How do I report a security vulnerability?

If you’ve found a security vulnerability in Todoist, we’d like to hear about it. Check out our bug bounty policy for details on how to submit a report and what’s in scope.

Learn more

Visit our Trust Center for detailed information on compliance certifications, infrastructure, data processing practices, and our security policies.

If you have questions about security, privacy, or need help with your account, get in touch with us. We’re happy to help.

Productivity

Use Beeminder with Todoist

Beeminder is an app that tracks your progress towards goals on Android and iOS.

With this integration, you can track Todoist tasks in Beeminder and ensure you’re meeting your goals.

Setting up the integration

  • Log in on Beeminder.
  • On the Beeminder homepage, click on Todoist.
  • Click on the Connect to Todoist button.
  • In the new window that opens, click on Agree to grant Beeminder permission to access your Todoist data.
  • Next, define your pledge by selecting how many tasks you want to complete per day, week, month or year.
  • (Optional) Select whether you only want this goal to apply to tasks in a specific project or with a specific label.
  • Click on Next.
  • Enter a name for your goal.
  • (Optional) Add a description.
  • Click on Continue.
  • Pledge your money (Beeminder will charge you if you don’t meet your goals).
  • Click on Add Credit card.
  • In the window that opens, enter your card details and click on Add Card.

Using the integration

To get a full and up-to-date overview of all the ways you can use Beeminder with Todoist, please visit Beeminder’s page for Todoist.

FAQ

If you no longer wish to use Todoist with Beeminder, here’s how to remove the integration:

  • Open Beeminder.

  • Click on your name or on the bee icon in the top-right corner.

  • Click on the name of the goal that you want to remove.

Use Klipfolio with Todoist

Setting up the integration

First, get your Todoist API token on todoist.com:

Next, set up the connection on klipfolio.com:

Use the Habit Tracker extension with Todoist

Build strong habits and improve your consistency with the Habit Tracker extension.

After completing your recurring tasks, view your progress in the task description. Your completion history is in the task comments, so you can appreciate your hard work and celebrate small wins.

The Habit Tracker tracks tasks with either a daily or specific recurring due date. If a task becomes overdue, is postponed, or rescheduled to another day, the Habit Tracker resets your streak.

Set up the extension

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com or the desktop apps.
  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Click the Integrations tab.
  • Click Browse at the top of the Integrations settings.

Use the extension

  • Click any task to open the task view.
  • Click the three dots icon in the top-right corner of the task view.

Remove the extension

  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Click the Integrations tab.
  • Click Habit Tracker.
  • Select Remove.
  • Click Remove to confirm.

Noteworthy

  • Avoid adding your own description to a tracked task. The Habit Tracker extension will override it.
  • Every new streak starts at zero. There’s no option to set the number when the streak begins.
  • If Vacation mode is turned on, the Habit Tracker will keep tracking your progress.

Use the Task Helper extension with Todoist

Do you ever find yourself doing some pretty boring and repetitive work when managing your tasks and sub-tasks? It’s a dirty job, but somebody has to do it, right? Or something for that matter, like this Task Helper extension!

The Task Helper extension has a collection of three automated task actions, all designed to speed up your work and save you from having to perform tedious manual actions over and over again. You can find these helpers in the task menu:

  • Apply a task’s attributes to all sub-tasks.
  • Create a follow-up task upon task completion.
  • Turn a task into an uncompletable task.

Set up the extension

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com or the desktop apps.
  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Click Integrations in the side menu.
  • Click Browse at the top of the Integrations settings.
  • In the list of available integrations, select Task Helper.
  • Click Add.
  • Click Confirm. When running the extension for the first time, you’re asked to grant access to read and write application data.

Use the extension

  • Click any task to open the task view.
  • Click the three dots icon in the top-right corner of the task view.
  • Click Task Helper.
  • Select one of the three Task Helper task actions:
    • Toggle uncompletable task: To turn a task into an uncompletable task.
    • Complete and create follow-up: You will be able to select what attributes you’d like to add to the follow-up tasks, like due dates, labels, and task assignee.
    • Apply attributes to sub-tasks: Like due dates, labels, priority, and task assignee.

Remove the extension

  • Click Remove to confirm.

Productivity & Karma

Forward emails to Todoist

Turn your emails into Todoist tasks by forwarding them to a unique email address. You can forward emails to specific projects to create new tasks, or forward them to existing tasks to add them as comments. This helps you centralize your work without leaving your inbox.

Forward an email to a project to create a task

Turn your emails into Todoist tasks by forwarding them to a project. When you forward an email, the subject line will become the task name, and the body of the email will be added as an attachment in a comment.

Find a project’s email address

Select Platform:

  • Open a project or your Inbox on the sidebar.
  • Click the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Email tasks to this project.
  • Click Copy email.
  • Forward your email to the unique email address. Keita · Customer Experience Lead

Jump straight to Inbox Zero by using any of these email integrations to turn email into tasks. All from the comfort of your inbox.

Add task details in your email

You can also add dates, labels, priority levels, and assignee right from your email client. All you have to do is include any of these in either the subject or any place above your signature in the body of your email:

To schedule the task right away, add . For example, , <date 12/22>, , and , are all supported. You can use any of Todoist’s supported date and recurring date formats.

The word date is required when adding a date. For example, adding won’t work, but adding will.

To add an existing label, type @labelname. For example, @work, @email, or @5min. If you’re creating a new label, add this label first to Todoist.

To add a priority, simply add p1, p2, or p3.

To assign the task when forwarding the email to a shared project, add +firstname\ lastname of the assignee in the subject. For example, if you’re collaborating with Amy Jones and you want to assign a task to her, simply add +Amy\ Jones.Prefix matches work too, so you can use +Amy, providing they’re the only collaborator with that name.

If you forward an email with this subject

This Todoist task will be created

Join our next event! p1

A task called “Join our next event!” with priority 1, dated on Friday.

Fwd: Tomorrow’s meeting @work p2 +Amy Jones

A task called “Fwd: Tomorrow’s meeting”, with priority 2, dated tomorrow, assigned to Amy Jones, with the @work label.

Re: Office supplies @email p3

A task called “Re: Office supplies”, with priority 3, dated next Wednesday, with the @email label.

Use Email Assist in Todoist

Email Assist takes the heavy lifting out of converting your forwarded emails into actionable tasks. Instead of manually adding task details before forwarding or editing the task afterward, Email Assist reads your email content and does it for you, extracting the date and time and rewriting the task name into something clear and actionable.

Forward emails puts content into Todoist. Email Assist makes that content useful without extra effort from you.

For example, here’s what Todoist creates from the same forwarded email as-is, with and without Email Assist:

Without Email Assist

With Email Assist

Task name

Fwd: Updated invitation: 1:1 performance review - Evert + Hannah @ Wed Mar 18, 2026 8:30am - 9am (SAST) (Hannah Rae)

Attend updated 1:1 performance review with Evert

Date and time

Not set

Wednesday, 08:30

Task description

None

Meeting details and link added automatically

Comments

Email attachment and meeting link

Email attachment and meeting link

Note

Email Assist is part of Todoist Assist, Todoist’s AI-powered productivity suite. It’s available on Pro and Business plans only and isn’t included in the Pro Legacy plan. See pricing for more details.

To turn Email Assist on or off:

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Select Settings .
  • Go to the Advanced section of the General settings and toggle it on or off.
  • Or, when you get your project’s email address, toggle Email Assist on or off.
  • Open a project or your Inbox on the sidebar.
  • Tap on the three dots icon.
  • Select Email tasks to this project.
  • Toggle Email Assist on or off.

Forward an email to a task to create a comment

Forward emails to Todoist as comments — ideal for when you need to attach information to an existing task or project.

Quick tip

Any message you add in the email’s body before forwarding it will automatically turn into a comment.

Find a task’s email address

Select Platform:

  • Click the task to open the task view.

  • Click the three dots icon.

  • Select Add comments via email.

  • Click Copy email next to the email address provided. Use this email address to forward emails to the task.

  • Click the task to open the task view.

  • Click the three dots icon.

  • Select Email to this task.

  • Click Copy email next to the email address provided. Use this email address to forward emails to the task.

  • Click the task to open the task view.

  • Click the three dots icon.

  • Select Email to this task.

  • Click Copy email next to the email address provided. Use this email address to forward emails to the task.

Note

It’s not possible to forward emails directly to a section of a project. If this is something that would be useful to you, let us know and submit it as a feature request.

Introduction to Karma

Karma boosts your motivation to get things done on time. Every completed Todoist task gains you Karma points, and a step closer to new Karma levels.

Play

Check your Karma level

When you first sign up for Todoist, your Karma starts at the Beginner level. As you complete tasks or use advanced features, you gain points that’ll help you advance to the next level.

Karma points

Karma symbol

Karma level

0-499

Beginner

500-2499

Novice

2500-4999

Intermediate

5000-7499

Professional

7500-9999

Expert

10000-19999

Master

20000-49999

Grand Master

50000 and more

Enlightened

To check your Karma level:

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Select the Productivity view.
  • Click the Karma tab to see your current level, Karma points, and Karma Trend.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap your avatar at the top-left.
  • Select the Karma tab to see your current level, Karma points, and Karma Trend. Quick tip

Once you reach Karma Enlightenment, a new mystery theme will be unlocked on your account.

Track progress with Karma Trend

Your Karma Trend lets you see how you’ve accumulated Karma points over the last week. Your progress is illustrated as a line graph below your current Karma level, and updates automatically as you gain or lose Karma points.

Here’s a breakdown of the Karma Trend symbols:

Karma symbol

What it means

You added new tasks.

You completed tasks.

You used advanced features.

You reached your Daily or Weekly goals.

Earn Karma points

To advance to the next Karma level, you’ll need to earn Karma points. You earn points when you:

  • Add tasks.
  • Complete tasks on time.
  • Use advanced features such as labels, recurring dates, and reminders.
  • Reach self-set goals regarding the number of tasks you want to complete either daily or weekly.
  • Achieve ongoing “streaks” by meeting your daily or weekly goals consistently. Karma points are added throughout the day. The higher the Karma level you have, the more challenging it becomes to earn points.

Quick tip

Earn bonus Karma when you’ve reached your daily or weekly task goals. Todoist also tracks how many days or weeks you have attained your goals, and achieving ongoing “streaks” will add to your positive Karma.

Lose Karma points

You lose Karma points when you have tasks that are five or more days overdue. Make sure to complete your tasks on time, or reschedule tasks to a later date.

Change Karma settings

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Select the Productivity tab in the side menu.
  • Make the necessary changes to your Karma:
    • Set your daily or weekly task goals.
    • Turn goal celebrations on or off.
    • Select days of the week when you’d like to take a break.
    • Turn Vacation mode on or off.
  • Click Update to confirm.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap Settings at the top-right.
  • Select Productivity.
  • Make the necessary changes to your Karma:
    • Set your daily or weekly task goals.
    • Turn goal celebrations on or off.
    • Select days of the week when you’d like to take a break.
    • Turn Vacation mode on or off.
  • Tap back to Settings at the top-left.
  • Tap Done to confirm.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap Settings at the top-right.
  • Select Productivity.
  • Make the necessary changes to your Karma:
    • Set your daily or weekly task goals.
    • Turn goal celebrations on or off.
    • Select days of the week when you’d like to take a break.
    • Turn Vacation mode on or off.
  • Tap back to Settings at the top-left. Your changes are saved automatically.

Turn off task goals

If you don’t benefit from using the daily and weekly goals, you can turn them off by setting the goals to zero. The goals will always be completed and won’t get in your way.

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar in the top-left.
  • Click Settings.
  • Click Productivity.
  • Change Daily tasks to 0.
  • Change Weekly tasks to 0.
  • Click Update.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.
  • Tap Productivity.
  • Change the Daily Task Goal number to 0.
  • Change the Weekly Task Goal number to 0.
  • Tap Done.
  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Tap Productivity.
  • Tap Daily goal.
  • Change it to 0.
  • Tap OK.
  • Tap Weekly goal.
  • Change it to 0.
  • Tap OK. Note

Todoist checks your goals every time you complete a task. If you change the goal to a lower number in the middle of the day, and don’t complete any other task, your streak will still break.

Turn off Karma

If you don’t want the pressure of earning or losing points, here’s how to turn Karma off:

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Click Settings.
  • Click Productivity.
  • Toggle Todoist Karma off.
  • Click Update to confirm.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.
  • Tap Productivity.
  • Tap Use Karma to turn it off.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.
  • Tap Productivity.
  • Tap the Karma checkbox to turn Karma off.

Reset your Karma level

Need a fresh start? Although there’s no option to reset your Karma level in Todoist, get in touch with us and we’ll reset it for you. Your Karma will go back to the default score of 50 points.

Restore a broken streak

If your daily or weekly streak broke and you couldn’t keep it going (for example, due to illness, travel, or a technical issue), get in touch with us. We can restore your most recently broken streak.

A few things to keep in mind:

  • We can restore your streak up to three times per account.
  • We can restore only the most recently broken streak. Older streaks aren’t recoverable.
  • We can’t set custom streaks.
  • To help avoid future streak breaks, turn on Vacation mode while you’re away, or set your days off in your Karma settings.

Best practices for Karma

To reach Enlightenment and prevent losing your streak, follow these best practices:

  • Select your days off, so you don’t lose points when you know you can’t use Todoist on those days.
  • Turn Vacation mode on if you’re going to be away for longer periods of time. Your Karma and streaks remain intact, even when you don’t achieve your daily or weekly goals.
  • Remember to turn Vacation mode off once you’ve returned, so you can start gaining Karma points again.
  • Postpone tasks you can’t work on just yet. This reduces pressure and gives you a better sense of how much time is needed to complete specific tasks.

Get started

Embark on your journey to Enlightenment by discovering the workflows that fit your needs. Check out the Get started guides or get a head start with Todoist setups.

If you’re experiencing any issues with Todoist Karma, get in touch with us.

Search for completed tasks

While working on your project, you realize you need to review or reference tasks that were completed in the past. Here’s how to include completed tasks in your search:

Select Platform:

  • Click Search in the sidebar or press the slash / hot key.

  • Enter keywords relevant to the completed task.

  • Scroll down the search results.

  • Click Search completed tasks. You’ll see a list of active and completed tasks that match your search keywords. Active tasks are listed at the top of the results.

  • Tap Search at the bottom.

  • Enter keywords relevant to the completed task.

  • Tap the Tasks section.

  • Tap Search completed tasks. You’ll see a list of active and completed tasks that match your search keywords. Active tasks are listed at the top of the results.

  • Tap Search in the sidebar.

  • Enter keywords relevant to the completed task.

  • Tap the Tasks section.

  • Tap Search completed tasks. You’ll see a list of active and completed tasks that match your search keywords. Active tasks are listed at the top of the results.

  • Tap Search at the bottom.

  • Enter keywords relevant to the completed task.

  • Tap the Tasks section.

  • Tap Search completed tasks. You’ll see a list of active and completed tasks that match your search keywords. Active tasks are listed at the top of the results.

Note

Archived projects and tasks included in these projects won’t appear in the search results. To view them, you’ll need to first unarchive these projects. Searching for partial keywords won’t match completed tasks.

Narrow down your search

If you’re having trouble finding the right information, enter search queries in the search bar to narrow down your results by date, priority level, project and more. Here’s a rundown of some queries you can use in Todoist:

Search based on:

Search query

What it does

search: report

Shows all tasks that contain the word “report”

search: Christmas

Shows all tasks that contain the word “Christmas”

search: sky*

Shows all tasks that contain the characters “sky” using * as a wildcard

Use an asterisk () as a wildcard to match partial words. For example, search: sky shows all tasks that contain “sky”.

Search query

What it does

14 days

Shows all tasks scheduled in the next 14 days

-5 days

Shows all tasks scheduled in the previous 5 days

tomorrow

Shows all tasks scheduled for tomorrow

created after: -30 days

Shows all tasks created in the last 30 days

today at 11am

Shows all tasks scheduled for today at 11am

today & date before: today at 5pm

Shows all tasks scheduled for today before 5pm

date before: may 5

Shows tasks scheduled before May 5

date after: march 10

Shows all tasks scheduled after March 10

date after: in 90 days

Shows all that are scheduled after 90 days from today

overdue

Shows tasks that are overdue (this only refers to dates, meaning that tasks that are overdue by an hour or several hours will not be included in the search results)

recurring

Shows all tasks with a recurring date

-7 days & p1

Shows all tasks from the last 7 days that are priority 1

tuesday & assigned to:Mary S*

Shows all tasks scheduled on next Tuesday that are assigned to any collaborator whose first name is “Mary” and last name starts with an “S”

date after: in 60 days & date before: in 120 days

Shows all tasks scheduled after 60 days from today and before 120 days from today

7 days & !assigned

Shows any tasks scheduled in the next 7 days that are unassigned

no date & #Work

Shows any task without a date in the Work project

(today | overdue) & assigned to: Mary Smith

Shows all tasks that are either scheduled for today or are overdue and are assigned to any collaborator with the name “Mary Smith”

7 days & assigned to:John

Shows all tasks scheduled in the next 7 days and are assigned to any collaborator with the name “John”

deadline: today

Shows all tasks with a deadline for today

deadline after: yesterday & deadline before: in 14 days

Shows all tasks with a deadline within the next 14 days

deadline before: today

See all tasks with overdue deadlines

due before: sat

See all tasks with the date or deadline in the current working week

due after: May 5 or due after: 5/5

See all tasks that have a date or a deadline after a specific date

no date

See all tasks without a date

Search query

What it does

today & p1

Tasks due today with priority 1

tomorrow & p3

Tasks due tomorrow with priority 3

assigned to: John Smith & p1

Tasks assigned to John Smith with priority 1

When searching based on assignee, you’ll need to type the person’s exact name in Todoist. Partial matches won’t pull up any search results. To help with this, here’s a broad list of ways to search based on assignee:

Search query

What it does

assigned to: John Smith

Shows all tasks assigned to any collaborator with the name “John Smith”

assigned to: Mary*

Shows all tasks assigned to any collaborator whose first name is “Mary”

assigned to: B* King

Shows all tasks assigned to any collaborator whose first name starts with an “B” and last name is “King”

assigned to: John Smith & @waiting

Shows all tasks assigned to any collaborator with the name “John Smith” and have the label @waiting

(today | overdue) & assigned to: Amy May

Shows all tasks that are either due today or are overdue and are assigned to any collaborator with the name “Amy May”

7 days & assigned to: Becky K*

Shows all tasks due in the next 7 days and are assigned to any collaborator whose first name is “Becky” and last name starts with an “K”

assigned

Shows all tasks that have been assigned to anyone (yourself and others)

!assigned

Shows all tasks that aren’t assigned to anyone

assigned to: others

Shows all tasks that have been assigned to others

assigned by: Steven Gray

Shows all tasks assigned by Steven Gray

assigned by: me

Shows all tasks that you have assigned to others

shared

Shows all tasks in shared projects

You can use search to find active projects and sub-projects. You won’t be able to pull up archived projects.

Search query

What it does

#Work

Shows all the tasks in the “Work” project.

#*Work

Shows all the tasks in projects which name ends with “work”. For example, #Artwork, #Network, and #Work.

##Work

Shows all the tasks in the “Work” project and all its sub-projects.

##Work & tomorrow

Shows all the tasks in the “Work” project and all its sub-projects and due tomorrow.

##Housework & p1

Shows all the tasks in the “Housework” project and all its sub-projects that are priority 1.

7 days & #Work & assigned to: Mary Smith

Shows all tasks due in the next 7 days of the Work project that are assigned to any collaborator with the name “Mary Smith”.

Rikke · Customer Experience Specialist

If you need to search for a project with an emoji in its name, use an asterisk to replace the emoji. For example, #Welcome *.

Search query

What it does

/Bills

Shows all the tasks from all sections with the name “Bills” in their names, no matter the project.

For example, you would see tasks both from the section “Household Bills” in your “Home” project, as well as the section “Work Bills” in your “Work” project.

/Bills*

Shows all the tasks from all sections which name begins with “Bills”, no matter the project.

For example, if you have a section called “Bills to pay” and a section called “Bills to reimburse”, you will see tasks from both of these sections.

#Work & /Bills

Shows all tasks belonging to the section “Bills” in the project “Work”.

Quick tip

If you have a Todoist Pro or Business plan, you can save these searches as filters for easy access.

Best practices for search

When there’s just a ton of information to wade through, search can be your powerful ally. Here are some best practices when using search in Todoist:

Check your list of recent searches

If you remember searching for a task or project in the past, chances are those keywords are still in your list of recent searches. Todoist saves up to five keywords in the Recent searches list, so it’s easy to find them in the search results.

If you want to remove them, either click Clear to remove them all, or click the dismiss icon beside the keyword to remove it individually.

Use search queries

If you need to find items that match specific criteria, you can use search queries to narrow down your search results. For example, enter p3 to see all tasks marked as Priority 3. If you scroll down further, you’ll find other relevant search results that match the keyword.

Get in touch

Ready to super charge your search skills in Todoist? Let this be your companion guide when searching for tasks, projects, comments, and the like with as little time and effort on your part.

If you’re having trouble with your search queries, get in touch with us.

Turn on or off vacation mode in Todoist

While you’re on vacation, traveling, sick, or just taking a personal day, you shouldn’t have to worry about losing your Karma daily or weekly streaks.

Vacation mode lets you put your Todoist Karma on hold for as long as you need. Once it’s turned on, there’s no pressure to complete your daily goal for that day.

You can turn on or turn off vacation mode in your Productivity settings.

Use the Productivity view in Todoist

The Productivity view lets you see how many tasks you’ve completed on a daily or weekly basis, how much progress you’re making towards your goals, and how many Karma points you’ve accumulated.

Access the Productivity view

Here’s how to view your Productivity:

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Click your name to open Productivity.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap your avatar at the top-left to open Productivity.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap your avatar at the top-left to open Productivity.

View completed tasks

The first thing you’ll notice in Productivity is how many tasks you’ve completed in total, which is also a link to view all completed tasks. Click or tap this option to see which tasks you’ve completed lately.

View your Daily and Weekly goals

In the Daily tab, you can see how many tasks you’ve completed today and whether you’ve completed your daily goal. If you no longer want to track daily goals, go to the Productivity settings and set the value of the daily goal to 0 to turn it off.

In addition to daily goals, Todoist keeps track of your weekly goals. You can view these in the Weekly tab. See how many tasks you’ve completed this week and how much progress you’ve made towards your goal.

By default, your daily goal is 5 and your weekly goal is 25. However, you can change these at any time in Todoist, either through the Edit Goals link or your Productivity settings.

Quick tip

Peek at your daily goal progress by glancing at the small pie chart in the top-right corner of your account.

Below your goals, you can check out your streak. Your streak is the number of days or weeks in a row that you’ve achieved your goal. You’ll also see your longest streak to keep you motivated.

Completed Task Summary

To get an idea of which projects you’re working on most, you can look at a summary of tasks you’ve completed in the last 7 days.

Note

You can also see the task breakdown over the last 4 weeks in the Weekly tab.

The colors represent the colors of the projects where you completed tasks. The vertical gray line represents your daily goal.

Karma

As you complete tasks on time in Todoist, you’ll gain Karma points and achieve new Karma levels. You can see your current Karma points and level by selecting the Karma tab in Productivity.

Learn more about Karma points, and how you earn them.

Productivity and Karma Settings

Change your productivity and Karma settings from the Karma menu in Settings:

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Click Settings.

Use Todoist while offline

In Todoist, you can add, delete, or make changes to your tasks even without an internet connection. You’ll see the offline icon at the top-right is automatically activated the moment you disconnect from the internet. If you’ve checked off tasks or made changes, these sync automatically as soon as you’re back online, so you don’t lose your work.

Warning

Don’t close Todoist or shut down your computer before your offline changes have finished syncing to the Todoist servers. Quitting the Todoist app before the sync completes may lead to data loss.

Make sure you’re logged in to your Todoist account before going offline. Without doing so, you can’t access or make changes to your tasks or projects.

View Reporting in Todoist

Check your daily progress or trace back changes made to a task with Reporting. It gives you complete visibility into what you and your teammates have been working on in Todoist. Information is organized by date and filtered by project, person, or event type.

View account activity

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar at the top-left of Todoist.

  • Select Reporting. To filter activity, use the menus at the top of Reporting. You can filter by project, person, event type, workspace, or select a date range to view activity within a specific time period.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.

  • Tap your avatar at the top-left.

  • Tap your name to open Reporting. In the Productivity view, there are two ways to filter the logs:

  • To filter by event or collaborator (for a shared project), tap the filter icon at the top-right.

  • To filter by project, tap the project icon at the top. Note

Filtering by workspace or date range isn’t available in Reporting on iOS yet. Use the web or desktop app for these filters.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.

  • Tap your avatar at the top-left.

  • Tap your name to open Reporting. In the Productivity view, there are two ways to filter the logs:

  • To filter by event or collaborator (for a shared project), tap the filter icon at the top-right.

  • To filter by project, tap the project icon at the top. Note

Filtering by workspace or date range isn’t available in Reporting on Android yet. Use the web or desktop app for these filters.

Presets

When you open Reporting, you’ll see a filter preset showing tasks you’ve completed. You can also choose from a selection of other presets to quickly focus on the activity that matters most.

To switch between filter presets:

Select Platform:

  • Open Reporting.
  • Click the dropdown beside the Activity header.
  • Choose from the list of presets. Presets

What it shows

All activity

Shows activity logs across all workspaces, projects, collaborators, and events.

My completed tasks

Shows tasks you have completed.

Projects & Sections

Add a project, label, or filter to favorites in Todoist

Separate your high-impact tasks from the everyday noise by adding important projects, labels, and filters to your favorites.

When adding a Todoist project, filter, or label as a favorite, they’ll appear in a new Favorites section in the sidebar. Then, all your favorites will sync across all your devices.

Add a project to Favorites

Select Platform:

  • In the sidebar, click the three dots icon beside the project name to view more project actions.

  • Select Add to favorites from the menu. The project will appear in the Favorites section of the sidebar.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.

  • Swipe right on the project to add as a favorite.

  • Tap the heart icon. The project will appear in the Favorites section of the navigation.

Quick tip

Add a project to your favorites by using context menus.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap My projects to add a personal project as a favorite or tap on the Name of the workspace to add a workspace project as a favorite.
  • Tap the pencil icon at the top-right of the screen.
  • Tap the heart icon beside the project to add it as a favorite. The project will appear in the Favorites section of the navigation.

Add a filter or label to Favorites

Select Platform:

  • Click Filters & Labels in the sidebar.

  • Click the heart icon beside the filter or label you want to add to your favorites. Your filter or label will show up in the Favorites section of the sidebar.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.

  • Swipe right on the name of the filter or label you want to add to your favorites.

  • Tap the heart icon. Your filter or label will show up in the Favorites section of the project overview.

Quick tip

Add a label or filter to your favorites by using context menus.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Tap Manage filters or Manage labels.
  • Tap the heart icon beside the filter or label you want to add as a favorite. The filter or label will show up in the Favorites section of the project overview.

Remove a project from Favorites

Select Platform:

To remove a project from the Favorites section, right-click the project and select Remove from favorites.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Swipe right on the project to remove as a favorite.
  • Tap the heart strikethrough icon. Quick tip

You can also remove a project as a favorite using the context menu.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap My projects to remove a personal project as a favorite or tap on the Name of the workspace to remove a workspace project as a favorite.
  • Tap on the pencil icon in the top-right.
  • Tap the heart strikethrough icon beside the project to remove as a favorite.

Remove a filter or label from Favorites

Select Platform:

To remove a filter or label from the Favorites section, right-click the filter or label and select Remove from favorites.

  • Swipe right on the name of the filter or label to remove as a favorite.
  • Tap the heart strikethrough icon. Quick tip

You can also remove a filter or label as a favorite using the context menu.

  • Tap on Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Tap Manage filters or Manage labels.
  • Tap the heart strikethrough icon beside the filter or label to remove as a favorite.

Reorder favorites

Favorites are listed in the same order as they appear in your projects, labels and filters lists.

To change the order in the Favorites section, drag the project, filter, or label to the preferred location of their respective lists. The new order will reflect in the Favorites section.

However, you can’t change the order that the favorites categories will be listed: projects, labels and then filters.

Collaborate with friends or family in Todoist

Need to plan your friend’s 30th birthday party, assign the kids’ chores, or share a grocery list with your spouse? With these best practices, learn how to turn Todoist into the central place to share ideas, updates, and wins on any project with friends or family.

Quick tip

Are you in charge of work-related projects? Check out these best practices to collaborate with your team in Todoist.

Share your project

Select Platform:

  • Click the project from the sidebar.

  • Click Share at the top-right.

  • Enter the name or email address of the person to invite to the project.

  • Click Invite to confirm. If the person you’re inviting doesn’t already have a Todoist account, they’ll receive a project invite email with the option to sign up for a free account.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.

  • Open the project.

  • Tap the add person icon. If you’re already sharing the project, tap the group icon. You’ll see two options:

    • Share Link: lets you copy an invitation link to join the project. Share this with anyone you want to share the project with.
    • Invite via name or email: lets you invite someone to your project by adding their name or email address.

  • Tap Done to confirm. When you select Invite via name or email, choose an existing collaborator from the list or enter their name or email address in the To: field. Whoever you invite will always have the Can Edit permission.

Rachel · Customer Experience Specialist

Tap the red plus icon in the To: field to invite someone from your phone’s Contacts app.

  • Open the project from the sidebar.
  • Tap the add person icon. If you’re already sharing the project, tap the group icon. You’ll see two options:
    • Share Link: lets you copy an invitation link to join the project. Share this with anyone you want to share the project with.
    • Invite via name or email: lets you invite someone to your project by adding their name or email address.
  • Tap Done to confirm. When you select Invite via name or email, choose an existing collaborator from the list or enter their name or email address in the To: field. Whoever you invite will always have the Can Edit permission.

Rachel · Customer Experience Specialist

Tap the red plus icon in the To: field to invite someone from your phone’s Contacts app.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open the project.
  • Tap the add person icon. If you’re already sharing the project, tap the group icon. You’ll see two options:
    • Share Link: lets you copy an invitation link to join the project. Share this with anyone you want to share the project with.
    • Invite via name or email: lets you invite someone to your project by adding their name or email address.
  • Tap the send icon to confirm. When you select Invite via name or email, choose an existing collaborator from the list or enter their name or email address in the To: field. Whoever you invite will always have the Can Edit permission.

Everyone you share your project with will have full access to all the information, like tasks, comments, and file attachments. Likewise, they can add new tasks, assign tasks, complete tasks, add comments, and upload new files.

Share a parent project

If you share a parent project with someone, they won’t automatically have access to its sub-projects. You’ll need to send them a project invitation for each sub-project.

Assign a task

Delegate tasks by assigning them to members of the project. They’ll receive a notification about their assigned tasks through either email or push notifications.

Select Platform:

Assign a new task
  • Click the shared project from the sidebar.
  • Click Add task or open Quick Add.
  • Type the task name followed by the plus character. The assignee menu will appear with all people in the project.
  • Select the person’s name to assign the task.
Assign an existing task
  • Click the shared project from the sidebar.
  • Click the assignee icon next to the task name. The assignee menu will appear with all people in the project.
  • Select the person’s name to assign the task.
Assign a new task
  • Open a shared project.
  • Tap the Dynamic Add button.
  • Write the task name and enter the plus character. The assignee menu will appear with all people in the project.
  • Select the person’s name to assign the task.
Assign an existing task
  • Open a shared project.
  • Tap the task to open the task view.
  • Tap the Assignee chip.
  • Select the person’s name from the menu.
Assign a new task
  • Open a shared project.
  • Tap the Dynamic Add button.
  • Write the task name and enter the plus character. The assignee menu will appear with all people in the project.
  • Select the person’s name to assign the task.
Assign an existing task
  • Open a shared project.
  • Tap the task to open the task view.
  • Tap the Assignee chip.
  • Select the person’s name from the menu. Note

You can only assign a single person to a task in Todoist. We believe in the concept of having a Direct Responsible Individual, which ensures that a single person is always clearly responsible for any given task.

If you need to delegate a large task to more than one person, split it into sub-tasks and assign these to the right people or duplicate the task and assign it to different people.

Use comments to share information

Once you’ve assigned all the tasks in the shared project, take to the comment section to share information, attach files, or notify other people in the project. Those you’ve tagged to the comments will receive a notification through either email or push notifications.

Complete tasks and make progress

Complete tasks whenever work gets done, and celebrate your progress! 🎉Click the circle icon beside the task name to mark it as Done, so that other people in the project can focus on what’s next.

Unassign a task

A friend just informed you that they can no longer contribute to the project. With deadlines fast approaching, it’s best to unassign them from tasks and remove them from the shared project.

Select Platform:

Unassign someone from a task
  • Click the shared project from the sidebar.
  • Click the assignee icon next to the task name.
  • Select Unassigned. Quick tip

Save time by selecting multiple tasks and unassigning the person from all of them.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open the shared project.
  • Open the person’s assigned task. This opens the task view.
  • Tap the assignee and select Nobody. Quick tip

Save time by selecting multiple tasks and unassigning the person from all of them.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open the shared project.
  • Open the person’s assigned task. This opens the task view.
  • Tap the assignee and select Nobody. Quick tip

Save time by selecting multiple tasks and unassigning the person from all of them.

Remove someone from your shared project

After you’ve unassigned the person from all their tasks, it’s time to remove them from the project.

Select Platform:

  • Click the shared project from the sidebar.
  • Select Share.
  • Click View all to see the full list of people in the project.
  • Click their role and select Remove from project from the menu.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open the shared project.
  • Tap the group icon.
  • Tap the remove person icon beside the person’s name.
  • Tap Remove collaborator to confirm.
  • Open the shared project from the sidebar.
  • Tap the group icon.
  • Tap the remove person icon beside the person’s name.
  • Tap Remove collaborator to confirm.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open the shared project.
  • Tap the group icon.
  • Tap the remove person icon next to the person’s name.
  • Tap OK.

Keep your ever-growing personal project lists neat and organized with sub-projects. For example, you might create “parent” projects called “Home” and “Health” and then organize various sub-projects underneath each one.

Since sub-projects are only available for personal projects, use folders to organize your team projects instead!

Todoist currently supports sub-projects on three indent levels for personal projects. To turn a project into a sub-project:

  • At the top-right, tap the pencil icon.
  • Drag and drop any project to the right or left to change its indent level. Quick tip

If you’ve hit the three-indent limit, sections are a great alternative to break down these large projects.
