Download or restore backups in Todoist

Never worry about lost tasks, empty projects, or missing comments. With a paid plan, Todoist automatically creates backups of all your active projects, so you can easily restore them at any time.

Play

About backups

Todoist creates a full backup on days you’ve been active and made any changes to your account. Up to 21 backups are stored as ZIP files and created at midnight in your time zone. Your projects are backed up as CSV files, so it’s easy to export or import back into Todoist. Whenever Todoist creates a new backup, it automatically deletes the oldest backup.

Every Todoist backup includes the following:

  • Active projects and tasks
  • Dates and time
  • Descriptions
  • Task duration
  • Deadlines
  • Recurring dates, excluding start dates
  • Up to 500 comments per task
  • Links to file attachments Completed tasks and archived projects aren’t included in a backup.

Samara · Customer Experience Specialist

Can’t find a project or task? Check whether the project was archived rather than deleted, or open Reporting and filter tasks by project, person, event type, or date range. Although Reporting doesn’t log archived or deleted projects, it can help you trace missing tasks.

Check out our security policy to learn more about how we make sure your data is safe and secure in Todoist.

If you’re on Todoist Pro or Business and still can’t find your work, check if it’s available in a backup.

Download a backup

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Click Settings.
  • Open the Backups tab. If you’ve turned two-factor authentication on for your account, copy the one-time password from your authentication app to access your backups.
  • Click Download next to a backup. This downloads a ZIP file containing CSV files for each of your active projects.
  • Extract the contents of the backup to your computer. You can only access and download backups while using the Todoist web app or desktop apps.

Keita · Customer Experience Lead

Click Create Backup at the top of your backups tab to manually create a backup of all of your active projects.

Restore a backup

Select Platform:

  • Create a new project.
  • Click the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Import from CSV.
  • Drag your project CSV file to the upload window, or click Upload from your computer. All the active tasks, dates, comments, and file attachments from the project CSV file will appear in the new project. If you’re using a list, board, or Week view of the calendar layout, Todoist retains the layout in the new project.

You can only access and restore backups while using the Todoist web app or desktop apps.

Import or export a project as a CSV file in Todoist

If you’re switching from your previous task manager, or moving your Todoist projects elsewhere, you can quickly import or export project data as a CSV file. Use the CSV format guide below to cross-check any missing or incorrect data, then follow the steps to export or import your CSV file in Todoist.

Review the CSV file

If your project is saved as a CSV file, here’s how to check if your CSV file follows the right format, and then import it in Todoist.

Quick tip

Download this template and modify it to ensure that you don’t encounter any issues when importing your tasks.

Column

Content

Description

TYPE

task, section, or note (these are case-sensitive and should be written in lowercase)

Use task to add a task. Use section to add a section. Use note if you’re adding a comment to the task in the row above.

CONTENT

name of the task, name of the section, or content of the note

Type the name of the task if you’re adding a task.

(When creating a task, you can add labels by typing the @labelname as an addition to the name of the task.)

Type the name of the section if you’re adding a section.

Type the content of the note if you’re adding a comment.

DESCRIPTION

content of the task, section, or project description

Type the content of the task, section, or project description to add a description for each.

PRIORITY

1, 2, 3, or 4

Type 1 to add p1 to the task (highest priority).

Type 2 to add p2 to the task.

Type 3 to add p3 to the task.

Type 4 to add p4 to the task (lowest priority).

Leaving this cell empty will automatically add p1 to the task.

INDENT

1, 2, 3 or 4

Use 1 and the task will not be indented (meaning the task is a parent task).

Use 2 to indent the task to be a sub-task.

Use 3 to indent the task to be a sub-sub-task.

And so on.

Leaving this cell empty will set the task to not be indented.

AUTHOR

username (ID)

Add the username + user ID in brackets of the person that created the task.

For example, Evan (14781400).

Leaving this cell empty will automatically add your name and ID.

RESPONSIBLE

username (ID)

Add the username + user ID in brackets of the person that you’d like to assign this task to.

For example, Evan (14781400).

Leaving this cell empty will not add an assignee to the task.

DATE

date and time or recurring date and time

Add a date and time if you want to schedule the task. You can also set a recurring date.

If you leave this cell empty, no date will be assigned to the task.

DATE_LANG

Language code

Add the language code for the language of your Todoist app to set the date (if any). These are the official Todoist language codes:

da for Danish.

de for German.

en for English.

es for Spanish.

fi for Finnish.

fr for French.

it for Italian.

ja for Japanese.

ko for Korean.

nb for Norwegian.

nl for Dutch.

pl for Polish.

pt_BR for Brazilian Portuguese.

ru for Russian.

sv for Swedish.

zh_CN for Simplified Chinese.

zh_TW for Traditional Chinese.

TIMEZONE

Time zone

Add the time zone set for your Todoist account in Settings > General (for example: US/Eastern).

Leaving this cell empty will have Todoist automatically detect your time zone.

DURATION

Number that represents the duration of a task

Add the estimated number of minutes it takes to work on a task.

Leave this cell empty to not add a task duration.

DURATION_UNIT

minute or None

Specify the unit of measurement for the task duration.

If there’s no task duration, None will appear in this cell.

meta

view_style=board

Import the template in board layout.

DEADLINE

date

Add a deadline to this cell. If you leave this cell empty, no deadline will be assigned to the task.

DEADLINE_LANG

Language code

Add the language code for the language of your Todoist app to set the date (if any). These are the official Todoist language codes:

cs for Czech.

da for Danish.

de for German.

en for English.

es for Spanish.

fi for Finnish.

fr for French.

it for Italian.

ja for Japanese.

ko for Korean.

nb for Norwegian.

nl for Dutch.

pl for Polish.

pt_BR for Brazilian Portuguese.

ru for Russian.

sv for Swedish.

zh_CN for Simplified Chinese.

zh_TW for Traditional Chinese.

IS_COLLAPSED

TRUE or FALSE

Optional. Controls whether a section is collapsed or expanded. Use TRUE to collapse the section by default. Use FALSE to keep the section open. This column is not required for imports: if it’s not included, Todoist assumes all sections are open/expanded. This column is specific to sections.

Assign tasks in the CSV file

To assign tasks to someone as soon as you import the CSV file, you’ll need to fill the person’s name and user ID in the RESPONSIBLE column. Here’s how to find it:

  • Open the shared project.
  • Click the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Manage data.
  • Select Export as CSV.
  • Open the CSV file.
  • Copy the username and user ID in the RESPONSIBLE cell of the assigned task’s row.

Import your CSV file

After checking that your CSV file follows the right format, here’s how to import it into Todoist:

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com.
  • Create a new project or open an existing project.
  • Click the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Manage data.
  • Select Import from CSV.
  • Drag your CSV file to the upload window, or click Upload from your computer. Todoist will import all the tasks and task attributes from the CSV file automatically into the project. If you’re using a list, board, or Week view of the calendar layout, Todoist retains it in the new project.

Stef · Customer Experience Specialist

Upload your CSV file directly to the templates gallery, so it’s easy to recreate the same project and its tasks for next time.

Troubleshoot a CSV file import

If you’re having trouble with importing or exporting your CSV file, there may be issues with its format. Here’s what you can do to resolve them.

Limitations with CSV files

There are specific limitations when importing or exporting a project as a CSV file.

Completed tasks

Completed tasks aren’t included when exporting a project as a CSV file. If you need to include them and don’t need all task attributes, use the Export to Google Sheets extension. This CSV file excludes labels, deadlines, comments, attachments, and reminders, but it allows you to include your project’s completed tasks.

Start date of a recurring date

When exporting a project, the start date of a recurring date isn’t saved in the CSV file. For example, if you have a task that recurs every year starting January 31 and export it, the task’s date will be changed to every year.

Import size limitations

Each project supports up to 300 tasks. If your CSV includes more than 300 task rows, the import can’t be completed. Importing large numbers of tasks from a template or CSV file can also trigger multiple errors. In both cases, split the template or file into smaller chunks and import them one at a time.

Wrong encoding format

For Todoist to import the CSV file correctly, it has to be encoded using UTF-8 formatting.

Use UTF-8 encoding in Microsoft Excel
  • Open your CSV file in Microsoft Excel.
  • Click File in the top-left of your screen.
  • Select Save as…
  • Open the menu next to File format.
  • Select CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited) (.csv).
  • Click Save.
Use UTF-8 encoding in Numbers
  • Open your CSV file in Numbers.
  • Click File in the top-left of your screen.
  • Select Export to…
  • Select CSV…
  • Click Advanced options.
  • Open the drop-down menu next to Text Encoding.
  • Select Unicode (UTF-8).
  • Click Next.
  • Click Save after choosing a name and location for your file.
Use UTF-8 encoding in Notepad
  • Open your CSV file in Notepad.
  • Click File in the top-left of your screen.
  • Select Save as…
  • Select the following options:
    • Open the Save as type menu. Select All Files.
    • Open the Encoding menu. Select UTF-8.
    • Rename your file using the .csv extension. For example, if you want to name your file “Work”, save your file as Work.csv.
  • Click Save.
Jumbled text in a column

When opening your CSV file in Microsoft Excel, you may notice a large amount of text inside a single column. Here’s how to fix this:

  • Click column A to select the entire column.
  • Click the Data tab.
  • Click the Text to Columns option.
  • Select Delimited.
  • Click Next.
  • Select only the Semicolon box.
  • Click Finish to confirm.
Incorrect format

If the file you’re importing to Todoist doesn’t follow the correct format, you’ll see a prompt that the import failed and the project remains empty.

Make sure to review the CSV format and double-check that every cell in the CSV file has the correct content. Content (for example: task, section and note) written in the TYPE column are case-sensitive and should be written in all lowercase.

Undo a CSV file import

If a CSV file was imported successfully to Todoist, there’s no option to undo the process. As a workaround, bulk select and delete any task that was imported by mistake.

Export your project as a CSV file

  • Log in to Todoist at todoist.com.
  • Open an existing project.
  • Click the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Manage data.
  • Select Export as CSV. A CSV file of your project is created and saved automatically to your computer. This is an exact duplicate of the original project, and it includes task, section, and project descriptions, dates, time, comments, attachments, and more.

Note

Project templates are available in English, Spanish, German, Dutch, Italian, Polish, Turkish, Japanese, Portuguese, Czech, French, Korean, and Russian. If you’ll create a template using any other language, the template will be in English.

Introduction to projects

Todoist projects keep all your tasks organized so you can achieve your goals, whether they are large or small. If you are planning a 3-day trip, tracking a marketing campaign, or keeping a list of books to read, projects provide a dedicated space to focus. By grouping related tasks together, you can gain clarity and take control of your day-to-day productivity.

Play

Identify project types

Before you start building, it’s helpful to understand the two environments where your projects can live. This ensures your tasks are visible to the right people, and stay organized in the right place.

Feature or purpose

My projects

Team projects

Primary use

Personal tasks or private work

Collaborating with teammates

Ownership

Account owner

Team admins

Project visibility

Account owner

All admins and members can browse, preview, and join any visible team project. Guests can only access projects they’re invited to.

Working with external people

Share your personal project with friends and family

Share a team project with a guest

Public projects or View-only mode

Public projects

Public projects

Restricted access

Restricted by default

Restricted projects

Create a project

All big achievements begin with a single project. You can create a project to house specific tasks and even customize it with colors to make it stand out in your sidebar. Let’s start with creating your first project:

Select Platform:

Create a personal project
  • Click the plus icon next to My Projects.
  • Select Add project.
  • Give the project a name, then click the hashtag icon to choose its color.
  • Click Add project to confirm. Quick tip

If you’re on the Beginner plan, you can have up to 5 active projects at a time. To manage more, you can archive or delete old projects or upgrade to a paid plan. On the Pro plan, you can create up to 300 projects, and on the Business plan, up to 500 projects.

Create a team project

From the sidebar:

  • Click the plus icon next to your team name.

  • Select Project.

  • Give your project a name and a description.

  • You can also customize your project with a color, access, folder, and layout.

  • Click Add to confirm. From the workspace overview:

  • Click the plus icon at the top-right of your workspace overview and select Project, or click + Add project at the bottom of the project list.

  • Give the project a name, then click the hashtag icon to choose its color.

  • Add teammates by typing + followed by a name to choose an existing member, or an email address to invite someone who isn’t part of your team yet.

  • Toggle the lock icon on to limit the project to invited people only, or leave it off so everyone on your team can access it.

  • Click Add project to confirm. Quick tip

You can copy a list of project names from a document or email and paste it into the project name field. Each line of your pasted text becomes a separate project.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap the plus icon next to either My Projects or your team projects.
  • Select Add Project.
  • Give the project a name, and choose its color and preferred layout.
  • Tap Done at the top-right to confirm. Quick tip

When creating a team project, tap Access and choose whether to give full access or keep it as a restricted project.

Edit a project

Projects grow and change over time. Whether you need to color code team projects, or your teammate came up with an even better project name, here’s how to make these changes to your project:

Select Platform:

Change the project name
  • Click the three dots icon next to the project name.
  • Select Edit from the menu.
  • Enter the new project name.
  • Click Save. Quick tip

If you already have the project open in Todoist, click the project name at the top and make your changes. Then, click Save to confirm.

Change the project color
  • Click the three dots icon next to the project name.
  • Select Edit.
  • Select the color you want for your project from the Color menu.
  • Click Save.
Add or edit a project description

Give your project more context with a description that appears as a one-line preview below the project name. Hover your mouse over the preview to see the full description.

  • Open the project from the sidebar.
  • Click Add a description below the project name.
  • Type your description.
  • Click Save. You can highlight text in your description and use the toolbar to format it.

Quick tip

To edit an existing description, click it to open the editor, make your changes, then click Save. You can also click the three dots icon next to the project name, select Edit, and update the Description field.

Change the project name
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Swipe left on the project name.
  • Tap the pencil icon.
  • Enter the new name for the project in the Name field.
  • Tap Done to confirm. Quick tip

Use the project’s context menu to quickly change its name.

Change the project color
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Swipe left on the project name.
  • Tap the pencil icon.
  • Tap Color and choose a different project color. Quick tip

Use the project’s context menu to change the project color.

Add or edit a project description

Give your project more context with a description that appears as a one-line preview below the project name.

  • Open the project.
  • Tap the project name at the top.
  • Tap the text field and type your description.
  • Tap Save. Quick tip

You can also tap the three dots icon at the top-right and select Description.

Change the project name
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Scroll down the project list and tap Manage Projects.
  • Open the project.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Tap Edit.
  • Enter the new name for the project in the Name field.
  • Tap the checkmark icon at the top-right to save the changes.
Change the project color
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Scroll down the project list and tap Manage Projects.
  • Open the project.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Tap Edit.
  • Select the color for the project.
  • Tap the checkmark at the top-right to save the changes.
Add or edit a project description

Give your project more context with a description that appears as a one-line preview below the project name.

  • Open the project.
  • Tap the project name at the top.
  • Tap the text field and type your description.
  • Tap Save. Quick tip

You can also tap the three dots icon at the top-right and select Description.

Note

Project members with view-only access can read the project description but can’t edit it. Descriptions support up to 16,383 characters.

The project color shows next to the project name in your sidebar, and on your tasks in the calendar layout when you color tasks by project. Projects without a color set, including Inbox, show gray.

Copy a link to a project

There are times when you’ll want to copy a link to a project to share with others. Here’s how to grab your project’s unique link:

Select Platform:

  • Click a project from the sidebar.
  • Click the three dots icon at the top.
  • Select Copy link to project. The project link is copied to your clipboard automatically.

Quick tip

You can right-click a project from the sidebar and select Copy link to project.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open a project.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Copy Link to Project. The project link is copied to your clipboard automatically.

Quick tip

When looking at your projects list, touch and hold the project to open the context menu and select Copy Link to Project.

  • Tap the project from the sidebar.
  • Open a project.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Copy Link to Project. The project link is copied to your clipboard automatically.

Quick tip

When looking at your projects list in the sidebar, touch and hold the project to open the context menu and select Copy Link to Project.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open the project.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Copy link to project. The project link is copied to your clipboard automatically.

Duplicate a project

If you find yourself copying or sharing the same task lists with different people, you can save time and effort by duplicating a project. You can only duplicate one project at a time.

Select Platform:

  • Click the three dots icon next to the project name.
  • Select Duplicate.
  • Open the duplicated project in the sidebar. The project name starts with Copy of.
  • Change the project name. Quick tip

If you’re already working in a project, click the three dots icon at the top-right and select Duplicate to duplicate the project.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open a project.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Duplicate. You’ll see a confirmation notice at the bottom of the screen.
  • Tap Show to open the duplicated project. Quick tip

To use the context menu, press and hold the project name and select Duplicate.

  • Tap the menu icon at the bottom.
  • Open a project and tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Duplicate. You’ll see a confirmation notice at the bottom of the screen.
  • Tap Show to open the duplicated project. When you duplicate a project, Todoist quickly creates a copy of that project. You’ll see the words Copy of added to the project name to help differentiate it from the original project. You can easily change the duplicate project’s name at any time.

Here’s what’s included and not included when you duplicate a project:

INCLUDED

NOT INCLUDED

Project name and color

Task reminders

Project description

Completed tasks and archived sections

Chosen view

Project and task comments

Chosen sorting, grouping, or filtering options

Favorites. Add the project as a favorite.

Active sections, tasks, and sub-tasks (with respective dates, priorities and labels)

Sharing settings: a duplicated project is private by default. You can share it later.

Sub-projects: you can duplicate them individually the same way as parent projects.

Share a project

Productivity is often a team sport. You can invite people to any project to delegate tasks and stay updated on progress together.

Select Platform:

  • Click the project from the sidebar.

  • Click Share at the top-right.

  • Enter the name or email address of the person to invite to the project.

  • Click Invite to confirm. If the person you’re inviting doesn’t already have a Todoist account, they’ll receive a project invite email with the option to sign up for a free account.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.

  • Open the project.

  • Tap the add person icon. If you’re already sharing the project, tap the group icon. You’ll see two options:

    • Share Link: lets you copy an invitation link to join the project. Share this with anyone you want to share the project with.
    • Invite via name or email: lets you invite someone to your project by adding their name or email address.

  • Tap Done to confirm. When you select Invite via name or email, choose an existing collaborator from the list or enter their name or email address in the To: field. Whoever you invite will always have the Can Edit permission.

Rachel · Customer Experience Specialist

Tap the red plus icon in the To: field to invite someone from your phone’s Contacts app.

  • Open the project from the sidebar.
  • Tap the add person icon. If you’re already sharing the project, tap the group icon. You’ll see two options:
    • Share Link: lets you copy an invitation link to join the project. Share this with anyone you want to share the project with.
    • Invite via name or email: lets you invite someone to your project by adding their name or email address.
  • Tap Done to confirm. When you select Invite via name or email, choose an existing collaborator from the list or enter their name or email address in the To: field. Whoever you invite will always have the Can Edit permission.

Rachel · Customer Experience Specialist

Tap the red plus icon in the To: field to invite someone from your phone’s Contacts app.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open the project.
  • Tap the add person icon. If you’re already sharing the project, tap the group icon. You’ll see two options:
    • Share Link: lets you copy an invitation link to join the project. Share this with anyone you want to share the project with.
    • Invite via name or email: lets you invite someone to your project by adding their name or email address.
  • Tap the send icon to confirm. When you select Invite via name or email, choose an existing collaborator from the list or enter their name or email address in the To: field. Whoever you invite will always have the Can Edit permission.

Everyone you share your project with will have full access to all the information, like tasks, comments, and file attachments. Likewise, they can add new tasks, assign tasks, complete tasks, add comments, and upload new files.

Share a parent project

If you share a parent project with someone, they won’t automatically have access to its sub-projects. You’ll need to send them a project invitation for each sub-project.

Accept or ignore a project invitation

Other people can invite you to their projects too. When someone does, a notification appears in Todoist. Accept the invitation to join the project. You can see all your invitations in the Notifications tab.

You don’t have to accept an invitation. If you don’t recognize the person or the project, leave the invitation unaccepted and you won’t join.

Todoist can also accept project invites for you automatically, but only from people whose invites you’ve accepted before or from members of your Todoist team. To turn this on or off, see Accept project invites automatically.

Best practices for projects

Now that you’ve created your project, let’s add and organize your tasks. Below are best practices to help you make the most of a project in Todoist:

Quick Add tasks to your project

Load up your new project with every relevant task you can think of. Use Quick Add or press Add task at the bottom of the task list to add tasks directly to your project. It’s a brainstorm, there are no bad ideas!

Stacey · Customer Experience Specialist

Use Quick Add to quickly move the task to a project. Type # in the task name and enter the name of the project.

Organize with sections or folders

Break your project down into manageable chunks with sections. Add tasks or drag existing tasks to their relevant section.

If you’re working on a large team project with hundreds of tasks, break it down into smaller team projects and use folders to organize them. In a team, all projects live at the same level, so folders are how you group related work. Sub-projects (nested projects) are available in My Projects only.

Add dates

As you’re organizing your project, you’ll find that there are tasks are due sooner than others.

To make sure you get things done on time, add a date and time to each task. These tasks will appear in the Today and Upcoming views, with the option to review them as a list, board, or calendar (available to Pro and Business customers).

Favorite a project

Turn the Todoist sidebar into your personal assistant by adding your most used projects as favorites. Turn on Add to favorites as you’re creating the project, or after identifying which projects you use the most.

Reorder your projects list

You can change the order of your personal projects by dragging them directly in the projects list under My Projects. There’s no separate drag handle, so you drag the project itself.

Select Platform:

  • Hover over a project under My Projects.
  • Drag the project up or down to its new position in the list.
  • Press and hold a project under My Projects.
  • Drag the project to its new position in the list, then let go.
  • At the bottom of your projects list, tap Manage projects.
  • In the top-right corner, tap the edit icon.
  • Drag the projects to reorder them. For team projects, anyone on the team can sort projects alphabetically (A-Z) or in reverse (Z-A). Admins can also choose Manual to drag and drop projects into any order. Click the Sort menu above the projects list to choose.

Sorting by creation date or last modified date isn’t available.

Create project templates

If you find yourself recreating the same task lists frequently, you can save time and effort by creating a project template. These templates are saved to the My templates section in the Todoist templates gallery, so you can access it any time.

Quick tip

When you import a template to a new project, the project doesn’t sync with the original version. When you make changes to one version, those changes won’t appear in the other.

Archive a project

If you need to shelve a project for later, archive that project to remove it from your projects list with the option to view and restore it later.

Select Platform:

  • Click the three dots icon beside the project in the sidebar.
  • Select Archive from the menu.
  • Click Archive to confirm.
Restore an archived project
  • Click My Projects or your team name.
  • Toggle the Archived projects only option on. You’ll see a list of archived projects.
  • Find the archived project and click the three dots icon next to its name.
  • Select Unarchive.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open the project you want to archive.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Tap Archive.
  • Tap Archive for me to confirm. If this is a team project, tap Archive for everyone. Quick tip

You can also archive a project through its context menu.

Restore an archived project
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap Manage Projects in My Projects.
  • Select Archived projects in the Project type menu.
  • Open the project you want to restore.
  • Tap Unarchive at the bottom.
  • Tap Unarchive for me to confirm. If this is a team project, tap Unarchive for everyone.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Open the project you want to archive.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top right.
  • Select Archive.
  • Tap Archive for me to confirm. If this is a team project, tap Archive for everyone.
Restore an archived project
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap Manage Projects.
  • Select Archived projects in the Project type menu.
  • Open the project you want to restore.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Unarchive.
  • Tap Unarchive for me to confirm. If this is a team project, tap Unarchive for everyone. Note

When you unarchive a project, all of its data is restored and preserved. This includes tasks, comments, reminders, attachments, and task assignments to collaborators.

If you’re a Pro or Business customer, Todoist automatically backs up your data every time you log in to your account. You can store up to 21 backups. If you deleted a project by accident, create a new project and import a backup.

Introduction to sections

Sections help you break a big project down into manageable parts, keeping you focused without feeling overwhelmed by a long, single list of tasks. In Todoist, you can create up to 20 sections per project to categorize tasks or organize them into phases. This way, you’ll know where a task belongs or which task to tackle first.

Play

Drag the Dynamic Add button to the section icon at the bottom-left of the project. The icon will expand in size, and you’ll see the words Add Section.

When using the board layout:

Rename a section

You may need to rename a section at any point of the project. Here’s how to do so:

Select Platform:

  • Click the three dots icon next to the section’s name.

If you delete a section, all its active and completed tasks are deleted as well, and these can’t be restored. If you’re a Todoist Pro or Business customer, and you need to recover that deleted section, download and import a backup.

Best practices for sections

Sections are useful when organizing and structuring your projects in Todoist. Here are some best practices to keep in mind when using sections.

Reorder sections in your project

Drag a section and all its tasks to its rightful place in your project. You can rearrange projects based on priority or category, alphabetically or chronologically. The sky’s the limit!

Archive a section after completing all its tasks

Think of sections as phases or milestones of your project. After completing all the tasks in one section, archive the section to signify you’ve completed this phase and are moving on to the next.

Use emoji or special characters

You can’t add labels, priorities, or comments to a section, but you can use emoji or special characters when naming sections in a project. Use emoji to add visual references, or special characters like " ( ) | & ! _ - or , to include more information in the section name.

Move tasks before archiving or deleting a section

Keep from archiving or deleting tasks you actually want to save by moving them out of the section:

Select Platform:

  • Open the project from the sidebar.
  • Bulk select the tasks in the section.
  • Click the Move to… icon.
  • Select the section or project to move these tasks to.
  • Open the project from the navigation.
  • Bulk select the tasks in the section.
  • Tap the move icon at the bottom.
  • Select the section or project to move these tasks to.
  • Open the project from the navigation.
  • Bulk select the tasks in the section.
  • Tap the move icon at the bottom.
  • Select the section or project to move these tasks to.

Introduction to templates in Todoist

Templates in Todoist allow you to quickly recreate your most successful workflows without starting from scratch every time. Browse through our vast library of pre-made templates, or create your own templates that best fit your unique workflow. Whether you’re managing a weekly project review or planning a social media campaign, using templates helps you save time and reduce mental effort.

You can use templates to:

  • Replicate successful projects like product launches or event planning
  • Track recurring habits such as reviews or monthly fitness goals
  • Standardize team processes by sharing templates for onboarding or meeting agendas
  • Organize personal lists for travel packing or grocery shopping Play

Get the most out of templates

Templates are huge time-savers when you find yourself frequently recreating the same project. Here are best practices to keep in mind when using templates in Todoist:

Everything’s in the name

Use consistent naming conventions to make templates easier to find and understand at a glance. For example, if a set of templates are for the Marketing team, you can prepend each template with the letters MK.

Provide context through task descriptions and comments

Rather than working with a blank slate, add descriptions and comments to tasks from the get-go to provide context about the template’s purpose. For example, a new employee will import your department’s onboarding template, and have all the instructions they need to get started right away.

Start right away with task templates

Task templates are made up of just the core tasks and sub-tasks. Create a custom template with just the essentials, then click the Apply my template option from the project menu to add the tasks to the project right away.

Update your templates regularly

Keep planning as frictionless as possible by updating your templates whenever significant changes happen within the project. If you notice that two or more tasks get deleted or you add just as many tasks after applying the template, save this as a new template and delete the older one.

Share your handcrafted templates with your team

If you created a Todoist team, a well-crafted template can save significant planning time and effort, allowing you to get that project up and running in minutes.

To share it with your team members, open your template and click the share icon at the top-right of the screen. Give access to everyone in the team, and click the Copy link button to share the template with them.

What’s the difference between the Inbox and a project?

The Inbox is your default task list in Todoist. When you add a task, it goes straight to your Inbox unless you specify that the task goes into a project.

A project is a task list that you create yourself. You give a project a name and then start adding tasks. You can also set a project’s color or share projects with your teammates.

Moving a task from the Inbox to a project

When adding a task, you may not be sure which project it belongs in. Don’t worry, just start by adding it to the Inbox.

Later on, you can drag the task right into a project of your choosing (Web, macOS, Windows) or edit the task and add it to a project by typing # in the name field (all platforms).

Adding a new task directly to a project

Of course, if you already know which project a task belongs in, you can just skip the Inbox and add your task there directly. When creating a new task, send it to a project by typing in the symbol # immediately followed by the project name. Once you type #, you can also choose from a list of existing projects, or create an entirely new one.

Reminders & Notifications

Add an urgent reminder in Todoist

There are tasks you just can’t miss, like paying bills before they’re due or picking up your kid from school on time. In Todoist, add urgent reminders to any task on top of your other reminders. They trigger a full-screen alarm that cuts through silent and Do Not Disturb modes, so you’ll never miss what matters most.

Warning

Urgent reminders are available on Todoist for iOS 26 and later, and on Android. They’re not available on Todoist for web or desktop.

Play

Quick tip

Urgent reminders are available on all plans. On the Beginner plan, you can mark your one reminder as urgent. With Pro or Business, you can add multiple urgent reminders to a task, and use a shortcut: type the time between two exclamation marks in the task name, like Call Peter !13:00!.

Add an urgent reminder

Select Platform:

Note

The Urgent toggle is attached to the reminder, not to the task’s date. After you add a time-based reminder, you’ll find the Urgent toggle below the calendar. Tapping the task’s date alone won’t show it.

Add an urgent reminder at a specific time

This requires a Pro or Business plan.

  • Tap the Dynamic Add button at the bottom-right to add a new task. If you’re editing a task, tap it to open the task view.
  • Tap the Reminders chip (alarm clock icon).
  • In the Date & Time section, tap Add to create a time-based reminder.
  • Toggle Urgent on. A prompt will appear once asking you to enable urgent reminders.
  • Tap Enable Urgent Reminders to confirm.
  • Tap Allow when your Apple device prompts you to enable alarms and timers.
  • Tap Save at the top-right. You’ll see the orange URGENT badge beside the reminder.
  • Tap the checkmark icon at the top-right to confirm.
Add an urgent Before Task reminder

This works on any plan.

  • Tap the Reminders chip (alarm clock icon).

  • Select Add to add a Before Task reminder.

  • Select how long before the task is due before Todoist sends a reminder.

  • Toggle Urgent on.

  • Tap Save at the top-right. To set a recurring urgent reminder, make sure the task has a Date and time, then:

  • Tap At time of task.

  • In the Date & Time section, tap Add reminder.

  • In the input field at the bottom, type a recurring date like “every Monday at 11 AM”.

  • Toggle Urgent on.

  • Tap Save at the top-right. The urgent reminder is now set. When the time comes, you’ll see a full-screen alarm even if your device is locked, in Silent mode, or in Focus mode.

Add an urgent reminder at a specific time

This requires a Pro or Business plan.

  • Tap the Dynamic Add button at the bottom-right to add a new task. If you’re editing a task, tap it to open the task view.
  • Tap the Reminders chip (alarm clock icon).
  • In the Date & Time section, tap Add reminder to create a time-based reminder.
  • Toggle Urgent on.
  • Tap Save at the top-right. You’ll see the orange URGENT badge beside the reminder.
  • Tap Okay at the bottom-right to confirm.
Add an urgent Before Task reminder

This works on any plan.

  • Tap the Reminders chip (alarm clock icon).
  • Select Add reminder under Before task.
  • Select how long before the task is due before Todoist sends a reminder.
  • Toggle Urgent on.
  • Tap Okay at the bottom-right. Standalone recurring urgent reminders aren’t currently available on Android.

Change the time of an urgent reminder

If you need to quickly change the time of an urgent reminder, tap the dismiss icon next to the reminder to remove it from the task. Then, add a new one with the updated time.

Note

Urgent reminders only work with time-based reminders, not location reminders.

Respond to an urgent reminder

Perfect timing! That reminder’s given you enough time to wrap up and prepare for your next task. Here’s how to respond to the urgent reminder:

Select Platform:

When an urgent reminder alarm goes off, it’ll appear on your device’s lock screen. You can either tap Complete or slide right to turn the alarm off.

When an urgent reminder alarm goes off, it’ll appear on your device’s lock screen. Press Stop to turn off the alarm.

Remove an urgent reminder

If you no longer need the urgent reminder, here’s how to remove it from the task:

Select Platform:

  • Tap the task with an urgent reminder. This opens the task view.
  • Tap the Reminders chip (alarm clock icon).
  • Tap the dismiss icon next to the urgent reminder to remove it.
  • Tap the task with an urgent reminder. This opens the task view.
  • Tap the Reminders chip (alarm clock icon).
  • Tap the dismiss icon next to the urgent reminder to remove it.

Introduction to reminders

A reminder sends you a notification about a task, either at a time you choose or when you arrive at a place. For example, you can get a reminder an hour before a report is due, or when you get to the grocery store. This guide explains how to set up automatic, custom, recurring, and location-based reminders in Todoist.

Play

Understand reminder types

In Todoist, you can add different kinds of reminders to a task:

  • Automatic reminders: A reminder that’s added by default whenever a date and time is scheduled to a task. This is based on your Reminders settings
  • Custom reminders: A reminder based on a specific date and time, or the amount of time before a task is due
  • Recurring reminders: A reminder that notifies you on a recurring basis (for example: ev Tuesday 7:00)
  • Location reminders: A reminder that notifies you when you’ve arrived at a specific location. Learn more about location reminders When you’ve identified which reminder suits your needs, here’s how to add them to your tasks.

Set up automatic reminders

When you add a date and time to a task, Todoist can automatically add a task reminder. You can adjust how long before the task date Todoist will remind you, as well as the type of notification you’ll receive, in your Reminders settings.

Select Platform:

  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Click the Reminders tab.
  • Click the Automatic reminders menu.
  • Select how long before the task’s time to receive a notification.
  • Turn on the type of notification you’d like to receive:
    • Desktop notification: Get notifications on your desktop computer.
    • Mobile notification: Get notifications on your mobile device.
    • Emails: Receive an email notification at your account email address.
Add an automatic reminder

To add an automatic reminder, always add a date and time to the task. This is because these reminders are relative to the time of a task.

Turn automatic reminders off

If you no longer want Todoist to add reminders automatically, click the Automatic reminders menu and select No automatic reminder.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.
  • Tap Reminders.
  • Tap Remind Me Via and choose which notification you’d like to receive:
    • Mobile Notification: Get notifications on your mobile device.
    • Desktop Notification: Get notifications on your desktop computer.
    • Email: Receive an email notification at your account email address.
  • Tap back to Reminders.
  • Tap Automatic Reminders and select a relative time from the list. Quick tip

When you snooze a reminder on iOS, you can choose to be reminded again at a later time. Tap When snoozed… and select an interval from the list.

  • Tap the gear icon at the top.

To add an automatic reminder, always add a date and time to the task. This is because these reminders are relative to the time of a task.

Turn automatic reminders off

If you no longer want Todoist to add reminders automatically, click the Automatic Reminders menu and select No automatic reminder.

  • Tap Browse in the bottom-right.

Add a custom reminder

Add custom reminders that’ll remind you on a specific date and time, or before a task is due. If you’re on Todoist Pro or Business, you can add multiple custom reminders, so you get notifications at any time of the day.

Select Platform:

Add a Date & Time reminder
  • Click a task to open the task view.
  • Click Reminders on the right side. A small window will appear.
  • Select the Date & time tab.
  • Select the hour you want to receive the notification, or use natural language to enter the date and time (for example: Mon 19:00)
  • Click Add reminder.
Add an additional custom reminder

  • Click a task to open the task view.

  • Click Reminders on the right side. A small window will appear.

  • Select the Before task tab.

  • Select how long before you’ll get a notification about the task in the menu. You’ll get a notification when it’s time for this task to be due.

  • Click Add reminder. In the Todoist mobile apps, you can only add a Date & time reminder. Here’s how to add them to your task:

  • Tap a task. This opens the task view.

  • Tap the Reminders chip. You’ll see suggested reminders that you can select from.

  • Tap Custom Date & Time. A scheduler will appear.

  • Select the date of the reminder, or use natural language to enter the date and time (for example: Mon 19:00).

  • Tap the Time menu and select the hour of the reminder.

  • Tap Save at the top-right. The custom reminder is added to the list.

  • Tap Done. In the Todoist mobile apps, you can only add a Date & time reminder. Here’s how to add them to your task:

  • Tap a task. This opens the task view.

  • Tap the Reminders chip. You’ll see suggested reminders that you can select from.

  • Tap Custom Date & Time. A scheduler will appear.

  • Select the date of the reminder, or use natural language to enter the date and time (for example: Mon 19:00).

  • Tap the alarm clock icon and select the hour of the reminder.

  • Tap OK. The custom reminder is added to the list.

  • Tap OK again to confirm.

  • Close the task view.

Assign a reminder

If you’re working on a shared project with other people, you can assign reminders to specific collaborators, so they don’t miss tasks that need their input.

Select Platform:

  • Click a task to open the task view.
  • Click Reminders on the right side.
  • Click the avatar beside the reminder.
  • Select the appropriate person from the assignee list.
  • Tap a task to open the task view.
  • Tap the Reminders chip.
  • Select Custom Date & Time.
  • Tap Notify.
  • Select the person to assign them to the reminder.
  • Tap a task to open the task view.
  • Tap the Reminders chip.
  • Select Custom date & time.
  • Tap Notify.
  • Select the person to assign them to the reminder.

Add a recurring reminder

Got a busy schedule and you can’t always check Todoist? Add a recurring reminder, so you get notifications about your tasks on a regular basis.

Quick tip

A custom Date & Time reminder added to a recurring task fires once for that occurrence only, and won’t repeat when the task does. To be notified on every occurrence, add a recurring reminder (for example: ev Mon 8:00) or an additional custom reminder that fires before each occurrence.

Select Platform:

  • Click a task to open the task view.
  • Click Reminders on the right side. A small window will appear.
  • Select the Date & time tab.
  • Enter the recurring date and time for the reminder (for example: ev Mon 8:00)
  • Click Add reminder.
  • Make sure the task has a date and time.
  • Tap the task. This opens the task view.
  • Tap the Reminders chip.
  • Tap At time of task.
  • In the Date & Time section, tap Add.
  • In the text field at the bottom of the page, type something like every day at 11 AM, then tap the search icon.
  • Optionally, toggle on Urgent before saving.
  • Tap Save. This adds the recurring reminder to the list.
  • Tap Done. Urgent reminders display a full-screen alarm that cuts through silent and Do Not Disturb modes, so you don’t miss the things that matter most. They’re available only on Todoist for iOS 26 and later – you won’t see the Urgent toggle on Android, web, or desktop. Learn how to use urgent reminders on iOS.

Recurring reminders aren’t supported in Todoist for Android. Switch to the Todoist web app or desktop apps, and add a recurring reminder to your task.

Use shortcuts to create reminders

If you’re on Todoist Pro or Business, use the exclamation mark ! as a shortcut to add a reminder as you’re creating or editing a task. In Quick Add, enter an exclamation mark ! in the task name followed by the desired time for the reminder.

Samara · Customer Experience Specialist

When you enter the exclamation mark, reminder suggestions will appear in a dropdown menu. Select the reminder that fits your needs.

Get notified at a specific time (like !3pm), after a certain amount of time has passed (like !2h), or at a certain amount of time before your task is due (like !30mb or !30min before). Todoist will even understand when you add a reminder for !later (4 hours later) or !tomorrow (the next day at 9:00 AM).

Here is the list of supported reminders:

Shortcut

Example

What it does

!30m

Work meeting today 10:30 !30m

Reminder set for 30 minutes from current time (time when added to task)

!2h30m

Call the hotel to confirm reservation !2h30m

Reminder set for 2 hours and 30 minutes from current time (time when added to task)

!0mb or !0min before

Lunch at restaurant 1pm !0mb

Reminder set at the exact time (0 minutes before)

!later

Clear the trash !later

Reminder set for around 4 hours later from current time (rounded down to the closest hour)

!1hb or !1h before

Prepare meeting agenda 11am !1h before

Reminder set 1 hour before it’s due

Note: When added to tasks without time, this will create a reminder set 1 hour from the current time.

!11am !1hb !3hb

Dentist appointment Thu 2pm !11am !1hb !3hb

Multiple reminders set for: the next instance of 11 AM, 1 hour before it’s due, and 3 hours before it’s due

!6pm

Get groceries after work !6pm

Reminder set for the next instance of 6 PM

!30mb or !30m before

Take vitamins every day at 9am !30mb

For each instance of the task, reminder is set for 30 minutes before 9 AM

!tmr 3pm

Hand in report before EOD !tmr 3pm

Reminder set for tomorrow at 3 PM

!Mon 9am

Check schedule for the week !mon 9am

Reminder set for Monday at 9 AM

!every 5pm

End of day review every day !every 5pm

Reminder set for every day at 5 PM

!every sat 9am

Water plants every weekend !every sat 9am

Reminder set to every Saturday at 9 AM

!every 2 hours

Check on Hariette’s progress !every 2 hours

Reminder set to every 2 hours

Warning

Reminder shortcuts don’t work with Microsoft Swiftkey. To resolve this, turn off this keyboard or switch to a different keyboard on your Android device.

Get the most out of reminders

Reminders keep you from missing out on important events and scheduled tasks. Make the most out of reminders by following these best practices:

Use natural language

Save yourself from extra clicks or taps by entering reminders using natural language. Any of the dates and times used to schedule your tasks also work for reminders.

Let Todoist suggest reminders

Todoist takes the load off your shoulders by proactively suggesting helpful reminders. If you’re using the web app or desktop apps, enter an exclamation mark ! to see a list of reminder suggestions. If you’re on your mobile device, suggestions will appear right away when you tap the Reminders chip in the task view.

Snooze the reminder for later

If you can’t work on a task at the time you get the notification, pull out your mobile device and snooze the reminder for later. Todoist will make sure to send the next notification at your preferred interval.

Here’s how to set up your snooze settings in Todoist:

Select Platform:

There’s no option to snooze a reminder in either the Todoist web app or desktop apps.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.
  • Select Reminders.
  • Tap When Snoozed… and select your preferred interval.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.
  • Select Reminders.
  • Tap When snoozed… and select your preferred interval.

Next steps

Manage your notifications in Todoist

Notifications keep you in the loop with what’s going on in your shared projects. In Todoist, you can receive notifications for different activities, either through email or push notification. These can range from someone posting a task comment to a teammate joining a project.

If you’re collaborating with a big group, that’s a lot of notifications, so we made sure to keep things easy and flexible by letting you choose which notification to receive on your devices.

Play

Set up notifications

Select Platform:

  • Log in to Todoist.
  • Click your avatar at the top-left.
  • Select Settings.
  • Click the Notifications tab.
  • Turn on Desktop and web notifications. Note

Desktop and web notifications use a single on/off toggle, independent of email and mobile. When Desktop and web notifications are on, you’ll receive desktop and web alerts for shared project activity, even if email and mobile are off for those activities. To stop, turn off Desktop and web notifications.

Notifications are turned on by default. To review or make changes to your notification settings:

  • Open Todoist for iOS.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.
  • Select Notifications. Then, review or toggle the notifications you want to receive or not receive from Todoist.

Notifications are turned on by default. To review or make changes to your notification settings:

  • Open Todoist for Android.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.
  • Select Notifications. Then, review or toggle the notifications you want to receive or not receive from Todoist.
Change the default notification sound

Give Todoist a unique ringtone by changing the default notification sound on your Android device:

  • Tap the Settings app of your Android device.
  • Select Notifications.
  • Tap App notifications. You’ll see a list of installed apps.
  • Tap Todoist.
  • Select Reminders.
  • Tap Sound and choose your preferred sound.
  • Tap Save to confirm. Note

These steps may differ depending on your Android device’s settings. If you’re not sure where the setting is located, get in touch with us and we’ll lend a hand.

Best practices for notifications

To stay on top of your schedule without bogging down in overwhelm, here are some best practices when using notifications in Todoist:

Check the Notifications tab

Check all of your notifications, both read and unread, in the Notifications tab. If you need to check just your unread notifications, you can open the Unread tab.

Summer · Customer Experience Specialist

If you want to mark all your unread notifications as read, simply click or tap the checkmark icon.

Choose notifications that matter to you

Cleaning up hundreds of project notifications isn’t the best use of your time. Choose which notifications matter the most and where you want to receive them by selecting either email or push notification, or both, beside the project activity you want to be notified about.

Take control of your inbox

Subscribing to our emails is just as easy and flexible. Toggle the email lists that are of value to you. You can remove yourself from the rest.

Use location reminders in Todoist

Set a location reminder for Todoist tasks when arriving or leaving at a selected place. Todoist can send a push notification about completing your 30-minute workout when you arrive at the gym, or to grab an umbrella when you’re leaving home.

Check the Location Services settings

Before adding a location reminder, check the Location Services settings of your mobile device, so it receives location-based alerts.

Select Platform:

  • Open the Settings app of your Apple device.

  • Tap Privacy & Security.

  • Tap Location Services.

  • Scroll down and tap System Services.

  • Check that Alerts & Shortcuts Automations is turned on for your device.

  • Tap back and select Todoist.

  • Allow location access while using the app.

  • Toggle Precise Location on. If you don’t see Todoist in the list of apps using location services, add a location reminder to a task to trigger the prompt to enable location services.

  • Open the Settings app of your Android device.

  • Tap Location.

  • Toggle the Use location option on.

  • Tap App location permissions.

  • Scroll down and select Todoist.

  • Select Allow all the time or Allow only while using the app. Note

These steps may differ depending on your Android device’s settings. If you’re not sure where the setting is located or if the interface is different, contact your device manufacturer.

Check the Notification settings

Then, check the Notifications settings of your Apple device, so it receives push notifications for reminders.

Select Platform:

  • Open the Settings app of your Apple device.
  • Select Notifications.
  • Scroll down and select Todoist.
  • Toggle Allow Notifications and Time-Sensitive Notifications on. These settings ensure you receive your reminders without delay.
  • Open the Settings app of your Apple device.
  • Select Notifications.
  • Tap App notifications.
  • Select Todoist.
  • Toggle All Todoist notifications on. Note

These steps may differ depending on your Android device’s settings. If you’re not sure where the setting is located or if the interface is different, contact your device manufacturer.

Add a location reminder

Let’s start by adding a location reminder to a task:

Select Platform:

  • Tap the task to open the task view.
  • Tap the Location chip. If the chip isn’t visible, learn how to customize Quick Add.
  • Enter the address of the location. If you’re adding a location reminder for the first time, you’ll be prompted to give Todoist location access.
  • Select the most accurate location from the search results.
  • Select to receive the reminder upon arrival or departure.
  • Tap the blue circle on the map. Then, drag it outward or inward to change the radius of the location.
  • Tap Save to add the reminder.
  • Tap the task to open the task view.
  • Tap the Location chip. If the chip isn’t visible, learn how to customize Quick Add.
  • Enter the address of the location. If you’re adding a location reminder for the first time, you’ll be prompted to give Todoist location access.
  • Select the most accurate location from the search results.
  • Select to receive the reminder upon arrival or departure.
  • Tap the submit icon next to the map. You’ll only receive push notifications for location reminders on your mobile device. This is because Todoist relies on your mobile device’s location services to send the push notification when you arrive at the specified location.

You can, however, add these reminders while using the Todoist web app or desktop apps, and then manage them on either Todoist for iOS or Android.

  • Click Add task and enter the task details.
  • Click the red Add task button to create the task.
  • Click the task to open its task view.
  • Click Location on the right-hand side.
  • Type the address of the location. If you see it, select it from the drop-down list.
  • Select if you’d like to receive the reminder upon arrival or departure.
  • Click the red Add location button.

Clear location suggestions

To save time, Todoist provides location suggestions based on your past location reminders. If the list starts to get cluttered, clear these location suggestions:

Select Platform:

  • Open Todoist for iOS.
  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap the gear icon in the top-right.
  • Tap Reminders.
  • Tap Clear Saved Locations.
  • Open Todoist for Android.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap the gear icon at the top-right.
  • Tap Reminders.
  • Tap Clear locations.

Security & Admin

Manage security options for your Todoist team

Teams often store sensitive, private, complex, or just plain quirky data within Todoist projects. To keep your information safe and streamline onboarding, you can manage various security options as a team admin. This guide covers how to link team domains, enable team discovery for new members, and restrict external guest access in your team.

Quick tip

Want to learn more about how we protect your data? Visit our Trust Center for detailed information on Todoist’s security, privacy, and compliance practices.

Link your team domain

The team domain option allows an admin to link their team to their corporate email domain.

Let’s say the admin’s email is alex@todoist.com. Their associated team domain would be todoist.com. Turning this option on is a prerequisite to use the Team Discovery option.

Team domains only work with unique corporate email domains. If you signed up with a generic email address, like gmail.com, yahoo.com, or hotmail.com, and you’d like to change it to your corporate email, follow these steps.

Team domain changes

If the admin who created the Todoist team changes their email associated with their account, the Team Discovery feature will still work with the admin’s previous email domain.

If alex@todoist.com changes their account email to alex@twist.com, Team Discovery will still be available to Alex’s teammates with the @todoist.com email domain.

Enable Team Discovery

When an admin turns on Team Discovery, any person that shares the same email domain can find and automatically join the associated team. In Todoist, they’ll see a Join the team link at the bottom of the sidebar.

This eliminates the need for admins to individually add each new member, saving time and reducing the administrative burden associated with growing teams. Continuing the example from above, anyone with the email address ending in @todoist.com can automatically join Alex the admin’s team and gain access to it.

Prohibit external guests

When an admin turns on the Prohibit external guests option, it won’t be possible to invite guests to team projects (only available on the Business plan).

This control is crucial for preserving the privacy of sensitive discussions, protecting intellectual property, and upholding compliance with data protection regulations that might be applicable to the company associated with the team.

Troubleshooting and limitations

  • The team admin’s email address must be verified in order to enable Team Discovery. Learn how to verify your email.
  • If the domain is already associated with an existing team or workspace, Team Discovery won’t be available. A workaround would be to reach out to the existing team’s administrator about the possibility of transforming it into a company-wide team. Then, each department can use folders to manage their projects.

Get help

If you’re having trouble setting up your Todoist team domain, or using Team Discovery, get in touch with us.

Teams FAQ

Team workspaces allow you to simplify and manage projects and tasks, no matter how small or large your team may be. Find answers to common questions about using teams in Todoist, including setup, member management, and billing. You can also check out our introduction to teams to see how it all works in action.

Quick tip

Rolling out Todoist to your team? The Run the Full Rollout course in the Todoist Toolkit covers launch day, the first two weeks, and what to do when momentum stalls.

Teams in Todoist

The Business plan includes all of the features of the Pro plan – like custom reminders, filters, and more – in addition to a few handy capabilities for team users and admins:

All team members will be able to:

  • Browse and preview public team projects and join only the ones that are relevant to them.

  • Share direct links to projects, sections, tasks, and comments that teammates can preview and instantly take action on.

  • Group or filter tasks by personal and/or team projects from the View Options menu in Today, Upcoming, and filter views to better separate work and life. For team leaders, adding a team to Todoist:

  • Gives you a transparent, organized overview of all your team’s work and lets you pop in to see progress, without having to join each and every individual project.

  • Makes data ownership crystal clear. Team projects belong to the team. Personal projects belong to the individual.

  • Grants admins more control over permissions and data access in team settings. Plus, when you upgrade your team to the Business plan, all members automatically get access to all personal Pro features – like custom reminders, calendar layout for projects, and task durations!

(After all, when your teammates are organized and on top of their personal to-dos, teamwork magically tends to flow more smoothly, too. 💆)

You can view a full overview of what is included with each plan on our pricing page.

You absolutely can! The simple yet powerful personal task manager you know and love isn’t going anywhere. As with all of Todoist’s power features, these team features are there when you need them and out of the way when you don’t. Your personal projects stay private and in your full control, even when you’re collaborating with a team in a shared workspace.

Use teams

Yes! There are no limits to the amount of paid teams you can create.

However, billing is per team. If you have the same person in two different paid teams, you’re paying twice for that person. This means that separate teams are best used when interacting with completely distinct groups – clients, vendors, or partner organizations – with no crossover.

Instead of creating new teams, you may choose to use folders or restricted projects to group and organize team efforts; in fact, that’s how we do it ourselves.

You can go here to see a full overview of the features and limits for each team plan.

This article explains in detail what the difference is between being an admin, a member, or a guest of a team.

Shared projects can be great for ad hoc collaboration, but when you work with the same group of people who all need access to the same projects and information, one-off shared projects leave a lot to be desired. Now there’s a dedicated home for your team’s work.

In a team:

  • All members can browse and preview projects on their own, or preview and join projects via link. No more manually inviting people, one-by-one, to join shared projects.
  • Every member can keep track of important projects in the team, while maintaining a completely separate space for their personal data. Custom filters allow for the mix of work and personal tasks that’s right for each individual.
  • Referencing projects, sections, and tasks is as easy as sharing a link.
  • Data ownership – what belongs to the team and what belongs to individuals – is crystal clear. Team projects belong to the team and personal projects stay private – even if you leave the team.
  • Admins can control access, manage roles, and get an overview of the team’s activity. And there’s more to come. We’ll continue to add more collaborative features based on real-world feedback from teams like yours.

From a data ownership perspective, all projects and tasks in your team belong to the team.

To keep your team’s data secure, moving projects and tasks out of the team isn’t allowed. Check that any project or task that are about to move to the team don’t include personal or private information.

We’re currently exploring ways to facilitate project moves (with appropriate Admin permissions), and will prioritize our efforts based on what users like you need most.

People outside of your organization can be invited to specific projects as guests, for free. Guests can join unlimited team projects, regardless of their personal account limits.

Pricing

Note

Each account is limited to 1 free team. To create a second team, you’ll need to upgrade your existing workspace to a Business plan. Each workspace has its own independent subscription.

When you create a team, you’ll automatically start with the Beginner plan. This gives everyone access to core collaborative features, with a few usage limits.

When you’re ready, you can upgrade the team to the Business plan to remove those limits and unlock more powerful features – like unlimited members, guests, and folders.

To experience the power of our collaborative features, you can test drive a single team for free. As your needs grow, you can upgrade to the Business plan. You’ll gain access to more features to help optimize your teamwork, plus the people you’ve invited will automatically receive access to Pro features in their personal projects at no extra cost.

Note that billing is per person per team. If you decide you need more than one team, check if you need to invite the same people in more than one team to avoid paying more.

You can view a full overview of what’s included with each plan on our pricing page.

When designing teams, our goal was to create a seamless experience where you and your teammates can organize your personal and team tasks in one place – without having to switch between two separate accounts – while at the same time keeping data ownership clearly separated.

But for most teams, some additional organization will be needed within the shared workspace to support the unique way your team operates.

Instead of creating new teams, you may choose to use Folders to group and organize team efforts… In fact, that’s how we do it ourselves. This makes managing your settings, billing, and members more streamlined, and avoids any double-billing for the same member. You may also find using restricted projects for precise access control helpful as well – we think it’s perfect for “1-on-1” projects, for example.

Of course, there are cases where creating separate teams make sense; they’re best used when interacting with completely distinct groups – like clients, vendors, or partner organizations – with no crossover.

Note that we’ll be continuing to gather feedback from users like you on how you’d like to see our team features evolve. So if folders and restricted projects aren’t meeting your needs, let us know how you would use multiple teams in Todoist.

Cancel a paid plan

Subscriptions to paid plans automatically renew every year or month. You can cancel subscriptions at any time from the billing settings.

If you choose to cancel a team plan, the team will still have access to paid features until the end of the ongoing billing period. Then the team will be moved back to the Beginner plan (and the corresponding usage limits). And don’t worry, if you do cancel, neither you nor your team will lose any data that was created while on a paid plan.

To receive a refund on a Pro or Business plan payment, you’ll need to request the refund within 30 days of subscribing and be on yearly billing, unless otherwise provided by applicable law. Monthly subscriptions aren’t eligible for refunds. Learn more in this article.

If you have paid for Pro and upgrade to Business before using your full Pro time, your remaining Pro time will be added as credit in our system. However, please note that this credit can only be used to pay for Pro subscriptions.

If you upgrade to Business within 30 days of having subscribed to Pro, you may be eligible for a full refund. Learn more in this article.

Data and security

Visit our Trust Center for our SOC 2 report, subprocessor list, and security documentation.

The short answer is very secure!

The longer answer, for the more technically-inclined:

When user data is stored in servers and databases, Todoist uses AES 256 encryption. When the data is being sent or received, it is encrypted with TLS 1.1 or above. Data backups on our servers are encrypted with AES256 and signed by RSA with 2048 key length.

Todoist also creates daily automatic backups within the app for our Business plan users, which follow our strict security protocols to prevent unauthorized access.

We also support 2-Factor Authentication to ensure access to your data remains secure.

When you create a team on behalf of an organization, the organization owns the data within it. Admins can:

  • Assign roles
  • Remove people
  • Delete the team Personal projects (the ones listed under My Projects in the sidebar) are controlled by the individual team member and can’t be accessed by anyone else.

Choose what works best for you. A good rule of thumb:

  • For work you just need to keep track of for yourself – or shared projects that include sensitive information you want to keep private – use a personal project.
  • For work to collaborate on with teammates – or projects to keep your team looped in on – use your shared team. You can find the most up-to-date information in our Privacy Policy and Terms of Service.

Cancel a Todoist subscription

Cancel a Pro subscription

If you’re on a free Pro trial instead of a paid subscription, follow the steps in Cancel your Pro trial instead.

In order to cancel your Pro subscription, simply stop your Pro plan from automatically renewing itself. To do this, you need to turn it off based on the payment method you used:

Note

If you can no longer access your Todoist account, you won’t be able to complete the steps below. Get in touch with us instead, and we’ll verify your identity and cancel the subscription for you.

Credit & Debit card payments made through Todoist will be set to auto-renew by default. Here’s how to turn it off:

You’ll find the Subscription tab in the Todoist web and desktop apps, not the mobile app.

  • Log in to your Todoist account on todoist.com.

  • Click your avatar at the top-left.

  • Select Settings.

  • Select Subscription.

  • Click Cancel plan.

  • Choose a reason for the cancellation. You can also share feedback on what we could improve.

  • Click Cancel subscription to confirm. What happens next depends on your subscription:

  • If you’re on a monthly plan, or outside the 30-day refund window on a yearly plan:

  • You’ll see the option to cancel your subscription, and it will remain active until the end of your current billing period.

  • If you’re within the 30-day refund window on a yearly plan you’ll see two options:

  • Cancel at the end of your billing period.

  • End the subscription immediately and receive a refund. Select your preferred option, then click Cancel subscription to confirm.

Please note that PayPal is no longer available as a payment option. Any past payments made using PayPal will not auto-renew.

App Store subscriptions auto-renew by default, so you need to manually cancel them. You can find the option to cancel the auto-renew by viewing your Apple ID in iTunes or the App Store and then selecting the “Subscriptions” option.

Google Play subscriptions may or may not auto-renew depending on many factors. Please check your Google Play account and verify if there is a recurring Todoist subscription there. If there is, remove it directly.

Todoist Pro payments made through the Microsoft Store won’t auto-renew.

Not sure which account your subscription is linked to?

If you want to cancel but you’re not sure which account your subscription is linked to, here’s how to find it. These steps apply to both Pro and Business plans.

  • Check whether you signed up with a different email address. Your subscription may be linked to another account you own.
  • Get in touch with us if you still can’t locate the account, and share the following details so we can find it for you:
    • The last 4 digits of the card that was charged
    • The card brand (Visa, Mastercard, etc.)
    • The card’s expiry date

Cancel and downgrade your Todoist Business subscription

To downgrade from Todoist Business to either Pro or Beginner, cancel the Business subscription first. Only admins can cancel a Business subscription. Team billing is only available in the Todoist web and desktop apps.

Cancel the Business plan

  • Click your team in the sidebar.
  • Click Subscription under the team name.
  • Click Cancel plan. You’ll see a list of benefits you’ll miss after canceling your subscription.
  • Click Cancel subscription.
  • Select the reason for the cancellation. Provide any feedback you may have about the plan.
  • Click Cancel subscription. You’ll see your plan type, price, and the end of the billing period.
  • Click Cancel subscription to review your subscription details.
  • Click Cancel subscription again to confirm.

After canceling your Business plan

Even after you cancel your Business plan, you’ll have access to Business features until your subscription expires. You can find your subscription’s expiration date when you access your team billing settings. After that, you’ll automatically move to the Beginner plan. To switch to Pro, you’ll need to manually upgrade once your subscription ends.

Downgrading also changes your account limits, and some projects may become read-only. To see exactly what changes, read What happens when I downgrade my plan?

Monthly Business payments aren’t refundable when you cancel, unless a refund is required by consumer protection laws in your country.

If you purchased or renewed your yearly Business subscription within the last 30 days, get in touch with us after canceling to request a refund. Include your payment receipt or order reference ID, which appears on any invoice you download from your team billing settings. For the full policy, read Request a refund.

If you’re not eligible for a refund, you may have credit on your account after canceling the subscription. This credit isn’t refundable, and it isn’t transferable to another team or plan.
