Use Everhour with Todoist

Everhour is a time-tracking tool that works inside Todoist, letting you track time, set estimates, and manage project planning without leaving your to-do list.

Note

The Everhour integration is currently only available when using Chrome.

Setting up the integration

  • Go to the Chrome Web Store.
  • Search for Everhour.
  • Click Add to Chrome.
  • Open Everhour in Chrome.
  • Log in to your Everhour account.
  • Select Settings.
  • Open the Integrations tab.
  • Click Todoist.
  • Select Agree.
  • After installing the Everhour extension, you’ll need to grant Everhour access to Todoist. To do so, click the Everhour icon in your Chrome toolbar.
  • Select Grant Access.
  • Select Allow. You are now ready to use Everhour when using Todoist in your Chrome browser.

Quick tip

To easily check whether your timer is running, keep Everhour visible in your browser toolbar. Click the puzzle piece icon, then click the pin icon next to Everhour to keep it in view.

Use the integration

After the integration is complete, you’ll notice that Everhour adds new features to the Todoist interface.

Note

You can’t use Everhour in your Todoist Inbox.

Track time in a task list
  • Open any view in Todoist that’s not your Inbox, such as a project, your Today or Upcoming view, or a filter or label.
  • Find the task you want to track, and click on the play button next to the task to start tracking time.
  • The button will display Starting before turning red to indicate that tracking is active.
  • Click it again to stop the timer. Stopping will appear, and the tracked time will be displayed.
Track time in the task view
  • Click the task you want to track to open task view.
  • Click Start Timer to begin tracking. The button will display Starting, and the tracker will begin. The timer will continue running even if you close the task.
  • You have the option to add a note about your progress by clicking the speech bubble next to the tracked time.
  • You can stop the time tracker in two ways:
    • If you are still in task view, simply click Stop.
    • If you have already closed task view, click the red time tracker next to the task name.
  • Stopping will appear, and the tracked time will be displayed.
Add time manually
  • To add time manually to a task, click the task to open task view.
  • You can now add time manually in two different ways:
    • Select Add Time, then enter the time, date, and any relevant notes before hitting Save.
    • Toggle on the option to enter the time as start/end instead. Rachel · Customer Experience

While settling into my new role, I used the Everhour integration to track how I spent my time on various onboarding tasks. The insight helped me understand where my energy was going and make small adjustments to better focus on key priorities and learning goals.

Review your tracked time

In the Todoist sidebar, click the Timesheet button to view a summary of all your tracked time.

Quick tip

You can create reports using your Todoist data by opening the report builder in Everhour and selecting what you’d like to include. Learn more.

Remove the integration

If you no longer want to use Todoist with Everhour, there are several ways to remove the integration:

  • Find the Everhour extension in Chrome by going to chrome://extensions. Then, click Remove or toggle it off.
  • Right-click the Everhour icon in your browser toolbar to open the drop-down menu, then select Remove from Chrome.
  • You can also disable the integration at any time from the Integrations tab in your Everhour account. Once removed, refresh your Todoist page to complete the process.

Get in touch

This integration is developed and maintained by Everhour. If you have any questions or run into any issues with this integration, don’t hesitate to get in touch with the Everhour support team for help.

Views, Filters & Labels

Customize views in Todoist

Customize which tasks you want to see and how they’re displayed to match your management style, project requirements, and workflow preferences.

Change a layout

There are five different view layouts in Todoist, which you can change whenever you like:

Layout

Use it to

List

See everything in one place. Get a clear overview of all your tasks and subtasks, from big-picture plans to small details.

Board

Organize tasks visually. Great for workflows where you move tasks through stages, like tracking progress, spotting bottlenecks, and setting priorities.

Day calendar

Focus on today. Review what’s overdue and due today, and time block your tasks to make the most of your day.

Week calendar

Plan your week. Time-block tasks across your week in any project, filter, label, or the Upcoming view. (On mobile, you’ll see 3 days at a time; on desktop, the full 7-day view.)

Month calendar

Look ahead. Manage and schedule tasks for the next 30 days in a project, filter, label, or the Upcoming view.

If the project is shared, people in the project will see the new layout when they open and view the project.

Color tasks in the calendar layout

In the calendar layout, tasks are colored by priority by default. Open Display and select Coloring to color them by label or project instead. Learn more about coloring tasks in the calendar layout.

Sort tasks

Arrange tasks using the following options:

Sorting type

Use it to

Grouping

Group tasks in a project, label, filter, Inbox, or Today view based on selected criteria.

Sorting

Sort tasks alphabetically or by assignee, date, creation date, priority, or project.

If sorting or grouping options are turned on for a shared project, these changes are only visible to you. People in the project will continue to see tasks in their current views.

Filter your tasks

In addition to sorting and grouping your tasks, you can also filter them. This means that rather than displaying all tasks in a project, label, filter, Inbox, or your Today view, you can filter out tasks. You can filter your tasks by:

Filter by

Use it to see

Assignee

Tasks assigned to you, a specific assignee, or no one

Date

Tasks within a certain time frame

Deadline

Tasks with a scheduled deadline

Priority

Tasks with a specific priority

Label

Tasks with a specific label

Workspace

Tasks in a specific workspace

Share your project view with collaborators

Once you’ve customized your project view using the grouping, sorting, and filtering options, you can save your layout as the default view by selecting Save for everyone. This ensures that all project collaborators see the same default view.

If you make changes to a project that already has a default view, you’ll notice an orange dot in you Display menu. This dot indicates that your current view differs from the default. If you click Save for everyone or Reset all, the orange dot will disappear.

Play

Note

Only admins and members are able to share project views when in a team project. Guests will not be able to share project views.

  • Color tasks in the calendar layout
  • Sort tasks
  • Filter your tasks

Introduction to filters

As Todoist starts to fill up with tasks, finding information needs to be speedy and efficient. That’s where filters come in handy! Filters are custom views of your tasks using specific query syntaxes, all based on specific criteria. You can narrow down your lists according to task name, date, project, label, priority, date created, and more.

Note

Filters are custom views you create. Today, Upcoming, and Priority are built-in views that work differently and can’t be edited with filter queries.

Play

Add a filter

Let’s start by creating your first filter:

Quick tip

Not sure how to write a query? Use Filter Assist to describe what you want in plain language, and it’ll write the query for you.

Select Platform:

  • Select Filters & Labels in the sidebar.

  • Click the Add icon next to Filters.

  • In the Add filter window, enter the name of the filter or change the filter color.

  • Enter the filter query. Check out these filter query examples.

  • Click Add to save your filter.

  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.

  • Tap Filters & Labels.

  • Tap the Add icon next to Filters.

  • Enter the filter name in the Name your filter field.

  • Enter the filter query in the Query field. Check out these filter query examples.

  • Tap Done at the top-right to save your new filter. Quick tip

  • Tap the Color menu to choose a different filter color.

  • Tap the Favorite toggle to add the filter to your favorites.

  • Touch and drag a filter to a new place in the list to rearrange the order.

  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.

  • Tap Filters & Labels.

  • Tap the Add icon next to Filters.

  • Enter a filter name.

  • Enter the filter query. Check out these filter query examples.

  • Tap the checkmark icon at the top-right to save your filter. Quick tip

  • Tap the Color menu to choose a different filter color.

  • Tap the Favorite toggle to add the filter to your favorites.

  • Touch and drag a filter to a new place in the list to rearrange the order. Note

If you can’t find the Filters & Labels view, it might be hidden from the sidebar. Customize your sidebar and make sure it’s set to appear with all your other views.

Edit a filter

You realize some of your filters have missing information, or are throwing an error. Here’s how to edit a filter:

Select Platform:

Click the pencil icon to the right of the filter name. Then, make changes to your filter.

  • Tap on Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Select a filter.
  • Tap the three dots icon in the top-right.
  • Select Edit Filter and make your changes.
  • Tap Done at the top-right to confirm. Quick tip

You can also edit a filter through the filter’s context menu.

  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Select a filter.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Edit filter and make your changes.
  • Tap the checkmark icon to confirm. Note

If you rename a project, any filters that reference the old project name will stop working. Update those filters manually after renaming.

Break it down with symbols

There are a range of symbols you can use when creating filters in Todoist:

Symbol

What it means

Example

OR

today | overdue

&

AND

today & p1

!

NOT

!subtask

()

Filter tasks based on queries inside parentheses first. Use & or | within and in between parentheses to run multiple queries in a single filter.

(today | overdue) & #Work

,

Display filter queries in separate lists.

date: yesterday, today


Use special characters in project, section, or label names as regular characters.

Filter tasks in projects, sections, or labels with two or more words in the name.

#One & Two

#Shopping list

Marija · Customer Experience Specialist

Parentheses are especially powerful when you need to run multiple queries in a filter. By adding & and | symbols inside and in between parentheses, you can filter tasks based on very specific criteria. For example, a filter can show either assigned and unassigned tasks that are overdue and due today, and that have the @work label.

Use these filters

Here’s a rundown of all the supported Todoist filters you can use to organize your work. If a filter query isn’t listed below, it’s not available or supported in Todoist. You enter these filter queries in Filters & Labels, not in Display settings.

Filter based on:

To create filters based on keywords, you can use search: followed by a keyword.

If you need to

Use this

See all tasks that contain the word “Meeting”

search: Meeting

See all tasks that contain the word “Meeting” that are due today

search: Meeting & today

See all tasks that contain either the word “Meeting” or “Work”

search: Meeting | search: Work

See all tasks that contain two or more specific words (for example: send email)

search: send email

See all tasks that contain web links

search: http

When searching for tasks that contain two or more specific keywords, the filter finds tasks containing all the keywords, but they may not necessarily be in that exact order.

Create a filter to either see or exclude sub-tasks in the view.

If you need to

Use this

See all sub-tasks

subtask

See all parent tasks while excluding their sub-tasks

!subtask

See all tasks scheduled for a specific date.

If you need to

Use this

View all tasks scheduled for January 3rd

date: Jan 3

See all tasks dated before a specific date

date before: May 5 or date before: 5/5

See all tasks dated after a specific date

date after: May 5 or date after: 5/5

See all tasks scheduled within the next four hours and all overdue tasks

date before: +4 hours

See all tasks that are dated before next week. Select the day that represents “Next week” in Settings > General > Next week.

date before: next week

See all tasks dated in the current working week

date before: sat

See all tasks that are dated for next week

(date: next week | date after: next week) & date before: 1 week after next week

See all tasks dated within the current calendar month

date before: first day

See active tasks dated yesterday, along with today’s tasks listed below

date: yesterday, today

See all tasks that have no date associated with them

no date

See all tasks with a date assigned to them

!no date

See all tasks with a date and time assigned to them

!no date & !no time

See all tasks dated today and before a specific time

date: today & date before: today at 2pm

See all tasks that are overdue

Overdue or over due or od

See all tasks that are overdue and have had time assigned to them, along with all tasks dated today and with time assigned to them

overdue & !no time, date: today & !no time

See all tasks in your Inbox without a date, followed by a separate section with all your tasks that have dates set, but are not in your Inbox

#Inbox & no due date, All & !#Inbox & !no due date

You can write a date in any of these ways:

  • Specific date: 10/5/2022, Oct 5th 2022
  • Specific date and time: 10/5/2022 5pm, Oct 5th 5pm
  • Relative date: today, tomorrow, yesterday, 3 days (dated in the next 3 days), -3 days (dated in the past 3 days)
  • Days of the week: Monday, Tuesday, Sunday If you need to

Use this

See all tasks with no deadline

no deadline

See all tasks with a deadline

!no deadline

See all tasks with a deadline today

deadline: today

See all tasks with a deadline within the next 7 days

deadline after: yesterday & deadline before: in 7 days

See all tasks with overdue deadlines

deadline before: today

The due query takes into consideration the date and deadline fields. If a task has both, a date and deadline, due prioritizes the date. If the task does not have a date, due will check if the deadline matches filter criteria. If you don’t use deadlines, due and date filters will return the same results.

If you need to

Use this

View all tasks due on January 3rd

Jan 3

See all tasks that are due before a specific date

due before: May 5 or due before: 5/5

See all tasks that are due after a specific date

due after: May 5 or due after: 5/5

See all tasks due within the next four hours and all overdue tasks

due before: +4 hours

See all tasks that are due before the day you’ve selected in Settings > General > Next week

due before: next week

See all tasks due in the current working week

due before: sat

See all tasks that are due next week

(due: next week | due after: next week) & due before: 1 week after next week

See all tasks due within the current calendar month

due before: first day

See active tasks due yesterday, along with today’s tasks listed below

due: yesterday, today

See all tasks due today and before a specific due time

today & due before: today at 2pm

See all tasks that are overdue

Overdue or over due or od

See all tasks that are overdue and have had a specific time assigned to them, along with all tasks due today and with only assigned time

overdue & !no time, today & !no time

See all tasks in your Inbox without a date or deadline, followed by a separate section with all your tasks that are due, but are not in your Inbox

#Inbox & no date, All & !#Inbox & !no date

See all tasks due within the next 5 days

5 days or next 5 days

See all tasks that have a recurring date

recurring

See all tasks that either have a non-recurring date or deadline, or no date at all assigned to them

!recurring

See all tasks with a date or deadline, but no due time, and which are not recurring

no time & !recurring

If you need to

Use this

See all tasks with priority level 1

p1

See all tasks with priority level 2

p2

See all tasks with priority level 3

p3

See all tasks with no priority level (i.e. p4)

p4 or No priority

In filters, p4 and No priority are equivalent. Both show every task without a priority level. No priority works as a filter query but not in Quick Add, where you’d use p4 to set a task’s priority.

Create filters based on labels. For example, the filter today & @email will pull up all tasks with the @email label that are due today.

If you need to

Use this

See all tasks with the label “email”

@email

See all tasks that don’t have any labels

no labels

If you need to

Use this

See all tasks in the “Work” project

#Work

See all tasks in the “Work” project and its sub-projects

##Work

When you search for tasks assigned to or by one of your collaborators, make sure that you use the name the collaborator uses in Todoist.

For example, Steve’s real name might be Stephen Gray, but if he is listed as “Steve Gray” in Todoist, you should search assigned by: Steve Gray or assigned to: Steve Gray.

A collaborator can be identified by:

  • The person’s email
  • The person’s full name
  • “Me” (referring to yourself)
  • “Others” (referring to all users other than yourself) If you need to

View the tasks in your filters in three different layouts: as a list, a board, or a calendar (calendar layout is only available to Pro and Business customers)!

Unsupported filters

Although Todoist filters can surface lots of valuable information, there are several unsupported filters you won’t be able to use for your tasks or projects:

Unsupported filter

Reason

assigned to: nobody

This is an unsupported filter query. To see all tasks that are assigned to nobody, use !assigned instead.

Show all tasks with comments

Todoist filters can’t access comment data. You can only filter by date, project, label, priority, assignment, and search terms.

Show task comments that contain a specific keyword

Todoist filters can’t access comment content.

Show completed tasks

Todoist filters show open or active tasks by default. Completed tasks aren’t visible in filter views.

Show parent tasks with their sub-tasks

Todoist filters only show either the parent task or the sub-task, not both.

Delete a filter

If you no longer need or use a Todoist filter, here’s how to delete it:

Select Platform:

  • Click Filters & Labels in the sidebar.
  • Right-click the filter or click the three dots icon beside the filter name.
  • Select Delete to remove the filter.
  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Select a filter.
  • Tap the three dots icon.
  • Select Edit Filter.
  • Select Delete Filter. Quick tip

You can also delete a filter through the filter’s context menu.

  • Tap Browse in the navigation bar.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Select a filter.
  • Tap the three dots icon.
  • Select Edit Filter.
  • Select Delete Filter.

Best practices for filters

As you get the hang of using Todoist filters, you’ll discover more ways to quickly surface information. Keep these best practices in mind to avoid bumping into errors:

Combine filters with symbols

You can combine any filter query you want to get the exact view you need. Here are a few examples:

If you need to

Use this

See all tasks that are due today and are also labeled @email

Today & @email

See all tasks that are labelled either @work or @office

@work | @office

See all tasks that are either due today or are overdue and are also in the “Work” project

(today | overdue) & #Work

See all tasks that are due in the next 7 days and are labeled @waiting

7 days & @waiting

See tasks assigned to Denise or Carol due next week, and that contain the Todoist label

(assigned to: Denise | assigned to: Carol) & (due after: sunday & due before: 8 days after sunday) & @Todoist

See all tasks are due today or are overdue, and that contain the @work label

(all | today) & (all | overdue) & @work

See all tasks that are due today but exclude tasks in the “Work” project

Today & !#Work

See all tasks that are due tomorrow in the “Homework” project, but exclude tasks with the @languages label

#Homework & tomorrow & !@languages

Use a wildcard

To filter for tasks with similar symbols or characters, enter an asterisk (*) in your search terms to use a wildcard.

For example, the filter query @urgent* will pull up a list of all tasks that have a label that start with the word “urgent”.

If you need to

Use this

See all tasks with any label that starts with “home”. For example, @homework and @homeoffice

See all tasks assigned to anyone whose first name starts with an M and last name is Smith

assigned to: m* smith

See all tasks from projects which name ends with “work”. For example, #Artwork, #Network, and #Work

#*Work

See all tasks from sections that have the word “Work” in the name. For example, /Work Meetings, /Work Admin, and /Work Calls

/Work

See all tasks that don’t belong to any section

!/*

Quick tip

If you need to search for a project which has an emoji in its title, you can use an asterisk to replace the emoji. For example, instead of adding #Welcome 👋 to your query, you can add #Welcome *.

Run two or more filter queries

You’ve the option to create multiple task lists in the same filter view by running several filter queries simultaneously. To separate each filter query in the view, add a comma in between filter queries.

For example, the filter query p1 & overdue, p4 & today shows two task lists in the same view:

  • A list of priority 1 overdue tasks
  • Priority 4 tasks that are due today

Use Filter Assist

Let Filter Assist generate the right filter for you. Describe which tasks you’d like to see in either English or Spanish, and Filter Assist will do the rest:

Select Platform:

  • Click Filters & Labels in the sidebar.
  • Click the Add icon next to Filters.
  • Click Try it in the Filter Assist banner at the top.
  • Describe which tasks you want to filter in the Filter request field.
  • Click Send.
  • Click Add filter. Quick tip

Go further by customizing your filter. Change the filter’s name, assign a different color, or add the filter to your favorites.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Tap the Add icon next to Filters.
  • Tap the Filter Assist banner at the top.
  • Describe which tasks you want to filter in the FILTER REQUEST field.
  • Tap Send.
  • Tap Add. Quick tip

Go further by customizing your filter. Change the filter’s name, assign a different color, or add the filter to your favorites.

  • Tap Browse in the bottom-right.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Tap the Add icon next to Filters.
  • Tap the Filter Assist banner at the top.
  • Describe which tasks you want to filter in the Filter request field.
  • Tap the Send icon.
  • Tap the checkmark icon to save your filter. Quick tip

Go further by customizing your filter. Change the filter’s name, assign a different color, or add the filter to your favorites.

Introduction to labels

Labels let you save time by batching similar tasks together. In Todoist, you can add as many labels as needed, and then pull up a list of tasks with any of these labels in seconds.

Play

Add a label

Select Platform:

  • Click Filters & Labels in the sidebar. If you don’t see this view, customize your sidebar to display it.
  • Click the plus icon next to Labels.
  • Type a label name and choose a color. If you use this label often, add it as a favorite.
  • Click Add to confirm.
Add a label to a new task
  • Click Add task to create a new task.
  • Click the Labels chip or type @ into the task field. If the Labels chip isn’t visible, customize Quick Add to add it as a task action.
  • Select the label(s) you want to add from the menu. If the label doesn’t exist, finish typing the label name and click Create to create it.
  • Click Add task to confirm.
Add a label to an existing task

  • Click a task to open the task view.

  • Click Labels on the right side of the task view.

  • Select the label or type the label name in the Type a label field. If the label doesn’t exist, enter the full label name and click Create to create it. You’ll find your newly created label in the Labels list.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.

  • Select Filter & Labels. If you don’t see this view, customize the navigation to display it.

  • Tap the plus icon next to Labels.

  • Type a label name and choose a color. If you use this label often, add it as a favorite.

  • Tap Done to confirm.

Add a label to a new task
  • Tap the Dynamic Add button.
  • Tap the Labels chip or type @ in the task name. If the Labels chip isn’t visible, customize Quick Add and add it as a task action.
  • Select the label(s) you want to add. If the label doesn’t exist, type the full label name and tap Add Label.
Add a label to an existing task

  • Tap a task to open the task view.

  • Tap the Labels chip or type @ in the task name.

  • Select the label(s) to add from the menu. If the label doesn’t exist, type the full label name and tap Add Label.

  • Tap Save to confirm. You’ll find your newly created label in the Labels list.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.

  • Select Filters & Labels. If you don’t see this view, customize the navigation to display it.

  • Tap the plus icon next to Labels.

  • Type a label name and choose a color. If you use this label often, add it as a favorite.

  • Tap the checkmark icon to confirm.

Add a label to a new task
  • Tap the Dynamic Add button.
  • Tap the Labels chip or type @ in the task name. If the Labels chip isn’t visible, customize Quick Add and add it as a task action.
  • Select the label(s) you want to add. If the label doesn’t exist, type the full label name and tap Add Label.
Add a label to an existing task
  • Tap a task to open the task view.
  • Tap the Labels chip.
  • Select the label(s) to add to the task or type @ in the task name. If the label doesn’t exist, finish typing the label name and tap Add label.
  • Tap the checkmark icon to confirm. You’ll find your newly created label in the Labels list.

Quick tip

You can add special characters, like @ , ” ( ) | & or !, when naming your labels.

A label’s color shows next to the label name, and on your tasks in the calendar layout when you color tasks by label.

Edit a label

As your workflow changes, so can your labels. Here’s how to change the label name or color:

Select Platform:

  • Click Filters & Labels in the sidebar.
  • In the Labels section, click the label.
  • Click the three dots icon to the right of the label.
  • Select Edit label.
  • Enter a new label name or click the Label color menu to choose a different color.
  • Click Save to confirm.
  • Tap the Filters & Labels view.
  • In the Labels section, tap the label.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Edit Label.
  • Enter a new label name or tap the Color menu to choose a different color.
  • Tap Done in the top-right to confirm. Quick tip

Change the color of a label through the label’s context menu.

  • Tap the menu icon at the bottom-left.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Tap Manage labels and select the label.
  • Select the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Edit.
  • Enter a new label name or choose a different color.

Turn a shared label into a personal label

In Todoist, there are two types of labels you can create and add to tasks:

  • Personal labels are those you’ve created. These labels come in a variety of colors, and they’ll stay on your list unless you remove them from your label list.
  • Shared labels are those added by collaborators in shared projects, and are added to your shared list if there’s no exact match in your personal label list. Shared labels are displayed only in gray, and they’ll only stay in the shared labels list if there are any active tasks with this label. Dermot · Customer Experience Specialist

Every member of the shared project can rename or delete a shared label. Their changes will apply to all the active tasks tagged with that label.

If you find yourself using a label often in your shared projects, here’s how to turn it into a personal label:

Select Platform:

  • Click Filters & Labels in the sidebar.
  • Under Shared Labels, find the label you want to add.
  • Click the three dots icon next to the label.
  • Select Move to personal labels.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Select Filters & Labels.
  • Find the label in the Shared section.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Edit Label.
  • Tap Move to Personal Labels.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Select Filters & Labels.
  • Select Manage labels at the bottom of the labels list.
  • Tap Shared.
  • Find the label.
  • Tap the three dots icon.
  • Tap Move to personal labels.

Delete a label

You may come across a label that no longer serves its purpose. No problem, you can simply delete it, so your labels list is neat and tidy:

Select Platform:

  • Click Filters & Labels in the sidebar.
  • Find the label you want to delete.
  • Click the three dots icon next to the label.
  • Select Delete label. Click Delete again to confirm.
  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.
  • Tap Filters & Labels.
  • Find the label you want to delete.
  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.
  • Select Edit Label.
  • Select Delete Label.
  • Tap Delete Label to confirm. Quick tip

Touch and hold a label to delete it using the context menu.

  • Tap Browse at the bottom-right.

  • Tap Filters & Labels.

  • Tap the label you want to delete.

  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.

  • Select Delete. Tap Delete again to confirm. If you need to delete more than one label, here’s how to bulk delete them:

  • Tap Filters & Labels.

  • Scroll to the bottom of your label list and tap Manage labels.

  • Select the labels you want to delete.

  • Tap the three dots icon at the top-right.

  • Select Delete. Tap Delete again to confirm. Note

If you deleted a personal or shared label, they’ll still appear on completed tasks. Whenever you uncomplete a task with a deleted label, a new label is created and added back to your labels lists. This label will have the name it had when the task was completed.

Use the board layout in Todoist

Boards are a powerful way to organize and visualize Todoist projects.

From weekly meal plans to five-year business strategies, boards provide a bird’s-eye view of your progress and help you get work done.

With the board layout, you can:

  • Add and rearrange sections.
  • Use sections to represent phases of the project.
  • Drag tasks to relevant sections.
  • View completed tasks. In the project, tasks are displayed as cards. Each section is displayed as a column. Tasks that don’t belong to any section appear in the default “No Section” column.

When the board layout is turned on, it syncs across devices:

Todoist for iOS

Todoist for Android

Select the board layout

Select Platform:

When creating a new project, select Board in the View menu.

To turn on the board layout for an existing project or view:

  • Open Today, Upcoming, or any project, label, or filter from the sidebar.
  • Click the view icon in the top-right.
  • Select Board. Quick tip

Use the Shift + V shortcut to switch to the list layout or calendar layout (only available to Pro and Business users).

When creating or editing a project, select Board in the View menu to turn on the board layout.

If you’re turning on the board layout for an existing project or view:

  • Open Today, or any project, label, or filter.
  • Tap the three dots icon in the top-right.
  • Tap View.
  • Select Board.
  • Tap Done. Warning

Boards are currently not available in the Upcoming view on iOS.

When creating or editing a project, turn on the board layout right away by selecting Board under the View option.

If you’re turning on the board layout for an existing project or view:

  • Open Today, or any project, label, or filter.
  • Tap the three dots icon in the top-right.
  • Tap View.
  • Select Board.
  • Tap Save. Warning

Boards are currently not available in the Upcoming view on Android.

Switch from the board layout

Select Platform:

  • Open Today, Upcoming, or any project, label, or filter from the sidebar.
  • Click the view icon in the top-right.
  • Select List or Calendar (Pro or Business users only).
  • Open Today, or any project, label, or filter.
  • Tap the three dots icon in the top-right.
  • Tap View.
  • Select List or Calendar (Pro or Business users only).
  • Tap Done.
  • Open Today, or any project, label, or filter.
  • Tap the three dots icon in the top-right.
  • Tap View.
  • Select List or Calendar (Pro or Business users only).
  • Tap Save.

Create a new section in the board layout

Select Platform:

  • Scroll through your existing sections to the far right and click the Add Section button, or simply press the s key to add a new section to the end. Alternatively, hover between existing sections and click the Add Section button to add a new section in that spot.
  • Type your section name.
  • Click Add Section or press Enter to save.
  • Swipe through your existing sections to the far right.
  • Tap the Add Section button at the top. Alternatively, tap the three dots icon in the top right-hand corner and select Add Section.
  • Type your section name.
  • Tap the submit button to save.
  • Swipe through your existing sections to the far right.
  • Tap the Add Section button at the top. Alternatively, tap the three dots icon in the top right-hand corner and select Add section.
  • Type your section name.
  • Tap the submit button to save.

Reorder sections in the board layout

Select Platform:

  • Hover over a section name.
  • Drag and drop your section to a new position in a project.
  • Long press a section name to activate the Reorder Section menu. Alternatively, tap the three dots icon next to a section name and select Reorder Section.
  • Drag and drop sections in the order you need.
  • Tap the Save button in the top right-hand corner to apply the change.
  • Long press a section name to activate the Reorder Section menu. Alternatively, tap the three dots icon next to a section name and select Reorder Section.
  • Drag and drop sections in the order you need. It will be applied right away.

Create tasks in the board layout

Select Platform:

  • Click the + Add task button in a section where you would like your task to be, or use Quick Add by clicking the + icon in the top-right corner. Alternatively, you can press the a key to add a new task to the first available column.
  • Type your task name and apply any parameters (e.g. a due date, priority, label etc.). You can also use the / shortcut to add a task to a specific section from anywhere.
  • Click the Add Task button to save your new task.
  • Tap the + Add task button in a section where you would like your task to be. Alternatively, drag the + Add task button to any position between your existing tasks to insert a new task there.
  • Type your task name and apply any parameters (e.g. a due date, priority, label etc.). You can also use the / shortcut to add a task to a specific section from anywhere.
  • Tap the submit button to save your new task.
  • Tap the + Add Task button in a section where you would like your task to be. Alternatively, drag the + Add Task button to any position between your existing tasks to insert a new task there.
  • Type your task name and apply any parameters (e.g. a due date, priority, label etc.). You can also use the / shortcut to add a task to a specific section from anywhere.
  • Tap the submit button to save your new task.

Reorder tasks in the board layout

Rearrange tasks by dragging them within the section, or from one section to another.

If a task has sub-tasks, they aren’t visible in the board layout and can’t be reordered in the same way. Instead, open the task in the task view and reorder the sub-tasks.

Use the calendar layout in Todoist

The Todoist calendar layout helps you and your team visualize upcoming work and align on important dates. By displaying tasks in a weekly or monthly grid, you can identify schedule gaps and stay organized. Use this guide to learn how to enable, navigate, and customize your calendar layout.

Play

Apply the calendar layout in a project

Select Platform:

Apply the layout during project creation

When creating a new project, select Calendar in the Layout section.

Change the layout of a view or existing project
  • Open the view or project from the sidebar.
  • Click Display at the top-right.
  • Select Calendar.
  • Choose between the Week or Month layout. If you no longer need the calendar layout, switch to either the board or list layouts.
Apply the layout during project creation

When creating a new project, select Calendar in the Layout section.

Change the layout of a view or existing project
  • Tap the project in the navigation menu.
  • Tap the three dots icon and select Display .
  • Select Calendar.
  • Tap Layout and choose between Agenda and Week (‘Week’ displays three days in portrait; seven days in landscape). If you no longer need the calendar layout, switch to either the board or list layouts in the Display menu. Then, tap Done.
Apply the layout during project creation

When creating a new project, select Calendar in the Layout section.

Change the layout of a view or existing project
  • Tap the project in the navigation menu.
  • Tap the three dots icon and select Display .
  • Select Calendar.
  • Tap Layout and choose between Agenda and 3-day / Week (depending on device orientation).
  • Tap Save to confirm. If you no longer need the calendar layout, switch to either the board or list layouts in the Display menu.

Olivia · Customer Experience Specialist

Take time management to the next level with the Upcoming view! Apply the calendar layout to this view and create a time-blocked plan for your week.

  • Enter the task name and add any task details.

  • Tap the submit button.
  • Drag the Dynamic Add button to the day to schedule a task.

Who says the week always starts on a Monday? Choose when your week starts in the General tab of your Todoist settings. This will automatically reflect in the calendar layout.

Schedule a task in the calendar layout

Select Platform:

Schedule a task without a date

View future occurrences

By default, recurring tasks will only show the next upcoming occurrence. However, if you are a Todoist Pro or Business customer, and you’ve applied the calendar layout to the Upcoming view on your desktop or web app, you’ll be able to see all future occurrences of your recurring tasks.

Select Platform:

To turn future occurrences on or off, click Display at the top-right and toggle Future occurrences.

Future occurrences are not supported on mobile apps yet.

Note

If the list or board layout is applied to the project, you’ll only see the next recurrence of the task.

Color tasks in the calendar layout

Tasks in the calendar layout are colored by priority by default. You can color them by label or project instead to see at a glance what kind of work a day holds. The setting applies to Inbox, Today, Upcoming, and Filters & Labels. It syncs across the platforms you use Todoist on.

Add deadlines to tasks 🎯: Jan 7

For many people, the Date you set for a task is the date you plan to do it. A Deadline, on the other hand, is the date a task needs to be completed by.

A big assignment at school. A report for your boss. Taxes (😱). Deadlines in Todoist let you track a task’s actual deadline separately, so you can schedule out time to start working on it.

Here’s Jon with an intro to this long-requested feature!

Play

How it works

  • Deadlines are available on paid plans whether you’re using Todoist solo or with your Team.
  • To add a deadline to a new task, click Deadline and select a date. For existing tasks, open the task view and set or edit its deadline. That’s it! That’s the feature. 🌈
  • The deadline of a task will be visible wherever you see that task in Todoist: Upcoming, Labels, Today, etc. As a deadline approaches (within 7 days), a countdown will show to give you a subtle reminder that it’s getting closer.
  • In the Calendar view, deadlines are highlighted in the All day section so you can’t miss them. Clicking them will take you to the task’s details so you can make sure you’ve planned to tackle it in time. 💪
  • When the deadline for an uncompleted task arrives, it will be shown in your Today and Upcoming views so it doesn’t slip through the cracks. Quick tip

If you prefer to add a deadline to a task while you type, use the {} shortcut. For example, {tomorrow} sets a task’s deadline as tomorrow. Learn more about adding task details by typing

When to use deadlines

Like setting the priority of a task, a deadline adds context that helps you plan your time. But they’re not always needed. In fact, the less you use them, the more powerful they become. (Insert mind-blown gif here 🤯)

Here are a few times when adding a deadline to a task is a good fit:

  • You’ve agreed with your boss to finish a report by the end of the month (but you’ll start working on it on Monday).
  • A task you’re handing-off to a teammate needs to be done by next Friday to keep the project on track.
  • You have a major assignment due in three weeks, but will definitely need multiple sessions to crack it. 🧠 Quick tip

For now, deadlines work with one-time tasks only. But, based on your feedback, we’re thoughtfully exploring how to also bring them to recurring tasks in a future update.

“When do you need this by?”

No more! 🥳 Adding a deadline to a task before you hand it over to a teammate effortlessly tells them when it needs to be done.

Once your teammate takes over, they can schedule time to work on the task using the Date field. The deadline will stay put, no matter how many times their plans change.

It starts with a task

Want some inspiration on how other Todoist users have met their own deadlines? Take a look at all of the weird and wonderful things they’ve achieved in the last year! Along with the first task that springboarded them to success. 🚀

Play

  • Instructions

Capture tasks at the speed of thought - Ramble (Beta): Nov 19

Ever wish Todoist could just listen while you think out loud? Now it can.

Ramble lets you add tasks by speaking. It turns your words into structured tasks, complete with any details you mention, like projects, dates, deadlines, and priorities.

It feels like magic.

How it works

Your thoughts move faster than your fingers. With Ramble, you can add tasks four times faster than typing them. Here’s how:

  • Click the waveform icon in Quick Add or the sidebar.
  • Speak normally, describing what you need to do and when you need to do it.
  • Edit, remove, or adjust the tasks as you speak. Say phrases like “Actually, I meant…” to edit a task, or “Remove that” to delete a suggested task. Ramble will update them as you go.
  • Done rambling? End the session by saying “that’s all” or clicking Add tasks. That’s it! The tasks are off your mind, in Todoist, and organized so you now know exactly what you need to do and when. 🧘‍♂️

Here’s Heather with a quick walkthrough:

Play

Quick tip

Ramble is in beta, which means you get early access while we continue to improve it based on your feedback. We’ll introduce a monthly limit for Free plans soon, but until then, use it, break it, tell us what you love (and what you don’t).

What Ramble captures

Ramble understands natural speech in 38 languages and allows you to set a project, date, time, recurrence, duration, deadline, priority, labels, and description while you speak.

For more details on what’s possible with Ramble visit our Help Center.

Note

Under the hood, Ramble is powered by Todoist Assist, which means that privacy is at the core. Ramble only keeps what matters – your tasks. The audio is processed securely, never stored, and never used for training. What stays are your organized tasks, not your words. That unhinged jumble of thoughts, expectations, hopes, and dreams is nobody’s business but yours.

When to use Ramble

Like any feature, Ramble isn’t for everything. But when it fits, it fits perfectly. Here are a few times when speaking beats typing:

  • Between contexts, when everything hits at once. You’re wrapping up a work call and suddenly remember you need to email the team, pick up prescriptions, and schedule that budget meeting. Get it all out in one breath. 💆
  • During your commute, when ideas flow. The train ride home is when you finally see how next week should unfold. Capture the entire plan before your stop.
  • At your desk when life interrupts. Your partner texts with a list of errands while you’re mid-flow. Ramble them off, then dive back into focus mode without missing a beat.
  • After meetings with scattered follow-ups. Your standup just ended, and you have a laundry list of client requests, updates for the team, and follow-ups to remember. Ramble captures it all before you’re back at your desk.

Give it a try

Ready for a quick brain dump? Pull up Ramble and just… talk. Get it out of your head. Ramble will handle the rest.

  • Instructions

A clearer picture of your team’s work: Apr 23

Better teamwork rarely starts with a big process change. Sometimes it starts with opening a tab and finally seeing what’s actually going on.

Turns out you don’t need a complicated system. Just a clearer picture.

These updates give your team a real-time read on who’s working on what, how projects are tracking, and what’s been happening within the team.

People tab (Beta)

Until now, the only way to know how your team’s work was distributed was to ask around, check individual projects, or trust the mental picture you’ve been carrying around – which, as it turns out, is often wrong.

The People tab brings everything into one place. Who’s assigned what, who’s carrying a heavy load, and who might have more capacity. Admins also see overdue tasks across the team, so nothing gets missed.

Find it next to the Projects tab in your team workspace overview.

Note

The People tab is currently in beta, which means that we’re actively looking to improve it with your feedback.

Insights

Your 1:1s were never supposed to be 40 minutes of “where are we on this one? And this one? And this one?”

Insights gives you a real-time health check for every project: how far along it is, where things are at risk, how the work is spread across the team. No setup, nothing to configure – it works from how your team already works.

Spot that one project that’s quietly falling behind, or the person who’s carrying significantly more than everyone else. So when you do sit down together, you already know. No status round. No surprises. Just the conversation you actually needed to have.

Insights is available on Todoist Business, across all platforms. Open any team project for a quick read on its health, or pull up the workspace overview to see how everything’s tracking at once.

Reporting (formerly Activity Log)

Reporting (formerly Activity Log) answers the question you didn’t want to have to ask: what’s actually been happening?

It lives in your sidebar, and it’s been reimagined for the web app. A cleaner layout, new filtering options, and presets that get you straight to what you’re looking for. Your completed tasks, activity across your favorite projects, everything the team shipped last week – it’s all there, ready to dig into.

Coming back from a long weekend? You’ll know exactly what happened while you were gone, all before your first coffee.

It exports to Markdown too – useful for weekly updates, meeting recaps, or putting it to work somewhere else.

Note

On free plans, Reporting history goes back seven days. If you find yourself wanting to reach further back, the Business plan gives your team full history.

Everything in one place

We put together a guide to walk you through all of it – four short videos, one per feature. Kaitlin, Marco, Dermot, and Denise each took one. Start wherever makes sense for your team.

Just talk to your wrist – Ramble on Wear OS (Beta): Mar 23

Some thoughts arrive at the worst possible moment – both hands occupied, phone out of reach, no way to type. Now there’s a better option.

Ramble is Todoist’s voice-to-tasks feature: speak naturally, and it pulls tasks, dates, and priorities straight out of what you say. And now it’s on your wrist! Ramble is available on Android smartwatches in beta, so you can capture tasks the moment they surface, without reaching for your phone.

How it works

  • Open the Todoist for Wear OS app on your smartwatch.
  • Tap the Ramble button.
  • Speak your tasks naturally. Ramble captures them in a preview on your watch screen as you talk.
  • When you’re done, tap Done or say “That’s all” to send everything to your Todoist Inbox. Your tasks are captured and waiting, and you’ll land straight in your Inbox to review them.

When to use Ramble

The magic of Ramble on your watch is that it meets you where your phone can’t, or where pulling it out would break the moment entirely:

  • You’re on a morning walk, and your mind drifts to everything you need to tackle before Friday. Talk it out, and clear your head again.
  • You step out of a back-to-back meeting with five follow-ups bouncing around your head. Get them out before the next one starts.
  • You’re cooking dinner, mid-chopping, and three things you need to do tomorrow suddenly all show up at once. Wrist up. Done.
  • Your gym set just ended, and your brain is firing on all cylinders. Capture it before the endorphins take it with them.
  • You’re drifting off to sleep, and your mind starts swirling with open loops. You don’t want to stare at your phone screen at this hour, so you just Ramble into your watch and zzzzzz…

A note on what’s different on watches

Ramble on smartwatches is built for quick capture on a small screen, so it works a little differently than Ramble on your phone or computer:

  • You can set a task’s name, date, and priority while speaking. Other attributes (like projects, labels, deadlines, and descriptions) are currently not supported.
  • All tasks are saved to your Inbox. You can move and refine them on your phone or other devices after capture. Note

What about Apple Watch?

We’re actively working with Apple to enable the required technology on Apple Watches. Stay tuned.

Try it out

Ramble is free to use on Android smartwatches during the beta period, on all plans. Available from Wear OS v12031.

Take it for a spin – and if something feels off or you have ideas for making it better, let us know. This is new territory for Ramble, and your input helps us get the wrist experience just right.

For a full look at everything Ramble can do across platforms, visit our help center.

Outlook Calendar integration is here! 📅: Jun 5

You asked (repeatedly! 😉), and now we can finally say: Todoist now integrates seamlessly with Outlook Calendar!

Your tasks and events, finally together

Whether you’re an Outlook devotee or just required to use it at the office, this integration gives you the complete picture: what you need to do alongside when you actually have time to do it. No more accidentally scheduling three hours of deep work when you’ve got back-to-back meetings all afternoon.

Hugo and the calendar team worked relentlessly to make this happen, and it’s available today for all Todoist plans. Here’s Hugo with a quick walkthrough of how it works:

Play

How to set it up:

  • Head to Settings > Calendars.

Time-blocking made simple

Scan notes, photos, and files for tasks – Task Capture (Beta): Apr 21

There’s always something waiting to be transferred into Todoist. The sticky note covered in action items from this morning’s meeting. The email chain where the actual ask is buried somewhere in the middle. The whiteboard photo that’s been sitting in your camera roll since Thursday.

Task Capture lets you drop it all in – and get an actual task list back. No retyping. No copy-paste-copy-paste.

How it works

Open Quick Add. Paste in meeting notes, drag in a PDF, share a photo from your camera roll. Todoist scans for tasks and shows you what it found – task names, dates, priorities, assignees, durations. You’ll see a preview before anything lands on your list.

You can work with:

  • Text – meeting transcripts, email threads, chat snippets, bullet points
  • Images – photos of whiteboards, handwritten notes, printed documents (JPEG, PNG, WebP up to 7MB)
  • Files – PDFs, Word docs, Markdown files, plain text Full instructions in the help center →

Samuel · Product Manager

“I’ve been using Task Capture daily while renovating our house. Standing in a half-finished kitchen on the phone with a contractor, scribbling notes on whatever’s nearby – paint samples, the back of permit papers, once on a piece of drywall. Now I just snap a photo with my phone and let Todoist pull out the to-dos. One less thing to worry about.”

Task Capture works with whatever you’ve got:

  • You’ve wrapped a client call and the transcript is a wall of text with action items buried somewhere in paragraphs three, seven, and twelve. Paste it in and let Todoist find them.
  • You went old school and scrawled notes on whatever paper was nearby. Snap a photo instead of retyping it all later.
  • Someone sends you a brief that’s twenty-seven pages long. Drop it in and start from a structured list instead of reading through it twice with a highlighter.

Available now in beta

The beta is open on web, desktop, and mobile for everyone, across all plans. After the beta, usage on free plans will be limited.

Task Capture is still being actively refined by Hiroki, Natalie, Panos, Pedro S., Ricardo, Samuel, and Sergio. If something doesn’t behave the way you’d expect, use the 👍/👎 in-app – your feedback goes directly to the people building it.

See team progress with Project Insights 📊: Oct 27

We have a confession: even here at Todoist, we love using Todoist for our individual work, but when it comes to tracking how our team projects are actually doing, we found ourselves in the same place you probably are: juggling spreadsheets, status docs, and gut feelings.

That’s why we’re building Project Insights.

Project Insights: now in beta for Business teams

Your team keeps working exactly as they do now in Todoist. Meanwhile, Project Insights interprets every completion, every assignment, every deadline to surface the project intelligence you’ve been missing.

No setup required. No new processes. No additional work for anyone.

Here’s Heather with a quick walkthrough:

Play

Note

Project Insights is currently in beta and available on the Business plan. Learn more about Business features and pricing.

What you’ll see (and why it matters)

Health – Automatic summaries that give you real context, not just red/yellow/green indicators. See things like “The project is moving, but inconsistently. 2 tasks are behind schedule, 1 has unclear ownership.”

Progress – Shows completion percentage, completed task count, and active (open) tasks. A simple snapshot of where your project stands right now.

Completed – Compare this period’s task completions to the previous one (week-over-week or month-over-month). Quickly see if momentum is building or stalling, and spot patterns in your team’s work rhythm. Simple trend arrows show whether you’re accelerating, maintaining pace, or slowing down.

Assigned – View task distribution among team members, sorted from heaviest to lightest load. Spot imbalances before they become problems, and catch unassigned tasks that may have fallen through the cracks.

Workspace Overview – Health and progress indicators across all projects in the overview help you scan your team’s entire progress at a glance. While currently limited to projects you’ve joined, the full workspace-wide visibility is coming soon, allowing you to quickly identify which projects need attention and which are running smoothly.

Project oversight without the overhead

Traditional project management tools often require elaborate workflows, complex dashboards, and heavyweight processes. We’re building something different: intelligence that emerges from your team’s natural work patterns, not from added layers or extra effort.

Like a fitness tracker that surfaces health insights from your natural activity, Project Insights automatically interprets your team’s work to tell you what matters – without you having to do anything extra.

This is just the beginning, and we’d love your help shaping what effortless project oversight looks like. Give it a try and let us know what you think. Where we go depends on what you need most.
